entries.title: A ring does not change the blow
entries.literal_meaning: A slap from a gold-ringed hand brings the benefit of bathing in the Ganga.
entries.explanation: The saying gives a blow from an adorned hand the value of a sacred bath. Our critical reading questions that elevation: an ornament does not make harm deserved or beneficial. This is our response to the line, not a supplied traditional counter-moral or a claim of ritual efficacy.
entries.meaning_odia: ସୁନାମୁଦି ପିନ୍ଧା ହାତର ଚାପୁଡ଼ାକୁ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଗଙ୍ଗାସ୍ନାନର ଫଳ ସହିତ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାମୂଳକ ପାଠ ସେହି ମୂଲ୍ୟଦାନକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ—ଅଳଙ୍କାର ଥିବାରୁ ଆଘାତ ଯୋଗ୍ୟ ବା ଉପକାରୀ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ। ଏହା ଆମ ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା; ଉତ୍ସରେ ଦିଆଯାଇଥିବା ପାରମ୍ପରିକ ବିପରୀତ ଉପଦେଶ ବା ଧାର୍ମିକ ଫଳର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical response separates an adorned hand from any justification for its blow.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା ଅଳଙ୍କାରକୁ ଆଘାତର ଯଥାର୍ଥତାଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ହାତରେ ଦାମୀ ଜିନିଷ ଥିଲେ ଆଘାତ ବଦଳିଯାଏ କି?” ଅନ୍ୟମାନେ ଅଳଙ୍କାର ଓ ବ୍ୟବହାରକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଆଲୋଚନା କଲେ। / Readers distinguish adornment from conduct. This discussion is invented; no assault is depicted or reported.
entries.cultural_context: The first duplicated headword block supplies this wording. A second repeats altered spellings; neither is silently repaired. The earlier Krishna Singh Mahabharata illustration is separate, not this saying’s authorship.

entries.title: Concealing it from the skilled observer
entries.literal_meaning: Like hiding one’s belly from the midwife.
entries.explanation: The example follows the definition of a skilled midwife. Our reading takes the contrast as attempted concealment from someone familiar with the matter. It is an analogy about expertise, not proof that any practitioner knows everything or a demand to disclose intimate information.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦକ୍ଷ ପ୍ରସବସହାୟିକାର ସଂଜ୍ଞା ପରେ ଏହି ତୁଳନା ଆସିଛି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ, ଯିଏ ବିଷୟଟି ଜାଣନ୍ତି ତାଙ୍କଠାରୁ ସେହି କଥା ଲୁଚାଇବାର ଚେଷ୍ଟା ଏଠି ଦିଶେ। ଏହା ଦକ୍ଷତାକୁ ନେଇ ଉପମା; କେହି ସବୁ ଜାଣନ୍ତି ବା ନିଜର ଗୋପନ କଥା କହିବାକୁ ବାଧ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading concerns attempted concealment from someone with relevant experience.

entries.title: A household’s changing circumstances
entries.literal_meaning: At times, a home with two wives; at times, blow and blow at the hearth until you die.
entries.explanation: The repeated “at times” turns a household image into an exhausting cooking complaint. The source gives no cause for the change. Our critical reading notices that the contrast relies on an expectation of women’s kitchen labour; describing that expectation does not make cooking their obligation.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାରମ୍ବାର ଆସୁଥିବା “କେତେବେଳେ” ଘରର ଚିତ୍ରକୁ ରାନ୍ଧି ରାନ୍ଧି ହାଲିଆ ହେବାର ଅଭିଯୋଗ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଏହି ବଦଳର କାରଣ ଉତ୍ସ କହେନାହିଁ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାମୂଳକ ପାଠରେ ଏଠି ନାରୀଙ୍କ ରୋଷେଇ ଶ୍ରମ ଉପରେ ଆଶା ରଖାଯାଇଛି; ସେହି ଆଶାକୁ ବୁଝିବା ଅର୍ଥ ରୋଷେଇ କେବଳ ତାଙ୍କ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ବୋଲି ମାନିବା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading distinguishes a household complaint from an obligation imposed on women.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଘରର ଅଭିଯୋଗକୁ ନାରୀଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଥୋପାଯାଇଥିବା ଦାୟିତ୍ୱଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ।

This response is invented, not the saying’s traditional moral.
entries.cultural_context: The quotation follows the figurative cooking sense. Its death wording is rhetorical here, not an established death event; no marriage history or reason for absence is supplied.

entries.title: Grain ripens, an elder dances
entries.literal_meaning: Gulji suan ripened; the Kharia elder danced.
entries.explanation: The line joins ripening grain to one elder’s dance. The dictionary’s note describes gathering and cooking this grain. Our reading attends to the connection between available food and delight, without making the named figure stand for everyone in a community or turning the dance into a documented ritual.
entries.meaning_odia: ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଶସ୍ୟ ପାଚିବା ସହ ଜଣେ ବୃଦ୍ଧଙ୍କ ନାଚକୁ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଅଭିଧାନର ଟୀକାରେ ଏହି ଶସ୍ୟ ସଂଗ୍ରହ କରି ରାନ୍ଧିବା କଥା ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ମିଳିବା ଓ ଆନନ୍ଦର ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଦେଖେ; ଜଣେ ପାତ୍ରକୁ ପୂରା ସମୁଦାୟର ସ୍ୱଭାବ ବା ନାଚକୁ ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ପର୍ବ ବୋଲି ଧରେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading follows the verse’s food-and-delight connection without generalising a community.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଓ ଆନନ୍ଦର ଯୋଗକୁ ଦେଖେ, ସମୁଦାୟ ବିଷୟରେ ସାଧାରଣ ନିୟମ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ଏହି ଲୋକଟିର ଆନନ୍ଦକୁ ଦେଖିବା, ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ସ୍ୱଭାବ ବୋଲି କହିବା ନାହିଁ।” / A reader asks the group to attend to the individual’s delight rather than make a community stereotype. This discussion is invented.

entries.title: A fitting pair
entries.literal_meaning: Blessed is that Prajapati: bride and groom suit each other.
entries.explanation: The headword here means suiting one another. The line praises a pairing through an invocation of Prajapati, whose precise referent is not explained here. Our reading attends to mutual fit rather than judging either person alone. Whether a particular use is sincere or ironic would depend on its setting.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏଠି ଘଟାଘଟିର ଅର୍ଥ ପରସ୍ପରକୁ ମାନିବା ବା ଉପଯୋଗୀ ହେବା। ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ପ୍ରଜାପତିଙ୍କୁ ଧନ୍ୟ କହି ଯୋଡ଼ିର ମେଳକୁ ପ୍ରଶଂସା କରେ; ପ୍ରଜାପତି କାହାକୁ ବୁଝାଏ ଏଠି ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପାଠ ଜଣକୁ ଅଲଗା ବିଚାରିବା ବଦଳେ ପରସ୍ପରର ମେଳକୁ ଦେଖେ। କଥାଟି ସରଳ ପ୍ରଶଂସା କି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ, ତାହା ପ୍ରୟୋଗର ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଉପରେ ନିର୍ଭର କରିବ।

entries.title: Will this fill the belly?
entries.literal_meaning: Cane berries full of bones—will eating them fill the belly?
entries.explanation: The question sets the berry’s apparent bulk against what it offers to eat. The dictionary describes a layer around the seed, which helps us read the bone image. Our editorial application asks whether something supplies enough usable substance for its purpose; it is not a nutritional verdict about the fruit.
entries.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ଫଳର ଆକାର ସହ ତାହାର ଖାଇବା ଅଂଶକୁ ତୁଳନା କରେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ମଞ୍ଜି ଉପରେ ଏକ ସ୍ତର ଥିବା କଥା ଅଛି; ସେଥିରୁ ହାଡ଼ର ଚିତ୍ରଟି ବୁଝିହୁଏ। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ପଚାରେ, କୌଣସି ଜିନିଷରେ କାମ ପାଇଁ ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ସାର ଅଛି କି। ଏହା ଫଳର ପୋଷଣ ବିଷୟରେ ରାୟ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: An insult and a plea
entries.literal_meaning: You call me a loose woman; do not go to live elsewhere.
entries.explanation: The reply places a plea not to leave beside a degrading name. Its position follows the dictionary’s pejorative sense, not its separate slender-body senses. Our critical reading keeps the speaker’s request distinct from accepting the insult. The source does not identify the relationship or explain why the speaker asks the other person not to leave.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅପମାନଜନକ ନାମର ପାଖରେ ଚାଲି ନ ଯିବାର ଅନୁରୋଧ ଆସିଛି। ଉତ୍ସରେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ନାରୀଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ବ୍ୟବହୃତ ଅପମାନସୂଚକ ଅର୍ଥ ପରେ ଅଛି, ପତଳା ଦେହର ଅଲଗା ଅର୍ଥ ପରେ ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାମୂଳକ ପାଠ ଅନୁରୋଧକୁ ଅପମାନ ମାନିନେବାଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ। ସମ୍ପର୍କ କଣ ବା କାହିଁକି ଯିବାକୁ ମନା କରାଯାଉଛି, ଉତ୍ସ କହେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical response separates the request to stay from the insulting label.

entries.cultural_context: Sense3 supplies a historically judgmental label. It is retained as attributed language, not an established trait, relationship history or traditional counter-moral.

entries.title: True, yet hard to believe
entries.literal_meaning: This is true, yet it is not believed.
entries.explanation: The line calls a statement true while registering a failure of belief. The headword’s second sense supplies that reading of the shortened ending. Our interpretation attends to the gap between asserting truth and finding something convincing; the line itself does not establish whether an unnamed statement is actually true.
entries.meaning_odia: କଥାଟିକୁ ସତ ବୋଲି କହି ମଧ୍ୟ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ ହେଉନଥିବା ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଧରେ। ଶେଷର ସଂକ୍ଷିପ୍ତ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ବୁଝିବାରେ ଶବ୍ଦର ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଅର୍ଥ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରେ। ଆମ ପାଠ ସତ ବୋଲି କହିବା ଓ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ ହେବା ମଧ୍ୟର ଫରକକୁ ଦେଖେ। ଅଜଣା କଥାଟି ପ୍ରକୃତରେ ସତ କି ନୁହେଁ, ଏଥିରୁ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading distinguishes a claim of truth from the experience of believing it.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ସତ୍ୟର ଦାବିକୁ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ ହେବାର ଅନୁଭବଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଜଣେ ପାଠକ ଅପ୍ରତ୍ୟାଶିତ ହିସାବ ଦେଖି ପୁଣି ଗଣିଲେ। ସଂଖ୍ୟା କିପରି ଆସିଲା ବୁଝିବା ପରେ ସେ କଥାଟି ମାନିଲେ। / A reader checks an unexpected calculation and understands how its result was reached. This is an invented application, not evidence for the saying’s origin.
entries.cultural_context: The quotation remains unfilled: it omits the headword’s ମନକୁ. Belief sense2, not approval sense1, supplies the literal rendering; no speaker identity or particular disputed fact is established.

entries.title: The nearby voice
entries.literal_meaning: The one who sleeps nearby speaks into the ear—can their words be distrusted?
entries.explanation: The question gives a nearby voice an apparent advantage. The dictionary places it under backbiting, making access to the listener part of the image. Our reading separates that closeness from reliability: being heard privately does not establish that a report is true. No spouse, gender or actual accusation is identified.
entries.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ପାଖରେ ଥିବା ସ୍ୱରକୁ ଏକ ସୁବିଧା ଦେଉଥିବା ପରି ଲାଗେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ଚୁଗୁଲି କହିବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ନିକଟତାକୁ ବିଶ୍ୱସନୀୟତାଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ—ଏକାନ୍ତରେ ଶୁଣିଲେ ବୋଲି କଥାଟି ସତ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ। ବକ୍ତା ପତି ବା ପତ୍ନୀ, କେଉଁ ଲିଙ୍ଗର ବା କେଉଁ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରୁଛନ୍ତି, ଉତ୍ସ ତାହା କହେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading asks whether private access is being mistaken for trustworthy evidence.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ପଚାରେ, ଏକାନ୍ତରେ କହିବାର ସୁଯୋଗକୁ ପ୍ରମାଣ ଭାବି ନିଆଯାଉଛି କି।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ସଭା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଜଣେ ସଦସ୍ୟ ଆଉଜଣଙ୍କ ବିଷୟରେ ଧୀର ସ୍ୱରରେ କିଛି କହିଲେ। ଶ୍ରୋତା ସମ୍ପୃକ୍ତ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ କଥା ମଧ୍ୟ ଶୁଣିବାକୁ କହିଲେ। / Before a meeting, a listener declines to judge another member from a private report alone. This scene is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The earlier Krishna Singh Mahabharata Adi quotation illustrates whispering sense1. It is separate from this Dhaga under sense2 and does not establish its author.

entries.title: The fish advertises its worth
entries.literal_meaning: The bhakuda fish said: I am king among fish; make broth from my head and see how enjoyable it is.
entries.explanation: The talking fish supports its royal claim with an offer of its own head for cooking. Our reading follows that odd self-advertisement: praise of its worth comes through what someone else might enjoy. This is a playful reading of the boast, not a supplied moral about sacrifice or a tested cooking recommendation.
entries.meaning_odia: କଥା କହୁଥିବା ମାଛ ନିଜକୁ ରାଜା କହି ନିଜ ମୁଣ୍ଡ ରାନ୍ଧିବା କଥା ଆଗକୁ ଆଣେ। ଆମ ପାଠ ସେହି ଅଦ୍ଭୁତ ଆତ୍ମପ୍ରଶଂସାକୁ ଦେଖେ—ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କ ଭଲ ଲାଗିବା ଭିତରେ ନିଜ ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଦର୍ଶାଯାଉଛି। ଏହା କଥାଟିର ରସମୟ ପାଠ; ଆତ୍ମତ୍ୟାଗର ଉପଦେଶ ବା ପରୀକ୍ଷିତ ରୋଷେଇ ପରାମର୍ଶ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading notices a boast that offers the speaker itself as evidence of its value.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଆତ୍ମପ୍ରଶଂସାର ପ୍ରମାଣ ଭାବେ ବକ୍ତା ନିଜକୁ ଆଗକୁ ଆଣୁଛି।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ ମାଛର ଗର୍ବିତ ସ୍ୱରରେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ପଢ଼ିଲେ। ଅନ୍ୟମାନେ ଦେଖିଲେ, ପ୍ରଶଂସାରେ ନିଜକୁ କେମିତି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଭାବେ ଆଗକୁ ଆଣିଛି। / Readers perform the boast and discuss its peculiar offer. This reading-circle scene is invented, not a cooking demonstration.
entries.cultural_context: The domestic noun gloss identifies bhakuda as Katla; earlier Sanskrit senses name Birata and Rohita separately. No species research, royal history, recipe or traditional sacrifice lesson is inferred.

entries.title: Someone else wears the blame
entries.literal_meaning: The villagers ate the jackfruit; they smeared its sticky substance on Bhandari’s head.
entries.explanation: The eaters and the person marked by the sticky residue are different. The headword explicitly explains laying blame or stigma on someone. Our reading follows that transfer: the visible mark is made to point away from those who acted. It is a way to question an accusation, not evidence about any community’s conduct.
entries.meaning_odia: ପଣସ ଖାଇଥିବା ଲୋକ ଓ ମୁଣ୍ଡରେ ଅଠା ବୋଳାଯାଇଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ଅଲଗା। ଶବ୍ଦର ଅର୍ଥରେ କାହା ଉପରେ ଦୋଷ ବା କଳଙ୍କ ଦେବା କଥା ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଦାଗଟି ପ୍ରକୃତ କାର୍ଯ୍ୟକାରୀଙ୍କ ବଦଳରେ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କୁ ଦୋଷୀ ଦେଖାଉଛି। ଏହା ଅଭିଯୋଗକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବାର ପାଠ, କୌଣସି ସମୁଦାୟର ଆଚରଣର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: A hard division between working and asking
entries.literal_meaning: Whoever works does not eat by asking; whoever eats by asking does not earn food through work.
entries.explanation: The paired clauses draw an absolute line between labour and asking for food. The headword supplies earning a livelihood through work. Our critical response questions the absolute division: the saying does not establish why anyone needs help or whether their work meets their needs. That response is editorial, not a counter-moral supplied by the dictionary.
entries.meaning_odia: ଧାଡ଼ି ଦୁଇଟି ପରିଶ୍ରମ କରି ଖାଇବା ଓ ମାଗି ଖାଇବାକୁ ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଅଲଗା କରିଛି। ଶବ୍ଦର ଅର୍ଥରେ ପରିଶ୍ରମ କରି ପେଟ ପୋଷିବା କଥା ଅଛି। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପାଠ ଏହି କଠୋର ବିଭାଜନକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ। କିଏ କାହିଁକି ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ମାଗୁଛି ବା ତାହାର କାମରୁ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ମେଣ୍ଟୁଛି କି, ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ତାହା ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ। ଏହି ପ୍ରତିପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଆମର, ଅଭିଧାନର ଉପଦେଶ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading refuses to treat asking for help as proof of not working.

entries.title: Let the hair fall
entries.literal_meaning: Let the hair loose, let it fall to the waist; let a hundred thousand champa flowers fall.
entries.explanation: The invitation to loosen the hair opens into an extravagant fall of flowers. The headword’s second sense supports letting hair loose. We read the line as a lyrical image, allowing its abundance to remain playful rather than supplying a practical lesson. The source labels it Dhaga but provides no occasion or explanation of the flower image.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାଳ ଖୋଲିଦେବାର ଆହ୍ୱାନରୁ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଲକ୍ଷେ ଫୁଲ ଝରିବାର ଚିତ୍ରକୁ ଯାଏ। ଶବ୍ଦର ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଅର୍ଥ ବାଳ ଖୋଲି ଲମ୍ବାଇବାକୁ ବୁଝାଏ। ଆମେ ଏହାକୁ ଏକ ଗୀତିମୟ ଚିତ୍ର ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ; ଏହାର ପ୍ରଚୁରତାରେ ରସ ଅଛି, ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ବ୍ୟବହାରିକ ଉପଦେଶ ଯୋଡ଼ୁନାହୁଁ। ଉତ୍ସ ଢଗ ବୋଲି ଚିହ୍ନାଇଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଅବସର ବା ଫୁଲର ଚିତ୍ରର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଦେଇନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading keeps the lyrical invitation and its abundant flower image without inventing a moral.

entries.title: Making a small thing large
entries.literal_meaning: Provisional rendering: like making a tiny pain or sore so large.
entries.explanation: The comparison moves from something called tiny to something made large. The headword explains the smallness and notes its pairing with ଟିକିଏ. Our editorial application asks whether a description enlarges what happened. It cannot tell us that someone’s actual pain is slight or exaggerated; the source gives no person or medical situation to assess.
entries.meaning_odia: ତୁଚ୍ଛ ବୋଲି କୁହାଯାଇଥିବା କିଛିକୁ ବଡ଼ କରିବାର ତୁଳନା ଏଠାରେ ଅଛି। ଶବ୍ଦର ଅର୍ଥ ଅତି ସାମାନ୍ୟ, ଏବଂ ଟିକିଏ ସହ ଏହାର ବ୍ୟବହାର ବିଷୟରେ ଟୀକା ଅଛି। ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ପଚାରେ, ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନାରେ ଘଟଣାଟି ବଢ଼ାଇ ଦିଆଯାଉଛି କି। କାହାର ପ୍ରକୃତ ବଥା ସାମାନ୍ୟ ବା ଅତିରଞ୍ଜିତ ବୋଲି ଏଥିରୁ କହିହେବନାହିଁ; ବିଚାର ପାଇଁ ଉତ୍ସ କୌଣସି ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ବା ଚିକିତ୍ସା ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଦେଇନାହିଁ। ବଥା ଶବ୍ଦଟିର ସଠିକ ଅର୍ଥଛାୟା ଏଠାରେ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our application questions an enlarged description, not the credibility of a person in pain.

entries.title: Was the remark meant for you?
entries.literal_meaning: You are not the one; why are you taking it personally?
entries.explanation: The speaker denies that the listener is the target, then questions the listener’s hurt. The dictionary places the line under taking something personally, not accepting responsibility. Our reading asks how the intended target and the felt effect may differ. The speaker’s denial does not prove that the listener has no reason to be hurt.
entries.meaning_odia: ବକ୍ତା କହୁଛନ୍ତି, କଥାଟି ଶ୍ରୋତାଙ୍କୁ ଲକ୍ଷ କରି କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ; ତେବେ ସେ କାହିଁକି ମନକୁ ନେଉଛନ୍ତି? ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଗତ ଭାବେ ନେବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି, ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ନେବା ଅର୍ଥରେ ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପାଠ କଥାର ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ ଓ ତାହାର ପ୍ରଭାବର ଫରକକୁ ପଚାରେ। ବକ୍ତା ଅସ୍ୱୀକାର କଲେ ବୋଲି ଶ୍ରୋତାଙ୍କ ମନଦୁଃଖ ଅକାରଣ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading distinguishes the speaker’s stated target from the listener’s experience.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ବକ୍ତାଙ୍କ କୁହାଯାଇଥିବା ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ ଓ ଶ୍ରୋତାଙ୍କ ଅନୁଭବକୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ।

entries.cultural_context: No particular offense, relationship or justified dismissal is established. The speaker’s claim is quoted rhetoric, not an independently verified account.

entries.title: The wedding is tomorrow
entries.literal_meaning: Today is mangana, tomorrow the wedding; what is the bride’s mother doing?
entries.explanation: The line puts a question beside an approaching event: today, then tomorrow. The headword explains mangana through the eve of a marriage. Our reading hears urgency in that sequence, while leaving the mother’s actual activity unknown. Nothing here establishes that she has neglected a duty or that preparation belongs to her alone.
entries.meaning_odia: ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ନିକଟେଇ ଆସୁଥିବା ଘଟଣା ପାଖରେ ଏକ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ରଖେ—ଆଜି, ତାପରେ କାଲି। ଶବ୍ଦର ଅର୍ଥରେ ମଙ୍ଗନକୁ ବିବାହର ପୂର୍ବଦିନ ସହ ବୁଝାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ଏହି କ୍ରମରେ ତତ୍ପରତାର ସ୍ୱର ଶୁଣେ, କିନ୍ତୁ ମାଆ ପ୍ରକୃତରେ କଣ କରୁଛନ୍ତି ତାହା ଅଜଣା ରହେ। ସେ କର୍ତ୍ତବ୍ୟରେ ଅବହେଳା କରିଛନ୍ତି ବା ସବୁ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି କେବଳ ତାଙ୍କର କାମ, ଏହାର ପ୍ରମାଣ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading notices urgency without turning the question into proof of a mother’s failure.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ତତ୍ପରତାକୁ ଦେଖେ, ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟିକୁ ମାଆଙ୍କ ବିଫଳତାର ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ।

entries.title: Wisdom and curry received from others
entries.literal_meaning: Wisdom taught by someone else; curry asked for and brought.
entries.explanation: The fragment places received counsel beside received food. The headword explains a plan or understanding gained through another person’s teaching. Our reading follows that shared dependence on another’s contribution. The quotation supplies no ending about whether either will last, work or satisfy; it need not become a verdict against learning from others.

entries.explanation: The divine name becomes the material of an imagined raft. The dictionary places this line under using a means to accomplish something, after the literal raft-making sense. entries.title: Wrongdoing meets magnanimity
entries.literal_meaning: You will steal; you will encounter a magnanimous person.
entries.explanation: The line brings theft and an encounter with a magnanimous person together. The first dictionary sense supplies generosity of character, not merely wealth or rank. Our reading attends to the tension between the act and the person encountered. It leaves the encounter’s result open: the source promises neither pardon nor reform and is not a recommendation to steal.

entries.explanation: The apparent praise turns sharply into rejection. The dictionary places the saying under figurative revulsion, separate from its physical sense. entries.title: Rice and the people who serve
entries.literal_meaning: If there is rice, are people serving for food hard to find?
entries.explanation: The question connects available food with the availability of a servant. The dictionary supplies both serving-for-food and servant senses. Our critical reading asks what is lost when a person’s labour is reduced to a meal. The wording does not establish that workers are plentiful everywhere, that food is adequate payment, or that anyone owes service for being fed.

entries.explanation: The question offers two explanations for conduct the speaker regards as impudent. That meaning comes from the dictionary’s third sense. entries.literal_meaning: Provisional reading: wearing another’s clothes, someone goes to the fair; when people ask, the person keeps nodding.
entries.explanation: The line places another person’s clothing beside a nodding response. Our reading notices a gap between visible appearance and an answer left unspoken. It does not tell us what people ask, what the nod means, or whether the wearer intends to deceive. Receiving or borrowing clothing is not itself evidence of dishonesty.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟର ଲୁଗା ପିନ୍ଧିବା ପାଖରେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ମୁଣ୍ଡ ଟୁଙ୍ଗାରିବାକୁ ରଖେ। ଉତ୍ସର ପଚାଲିଲେ ଶବ୍ଦରୂପ ଅବିକଳ ରହିଛି; ପଚାରିବା ସମ୍ବନ୍ଧୀୟ ଏହି ପାଠ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ। ଆମ ପାଠ ବାହାରକୁ ଦିଶୁଥିବା କଥା ଓ ଅକୁହା ଉତ୍ତର ମଧ୍ୟର ଫାଙ୍କ ଦେଖେ। ଲୋକେ କଣ ପଚାରିଲେ, ମୁଣ୍ଡ ଟୁଙ୍ଗାରିବାର ଅର୍ଥ କଣ, ବା ଠକିବା ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ ଥିଲା କି ନାହିଁ—କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଅନ୍ୟର ଲୁଗା ନେବା ନିଜେ ଅସାଧୁତାର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading leaves the nod’s meaning open rather than supplying a confession.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ମୁଣ୍ଡ ଟୁଙ୍ଗାରିବାର ଅର୍ଥ ଖୋଲା ରଖେ, ସ୍ୱୀକାରୋକ୍ତି ଗଢ଼େନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ନାଟକ ପାଇଁ ଲୁଗା ନେଇଥିବା ଜଣେ ଦର୍ଶକଙ୍କୁ କହିଲେ କିଏ ଦେଇଥିଲେ। ସହାୟତାର କଥା କହିବାରେ ତାଙ୍କର ଲଜ୍ଜା ନଥିଲା। / A performer acknowledges borrowed clothing openly. This response is invented.
entries.cultural_context: Sense1 is wearing clothes. Exact spelling is retained; no owner’s return, withdrawal, shame ending, wearer’s gender or verified fair custom is added.

entries.title: Gone before the head is dry
entries.literal_meaning: The matter of taking the dip is gone by the time the head is dried.
entries.explanation: The line measures a short interval through bathing and drying the head. The dictionary places it under the ordinary sense of bathing. Our reading follows how quickly a matter can cease to hold attention. The wording does not specify a promise, the words spoken during the bath, or why the matter no longer remains.
entries.meaning_odia: ଗାଧୋଇବା ଓ ମୁଣ୍ଡ ଶୁଖାଇବା ମଧ୍ୟର ଅଳ୍ପ ସମୟକୁ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଧରେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ସାଧାରଣ ସ୍ନାନ ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ଦେଖେ, କେତେ ଶୀଘ୍ର ଗୋଟିଏ କଥା ଧ୍ୟାନରୁ ଚାଲିଯାଇପାରେ। କୌଣସି ପ୍ରତିଜ୍ଞା, ଗାଧୋଇବା ବେଳେ କୁହାଯାଇଥିବା ଶବ୍ଦ ବା କଥାଟି ଆଉ ନ ରହିବାର କାରଣ ଦିଆଯାଇନାହିଁ। ତେଣୁ ସେଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ ଆମେ ଭରିଦେଉନାହୁଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading notices a brief hold on attention, without inventing a broken vow.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଅଳ୍ପ ସମୟର ଧ୍ୟାନକୁ ଦେଖେ, ଭଙ୍ଗା ବ୍ରତର କଥା ଗଢ଼େନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଆଲୋଚନାରେ ଉଠିଥିବା କାମଟି ଭୁଲି ନ ଯିବା ପାଇଁ ଦଳର ଜଣେ ସଭ୍ୟ ତାହା ଲେଖି ରଖିଲେ। / A group writes down a task so it is not lost after the discussion. This application is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The earlier religious-vow sense is separate. No ritual failure, hypocrisy, memory diagnosis or bathing efficacy is established; attention is an editorial application of the interval.

entries.title: Cut off food, cut off life
entries.literal_meaning: Stopping someone’s food and cutting off their head are called the same thing.
entries.explanation: The dictionary places the saying under stopping someone’s food. Its stark comparison gives deprivation the force of a threat to life. Our reading treats that equivalence as rhetorical emphasis on food’s importance, not a clinical equation or an instruction to injure anyone. The line does not identify who withholds food or describe an actual incident.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ବନ୍ଦ କରିବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି। ତୀବ୍ର ତୁଳନାଟି ଖାଦ୍ୟରୁ ବଞ୍ଚିତ କରିବାକୁ ଜୀବନ ପ୍ରତି ବିପଦ ପରି ଦେଖାଏ। ଆମ ପାଠ ଏହାକୁ ଖାଦ୍ୟର ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଉପରେ ଜୋର ବୋଲି ବୁଝେ, ଚିକିତ୍ସାଗତ ସମାନତା ବା କାହାକୁ ଆଘାତ ଦେବା ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ନୁହେଁ। କିଏ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ବନ୍ଦ କଲା ବା ସତରେ କଣ ଘଟିଲା, କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading takes the food-deprivation warning seriously without literalizing its violence.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଖାଦ୍ୟରୁ ବଞ୍ଚନାର ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଦେଖେ, ହିଂସାକୁ ଆକ୍ଷରିକ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ସମୂହ ଭୋଜନର ତାଲିକାରେ କାହାର ନାମ ଛାଡ଼ିଗଲା କି ନାହିଁ ଦଳଟି ପୁଣି ଦେଖିଲା। / Organizers check that nobody has been omitted from a shared meal. This scene is invented.
entries.cultural_context: Sense1 is distinct from eating smaller portions in later senses. No dietary, medical or financial recommendation, verified deprivation event or traditional charity rule is supplied.

entries.odia: ଶହେ ଭାକା, ଏକଲେଖା
entries.title: A hundred utterances, one writing
entries.literal_meaning: Provisional reading: a hundred utterances, one written record.
entries.explanation: The source places this compact fragment under matter committed to writing. Our reading understands the contrasting term as spoken utterances, but the head does not separately gloss it. The numbers set many beside one; no verb supplies a precise equation or legal rule. We read an invitation to consider what writing preserves, not proof that every written statement is true.
entries.meaning_odia: ଲିଖିତ ବିଷୟ ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଉତ୍ସ ଏହି ଛୋଟ ଖଣ୍ଡଟି ରଖେ। ଭାକାକୁ ମୁହଁର କଥା ଭାବେ ନେଇ ଆମେ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପାଠ ଦେଉଛୁ; ଏହି ଶବ୍ଦର ଅଲଗା ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏଠି ନାହିଁ। ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଅନେକ ପାଖରେ ଗୋଟିଏକୁ ରଖେ, କିନ୍ତୁ କ୍ରିୟା ନଥିବାରୁ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ସମୀକରଣ ବା ଆଇନର ନିୟମ ମିଳେନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପାଠ ଲେଖା କଣ ରଖିପାରେ ଭାବେ, ସବୁ ଲେଖା ସତ ବୋଲି ମାନେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our provisional reading compares speech and writing without inventing a full rule.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପାଠ କଥା ଓ ଲେଖାକୁ ତୁଳନା କରେ, ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ନିୟମ ଗଢ଼େନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଆଲୋଚନା ପରେ ଦଳଟି ଠିକ୍ ହୋଇଥିବା କାମଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଲେଖିଲା ଓ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ ପୁଣି ପଢ଼ି ଶୁଣାଇଲା। / A group writes and checks its agreed tasks together. This application is invented.
entries.cultural_context: Exact ଭାକା and fused ଏକଲେଖା remain unchanged. Other sayings and Krishna Singh literary examples in this long head are separate witnesses, not this fragment’s authorship.

entries.title: Coming and going alone
entries.literal_meaning: You came alone and will go alone; the family will not go with you.
entries.explanation: The repeated solitude stands against the family named in the final phrase. The dictionary gives family members, including children, as the relevant sense. Our reading hears a reflection on mortality and the limits of accompaniment. That interpretation does not make family affection worthless, require withdrawal from loved ones, or prove a doctrine about what follows death.
entries.meaning_odia: ପୁଣିପୁଣି ଆସୁଥିବା ଏକାପଣ ପାଖରେ ଶେଷ ଖଣ୍ଡ ପରିବାରକୁ ରଖେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ପିଲାମାନଙ୍କ ସହ ପରିବାରସ୍ଥ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ଅର୍ଥ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ଏଠି ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ଓ ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ରହିପାରିବାର ସୀମା ନେଇ ଭାବନା ଶୁଣେ। ଏହା ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା; ପରିବାରର ସ୍ନେହ ମୂଲ୍ୟହୀନ ବୋଲି ନୁହେଁ। ପ୍ରିୟଜନଙ୍କୁ ଛାଡ଼ି ରହିବା ବା ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ପରେ କଣ ହୁଏ ସେବିଷୟରେ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ମତ ମଧ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading holds life’s limits beside the value of present companionship.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଜୀବନର ସୀମା ସହ ବର୍ତ୍ତମାନର ସାଙ୍ଗତ୍ୟର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ରଖେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ପଢ଼ି ଜଣେ ପ୍ରିୟଜନଙ୍କ ସହ ସମୟ କାଟିବାକୁ ଠିକ୍ କଲେ। / A reader responds by making time for loved ones. This response is invented, not a traditional use claim.
entries.cultural_context: Arrival and departure are the quoted images; mortality is our interpretive frame. The later Fakirmohan example illustrates another sense and does not identify the saying’s author.

entries.odia: ଯାହା ବାପ ଚଢ଼େ ଘୋଡ଼ା, ତା ପୁଅ ଚଢ଼େ ଥୋଡ଼ା
entries.title: The father rides; the son, a little
entries.literal_meaning: Whose father rides a horse, that son rides a little.
entries.explanation: The rhyme moves from a father’s riding to a smaller amount in the son’s clause. The dictionary quotes it under “slightly; a little.” Our reading notices the partial echo between generations, without turning it into a law of inheritance. The line does not explain how either person learned, measure their skill, or establish that every child repeats a parent’s occupation.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାପଙ୍କ ଘୋଡ଼ା ଚଢ଼ିବାରୁ ପୁଅଙ୍କ ଖଣ୍ଡରେ ଅଳ୍ପ ପରିମାଣକୁ ଛନ୍ଦ ଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ସାମାନ୍ୟରେ ବା ଈଷତ ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ପିଢ଼ି ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଆଂଶିକ ପ୍ରତିଧ୍ୱନି ଦେଖେ, ବଂଶଗତ ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ। କିଏ କିପରି ଶିଖିଲେ, କାହାର ଦକ୍ଷତା କେତେ, ବା ସବୁ ପିଲା ବାପମାଆଙ୍କ ପେଶା ନିଅନ୍ତି କି ନାହିଁ—ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ତାହା ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading hears a small repetition, not an inherited destiny.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଅଳ୍ପ ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତି ଶୁଣେ, ବଂଶଗତ ଭାଗ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ବାପଙ୍କ ସହ କାମ ଦେଖିଥିବା ପୁଅଟି ନିଜେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଛୋଟ କାମ ଶିଖିଲା। ତାଙ୍କ ଅନ୍ୟ ପସନ୍ଦକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ପରିବାର ସ୍ଥାନ ଦେଲା। / A child learns one small task while retaining other interests. This scene is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The quotation’s father and son remain intact, without an added biological or caste claim. The earlier Radhanath Darbar verse illustrates a different sense and is not this saying’s authorship.

entries.title: Neither doing it nor making way
entries.literal_meaning: Provisional reading: that person neither shits nor makes way.
entries.explanation: The blunt bodily image pairs not doing something with not letting another pass. The dictionary supplies making room for another as the relevant sense of leaving the way. Our reading applies the contrast to obstruction: someone neither proceeds nor clears space. This does not identify a real person’s health, intention or circumstances, and it is not advice about bodily functions.
entries.meaning_odia: ରୁକ୍ଷ ଶାରୀରିକ ଚିତ୍ରଟି ନିଜେ ନ କରିବା ସହ ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ବାଟ ନ ଛାଡ଼ିବାକୁ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ଯିବାକୁ ଜାଗା ଦେବା ଅର୍ଥ ଅଛି। ଉତ୍ସର ହଗ ଶବ୍ଦରୂପ ଅବିକଳ ରଖି ଆମେ ଏହାର ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପାଠ ଦେଉଛୁ। ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ କେହି ନିଜେ ଆଗେଇନାହାନ୍ତି କି ଜାଗା ମଧ୍ୟ ଛାଡ଼ୁନାହାନ୍ତି। ଏଥିରୁ ପ୍ରକୃତ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ ସ୍ୱାସ୍ଥ୍ୟ, ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ ବା ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ ହୁଏନାହିଁ। ଏହା ଶରୀର ସମ୍ବନ୍ଧୀୟ ପରାମର୍ଶ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading describes obstruction while keeping the coarse register visible.

entries.title: Still tying the turban as court closes
entries.literal_meaning: While tying the turban, the court closes.
entries.explanation: The repeated tying phrase keeps preparation in progress while the court closes. The dictionary places the line under an office or court stopping work, not dismissal from a job. Our reading notices an opportunity ending before preparation finishes. The line does not say why the person took time, identify their role, or establish a particular court schedule.
entries.meaning_odia: ପାଗ ବାନ୍ଧିବା ଚାଲିଥିବା ବେଳେ କଚିରି ବନ୍ଦ ହୁଏ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି କଚିରିର କାମ ବନ୍ଦ ହେବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି, ଚାକିରିରୁ ବାହାରିବା ଅର୍ଥରେ ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ସରିବା ଆଗରୁ ସୁଯୋଗ ସରିଯାଏ। କାହିଁକି ସମୟ ଲାଗିଲା, ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ ପଦ କଣ ବା କଚିରିର ସମୟସୂଚୀ କିପରି—ଉତ୍ସ ତାହା କହେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading contrasts unfinished preparation with a closing opportunity.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠରେ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ଅସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ, ସୁଯୋଗ କିନ୍ତୁ ସରିଲାଣି।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଜଣେ ଫର୍ମଟି ସଜାଉଥିବା ବେଳେ ଆବେଦନ ସମୟ ସରିଗଲା। ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ଥର ପାଇଁ ସେ ଆଗୁଆ ତାରିଖ ଲେଖିରଖିଲେ। / Someone misses an application deadline while arranging the form, then plans ahead for the next one. This scene is invented.

entries.title: Naming the rain amid the flood
entries.literal_meaning: The house is flooded, the water knee-deep; the one-eyed person says it is raining in torrents.
entries.explanation: The house and knee-deep water show a consequence; the speaker names the rain. The dictionary explicitly glosses torrential rain, not a light shower. Our reading asks whether naming an event is enough when its effects need attention. We reject using the quoted disability label to explain anyone’s judgment: the line supplies no evidence that impaired sight causes such a response.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘର ବୁଡ଼ି ପାଣି ଆଣ୍ଠୁଏ; ବକ୍ତା ବର୍ଷାର କଥା କହୁଛନ୍ତି। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଦୁଲୁକିବା ଅର୍ଥ ପ୍ରବଳ ବର୍ଷା, ଅଳ୍ପ ବର୍ଷା ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପାଠ ପଚାରେ: ପ୍ରଭାବକୁ ଦେଖି କାମ କରିବା ଦରକାର ବେଳେ ଘଟଣାର ନାମ କହିବା ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ କି? ଉତ୍ସର ଦୃଷ୍ଟିସମ୍ବନ୍ଧୀୟ ତାଚ୍ଛଲ୍ୟକୁ ଆମେ ବିଚାରଶକ୍ତିର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଭାବେ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରୁନାହୁଁ। ଏପରି ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟାର କାରଣ ଦୃଷ୍ଟିବାଧା ବୋଲି ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading attends to consequences without endorsing the disability taunt.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ପ୍ରଭାବକୁ ଦେଖେ, ଦୃଷ୍ଟିବାଧା ସମ୍ବନ୍ଧୀୟ ତାଚ୍ଛଲ୍ୟକୁ ସମର୍ଥନ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଛାତରୁ ପାଣି ଝରୁଥିଲା। କେବଳ ବର୍ଷାର କଥା ନ କହି ଦଳଟି ଭିଜୁଥିବା କାଗଜକୁ ଶୁଖିଲା ସ୍ଥାନକୁ ନେଲା। / A group moves papers away from a leak instead of merely describing the rain. This response is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The critical response is editorial, not a supplied traditional counter-moral. No actual flood, medical assessment or disability-group trait is documented; other senses concern vibration and fear.

entries.title: We know why you keep passing
entries.literal_meaning: We know what you are moving back and forth for.
entries.explanation: The speaker claims to know the purpose behind someone’s repeated passing. The dictionary places the line under movement to and fro, not its later sense of delaying work. Our reading hears a knowing challenge, while leaving open whether the claimed knowledge is correct. The line identifies neither the purpose nor the relationship; it does not establish deceit, romance or wrongdoing.
entries.meaning_odia: କାହାର ବାରମ୍ବାର ଯିବାଆସିବା ପଛର କାରଣ ଜାଣିଛୁ ବୋଲି ବକ୍ତା କହୁଛନ୍ତି। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଯିବାଆସିବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି, ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ କାମରେ ବିଳମ୍ବ ଅର୍ଥରେ ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ବକ୍ତା ଜାଣିଥିବାର ଭଙ୍ଗୀରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠାଉଛନ୍ତି। ସେ ପ୍ରକୃତରେ ଠିକ୍ ଜାଣନ୍ତି କି ନାହିଁ, ତାହା ଖୋଲା ରହେ। ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ ବା ସମ୍ପର୍କ ଅଜଣା; ଠକାମି, ପ୍ରେମ ବା ଅପରାଧ ଏଥିରୁ ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: The speaker claims insight; our reading leaves that claim unproved.
entries.odia_summary: ବକ୍ତା ଜାଣିବାର ଦାବି କରନ୍ତି; ଆମ ପାଠ ତାକୁ ପ୍ରମାଣ ମାନେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଟେବୁଲ୍ ପାଖେ ବାରମ୍ବାର ଆସୁଥିବା ସାଥୀଙ୍କୁ ଜଣେ ପଚାରିଲେ, କିଛି ଦରକାର କି? ଅନୁମାନରେ ଅଟକି ନ ରହି ସେ ଉତ୍ତର ଶୁଣିଲେ। / Someone asks a repeatedly passing colleague what they need and listens instead of relying on a guess. This response is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The invented response asks rather than asserts knowledge; it is an editorial alternative, not a recorded traditional use. No gender, fixed social setting or hidden motive is supplied.

entries.title: The dragging is what hurts
entries.literal_meaning: Being taken by a tiger does not hurt; the dragging hurts.
entries.explanation: The line sets being taken by a tiger beside the discomfort of being dragged. The dictionary quotes it under dragging along the ground. Our reading hears an exaggerated complaint that singles out one part of a larger ordeal. It does not measure pain or establish that the larger danger is harmless; no actual encounter or speaker is identified.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାଘ ନେବା ସହ ଭୂମିରେ ଘୋଷାରି ନେବାର କଷ୍ଟକୁ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ରଖେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ଭୂମିରେ ଟାଣିନେବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ବଡ଼ ଦୁର୍ଦ୍ଦଶାର ଗୋଟିଏ ଅଂଶକୁ ବାଛି ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତିରେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରାଯାଏ। ଏହା ଯନ୍ତ୍ରଣାର ମାପ ନୁହେଁ ବା ବଡ଼ ବିପଦ ନିରାପଦ ବୋଲି ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ। ପ୍ରକୃତ ଘଟଣା ବା ବକ୍ତା ଚିହ୍ନଟ ହୋଇନାହାନ୍ତି।
entries.english_summary: Our reading singles out one discomfort within an exaggerated ordeal.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଅତିଶୟ ଦୁର୍ଦ୍ଦଶା ଭିତରୁ ଗୋଟିଏ କଷ୍ଟ ଅଭିଯୋଗର କେନ୍ଦ୍ର।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଲମ୍ବା ଯାତ୍ରାର ସବୁ ଅସୁବିଧା ମଧ୍ୟରୁ ଭଙ୍ଗା ବ୍ୟାଗ୍ ଟାଣିବା କଥାଟି ଜଣେ ବାରମ୍ବାର କହିଲେ। / A traveller keeps returning to the broken bag amid a difficult journey. This comparison is invented.
entries.cultural_context: Exact fused ବାଘନବା remains unchanged. The quoted contrast is rhetorical, not medical or wildlife advice. Later road and laziness senses do not supply this saying’s meaning.

entries.title: One keeps; another will squander
entries.literal_meaning: The books say: one will squander; one is keeping.
entries.explanation: The saying invokes books while putting keeping beside future squandering. The dictionary’s following explanation describes one person laboriously saving wealth and another later wasting it. Our reading notices the contrast between their actions. No particular book is named or independently checked, and the line does not establish a universal family pattern or identify an heir.
entries.meaning_odia: ବହିର କଥା ଉଠାଇ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ରଖିବା ସହ ଉଡ଼ାଇବାକୁ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଅଭିଧାନର ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ଜଣେ କଷ୍ଟରେ ଧନ ସଞ୍ଚନ୍ତି, ପରେ ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣେ ତାହା ଅପବ୍ୟୟ କରନ୍ତି। ଆମ ପାଠ ଏହି ଦୁଇ କାମର ବିରୋଧକୁ ଦେଖେ। କେଉଁ ବହି, ଉତ୍ସ ନାମ କହେନାହିଁ; ସ୍ୱତନ୍ତ୍ର ଯାଞ୍ଚ ମଧ୍ୟ ହୋଇନାହିଁ। ଏହା ସବୁ ପରିବାରର ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ ବା କୌଣସି ଉତ୍ତରାଧିକାରୀଙ୍କ ପରିଚୟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading contrasts saving and waste, without verifying a scripture.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ସଞ୍ଚୟ ଓ ଅପବ୍ୟୟର ବିରୋଧ ଦେଖେ, ଶାସ୍ତ୍ର ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଦଳଟି ଅନେକ ମାସ ଧରି ଜମାଇଥିବା ଟଙ୍କା ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ସଜାରେ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ହେଲା। ପରେ ସମସ୍ତେ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚର ଯୋଜନା ମିଳିତ ଭାବେ କଲେ। / A group revisits spending decisions after savings go on unnecessary decoration. This scene is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The ancient-books assertion belongs to the dictionary and quoted voice, not verified textual history. Exact tense contrast is retained; there is no financial recommendation or prescribed relationship.

entries.odia: ଲାଗି ରହି ଥାଉ ଯାଆସ ଆସ, ନ ଥାଉ ମୁଠିଏ ଭାତରେ ଆଶ
entries.title: Let the visits continue
entries.literal_meaning: Let the coming and going continue; let there be no hope of a handful of rice.
entries.explanation: The line wishes for continued visits while setting aside an expectation of rice. Its dictionary placement concerns frequenting a place. Our reading values contact beyond what a visit might provide. That application is editorial: the source names no particular friendship, household or exchange, and it does not require a hungry guest to deny their needs.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯିବାଆସିବା ଚାଲିଥାଉ, କିନ୍ତୁ ମୁଠିଏ ଭାତର ଆଶା ନ ଥାଉ—ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଏହି ଇଚ୍ଛା କହେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ବାରମ୍ବାର କୌଣସି ସ୍ଥାନକୁ ଯିବା ଅର୍ଥ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ପ୍ରାପ୍ତିର ଆଶାଠାରୁ ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଦେଖେ। ଏହା ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ; ଉତ୍ସ କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ବନ୍ଧୁତା, ପରିବାର ବା ଦେଣନେଣ କହେନାହିଁ। ଭୋକିଲା ଅତିଥି ନିଜ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ଲୁଚାଇବାକୁ ବାଧ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading separates continued contact from an expected material return.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଯିବାଆସିବା ଓ ପ୍ରାପ୍ତିର ଆଶା ଅଲଗା ରହେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଦୁଇ ବନ୍ଧୁ କିଛି ଦେବାନେବା ନ ଥିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଦେଖା କରୁଥିଲେ। ଦରକାର ପଡ଼ିଲେ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କଥା ମଧ୍ୟ ଖୋଲାଖୋଲି କହୁଥିଲେ। / Two friends keep meeting and can also speak honestly about needing help. This scene is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The earlier Fakirmohan Galpaswalpa passage illustrates coming and going separately; it is not this saying’s authorship. No fixed hospitality custom, denial of food or duty is established.

entries.title: Six ears and a disclosed secret
entries.literal_meaning: Six ears, disclosure of the secret.
entries.explanation: The dictionary explains six ears as three people: a matter known to two reaches a third. The short saying compresses that disclosure into a phrase. Our reading notices how adding a listener changes the circle of knowledge. It does not prove that every third person spreads a secret or forbid seeking appropriate help about something troubling.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଛଅଟି କାନ ଅର୍ଥ ତିନି ଜଣ: ଦୁଇ ଜଣଙ୍କ ଗୁପ୍ତ କଥା ତୃତୀୟ ଜଣ ଜାଣନ୍ତି। ଛୋଟ ଢଗଟି ସେହି ପ୍ରକାଶକୁ ଧରେ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଆଉ ଜଣେ ଶୁଣିଲେ ଜାଣିଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ପରିସର ବଦଳେ। ସବୁ ତୃତୀୟ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି କଥା ପ୍ରଚାର କରନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ। ଚିନ୍ତାଜନକ ବିଷୟରେ ଉପଯୁକ୍ତ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ମାଗିବାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଏହା ବାରଣ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading tracks a wider circle, not inevitable betrayal.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଜାଣିବାର ପରିସର ବଢ଼େ, ବିଶ୍ୱାସଘାତ ଅନିବାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଦୁଇ ଜଣଙ୍କ ଯୋଜନା ଆଉ ଜଣଙ୍କୁ କହିବା ଆଗରୁ ସେମାନେ କଣ ଭାଗ କରିବେ ଠିକ୍ କଲେ। / Two collaborators agree what to share before inviting another into their planning. This example is invented.
entries.cultural_context: Exact quotation ଛଡ଼ାକାନ differs from headword ଛଡ଼କାନ and is not repaired. The supplied secret-disclosure sense guides the rendering; no named author, ritual or historical incident is established.

entries.odia: କାଳୀମାୟୀ, ଚୂନ ବୋଳିଲେ କି ଗୋରୀ ହୋଇ?
entries.title: A question about complexion
entries.literal_meaning: Dark woman, does applying lime make you fair?
entries.explanation: The question places a woman’s dark complexion beside an applied white substance. The dictionary quotes it under the domestic word for woman, not its earlier magical or divine senses. Our critical reading asks why fairness should be a measure of worth at all. That response is editorial: the source supplies the taunt, not a stated challenge to colour prejudice.
entries.meaning_odia: କଳା ରଙ୍ଗର ସ୍ତ୍ରୀଙ୍କ ଦେହରେ ଚୂନ ବୋଳି ଗୋରା ହେବାର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ଉଠିଛି। ଉତ୍ସରେ ଏହା ନାରୀ ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି, ପୂର୍ବର କୁହୁକ ବା ଦେବତା ଅର୍ଥରେ ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାମୂଳକ ପାଠ ପଚାରେ, ଗୋରା ରଙ୍ଗ କାହିଁକି ମଣିଷର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ କରିବ? ଏହା ଆମ ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା; ଉତ୍ସରେ ଥିବା ତାଚ୍ଛଲ୍ୟକୁ ପାରମ୍ପରିକ ସମତାର ବାଣୀ ବୋଲି କହୁନାହୁଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical response questions the colour hierarchy implied by the taunt.
entries.odia_summary: ରଙ୍ଗକୁ ମୂଲ୍ୟର ମାପ କରିବା ଧାରଣାକୁ ଆମ ପାଠ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଏକ ପୁରୁଣା କଥା ଆଲୋଚନାରେ ଜଣେ ରଙ୍ଗକୁ ନେଇ ଥଟ୍ଟା କଲେ। ଆଉ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, ଦେହର ରଙ୍ଗ ମଣିଷର ମୂଲ୍ୟ କହେନାହିଁ। / In an imagined discussion, a listener challenges a colour-based joke. This response is invented.
entries.cultural_context: Attributed gendered colour taunt, not a biological, cosmetic or medical claim. No historical speaker, incident or community-wide attitude established.

entries.odia: ଥାଇକରି ଯେ ଖାଇମନ କରେ ତା ମୁହଁଟା ପୋଡ଼ୁ
entries.title: A curse directed at craving
entries.literal_meaning: Provisional reading: may the mouth of one who craves while having be burnt.
entries.explanation: The headword defines wanting a particular food. The line curses someone described as having yet craving; it does not specify what is possessed or establish that their needs are met. Our critical reading separates a speaker’s accusation from knowledge of another’s circumstances. Neither the curse nor the accusation becomes advice about how a person should eat.
entries.meaning_odia: ଖାଇମନ କରିବାର ଅର୍ଥ କୌଣସି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ପାଇଁ ଇଚ୍ଛା କରିବା। ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ଚାହୁଁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କୁ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଅଭିଶାପ ଦିଏ। କଣ ଅଛି ବା ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ପୂରଣ ହୋଇଛି କି, ଉତ୍ସ କହେନାହିଁ; ଏହି ପାଠ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ କଥକଙ୍କ ଅଭିଯୋଗ ଓ ଅନ୍ୟର ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଜାଣିବା ଅଲଗା। ଅଭିଶାପଟି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ବା ଆଚରଣର ପରାମର୍ଶ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: The accusation leaves the person’s possessions and actual needs unspecified.
entries.odia_summary: କଣ ଅଛି ଓ କଣ ଦରକାର, ଅଭିଯୋଗଟି ତାହା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଆଉ ଗୋଟିଏ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ମାଗିବାରୁ ଜଣେ ଅତିଥିଙ୍କୁ ଦୋଷ ଦିଆଗଲା। ଘରଲୋକ ପ୍ରଥମେ ତାଙ୍କ କଥା ଶୁଣିବାକୁ କହିଲେ। / An imagined host asks others to hear a guest’s reason before judging a request. This alternative is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The later pregnancy sense does not identify this subject. The following Nilamani Chintatarangini passage is a separate literary illustration, not this saying’s author.

entries.odia: ଆସିବୁ ଯିବୁରେ କଳାମାଣିକ! ତୋହରି ପାଇଁ କି ନିତି ଗଞ୍ଜଣା, ପିଠିରେ ତିନ୍ତୁଳି ଛାଟ
entries.title: Visits and a painful complaint
entries.literal_meaning: Provisional reading: come and go, dark jewel! Must there be daily reproach for you, a tamarind switch on the back?
entries.explanation: The address joins coming and going to a question about repeated reproach and a switch on the back. The dictionary defines the switch but does not identify who speaks, visits, receives a blow or inflicts one. Our reading hears a complaint about a connection’s painful cost, while leaving those roles open. It neither reconstructs a romance nor justifies punishment.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆସିବାଯିବାର ସମ୍ବୋଧନ ସହ ନିତି ଗଞ୍ଜଣା ଓ ପିଠିରେ ଛାଟର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଅଛି। ଏହା ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପାଠ; କିଏ କହୁଛନ୍ତି, ଯାଆନ୍ତି, ମାଡ଼ ଖାଆନ୍ତି ବା ଦିଅନ୍ତି, ଉତ୍ସ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କରେନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଏକ ସମ୍ପର୍କର କଷ୍ଟକୁ ନେଇ ଅଭିଯୋଗ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ଏଥିରୁ ପ୍ରେମକାହାଣୀ ତିଆରି କରୁନାହୁଁ ବା ଦଣ୍ଡକୁ ଯଥାର୍ଥ କହୁନାହୁଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our provisional reading hears complaint without assigning the unnamed roles.
entries.odia_summary: ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପାଠରେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ ଅଛି; ଅକୁହା ଭୂମିକା ଭରିଦିଆଯାଏନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଆଲୋଚନାରେ ଜଣେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟିକୁ ପ୍ରେମକାହାଣୀ କହିଲେ। ଅନ୍ୟଜଣେ ପଚାରିଲେ, କଥକ ଓ ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଉତ୍ସ କେଉଁଠି ଚିହ୍ନାଇଛି? / An imagined reader questions an unsupported romantic reconstruction. The exchange is invented.
entries.cultural_context: No gender, lover, deity, actual assault or disciplinary custom established. The dictionary’s adjacent physical claims about switches are not adopted as practical guidance.

entries.title: Three separate commanders
entries.literal_meaning: Three separate victorious generals.
entries.explanation: The dictionary defines the title as a victorious general and explicitly explains this saying as work going wrong when three people oversee it. That is the source’s explanation, not a rule that three people cannot cooperate. Our editorial application asks whether responsibility and decisions have been made clear when several people supervise one task.
entries.meaning_odia: ଉତ୍ସରେ ଫତେଖାଁ ଜୟଲାଭ କରିଥିବା ସେନାପତି। ତିନି ଜଣଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ତନଖିବାର ଭାର ଥିଲେ କାମ ବିଗିଡ଼େ ବୋଲି ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହି ଢଗକୁ ବୁଝାଇଛି। ଏହା ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା; ତିନି ଜଣ କେବେ ମିଳି କାମ କରିପାରିବେନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ଅନେକେ ତଦାରଖ କଲେ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ଓ ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି କେତେ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ, ସେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠେ।
entries.english_summary: The source warns of divided supervision; our application asks for clear responsibilities.
entries.odia_summary: ଉତ୍ସରେ ତନଖିବାର ଭାରକୁ ନେଇ ସତର୍କତା; ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କରିବାର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଏକ ପତ୍ରିକାର ପୃଷ୍ଠାକୁ ତିନି ଜଣ ଅଲଗା ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ଦେଲେ। ଦଳଟି ମିଳି ଅନ୍ତିମ ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି କିଏ ନେବେ ଠିକ୍ କଲା। / In an imagined editing team, conflicting directions lead to an agreed decision process. The resolution is invented.
entries.cultural_context: A title used in an attributed saying, not a named historical commander or an ethnic trait. No origin story or universal management law established.

entries.title: One phrase, food and body
entries.literal_meaning: One who eats dry fare becomes dry and rough.
entries.explanation: The dictionary links two senses of the repeated phrase: dry food without ghee or curry, and an unoiled, dry body. Its inserted numbers identify those senses, not spoken words. The saying makes a food-to-body connection; the entry does not verify that connection medically. Our critical reading notices the wordplay without treating someone’s food or appearance as a measure of worth.

entries.explanation: The line places admired appearance beside a supply of ghee. It does not explain who admired her or why. entries.title: Why signal when nothing is there?
entries.literal_meaning: There are no mangoes on the mango tree; why throw a stick? I have no money at my waist; why signal with your eyes?
entries.explanation: The dictionary defines the thrown stick as one used to knock fruit down. Two questions pair an empty tree with a speaker who says they have no money. Our reading hears a challenge to an expectation without its object. The eye signal’s purpose and the relationship remain unstated; neither a bargain nor flirtation is established.

entries.literal_meaning: An alu leaf or a saru leaf—will it become betel? Will the woman you later take as wife know your mind?

Our critical reading asks why understanding should be ruled out beforehand. The line supplies no particular marriage history, earlier partner or cause; its doubt is not a fact about women or later marriages.

ଦାନ୍ତ ଅଛି ଦରଘଷା।
entries.literal_meaning: Akhai is observing a fast: she ate a dol-full of rice in one sitting, yet her teeth are still only half-brushed.
entries.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରକୃତ କାମକୁ ଲୁଚାଇ ଅନ୍ୟମାନଙ୍କ ଆଗରେ ସଂଯମର ଦେଖାଣି କରିବାକୁ ଏହି ଢଗରେ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The comic contradiction is between a claim of fasting and the large meal already eaten. The closing image keeps up the appearance of a morning before food, although the meal has happened. Read this as a criticism of pretence: the declared discipline does not agree with the action. The journal’s gloss supports that general reading; the connection between tooth-cleaning and the pretended sequence of events is an editorial interpretation.
entries.usage_example: Someone announces a day of restraint after quietly taking the largest share. A listener may recall this saying to question the performance of self-denial. This is a newly composed example, not a recorded conversation.
entries.cultural_context: The verse uses food, an observance called ଓଷା, and tooth-cleaning to make its contrast visible. Its female figure is part of this wording, not a claim about women or religious observance generally. ଡୋଲିକ is retained as a traditional quantity expression; no modern weight or volume has been established.

witnesses.locator: Printed p.17 / PDF page2, Odia example2, beginning ଅଖାଇ କରିଛି ଓଷା.
witnesses.note: Published text corroborates the three-line saying and supplies a brief interpretation about concealing one’s actual nature. Uploaded PDF page1, second saying, is the selection witness and supplies displayed କରିଚି; journal has କରିଛି.

entries.origin_note: A version appears in Sagarika Dalai’s March 2019 comparative article. This dates an inspected printed witness only; first authorship, earliest occurrence and geographical distribution remain unknown.

entries.odia_summary: କାମରେ ନଥିବା ସଂଯମକୁ କଥାରେ ଦେଖାଇବାର ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ।
entries.english_summary: A claim of self-denial rings hollow after the indulgence has already happened.

entries.title: A carefree song on the way home
entries.odia:
ଅଚିନ୍ତା ନାରୀ ବାପଘର ଯାଏ
ମନ ଫୁଲାଣୀଆ ଗୀତ ଗାଏ।
entries.literal_meaning: A carefree woman goes to her father’s home, singing a cheerful song.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚିନ୍ତା ନଥିଲେ ମନର ଆନନ୍ଦ ଗୀତରେ ପ୍ରକାଶ ପାଏ—ବାପଘରକୁ ଯାଉଥିବା ନାରୀର ଚିତ୍ରକୁ ଏଠାରେ ଏଭଳି ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: A carefree woman sings cheerfully while going to her father’s home. This edition reads the scene as ease showing itself in song. That is an editorial reading; the text does not explain why she is free of worry.
entries.usage_example: After finishing a difficult piece of work, someone hums happily on the journey home. This saying could describe that unburdened mood. This is a newly composed illustration, not a recorded use.
entries.cultural_context: The destination is ବାପଘର, the woman’s father’s home. It provides a concrete family setting for the cheerful journey. Nothing in these two lines establishes the conditions in her other household or makes this experience universal for women.

witnesses.locator: Opening list, ଅଚିନ୍ତା ନାରୀ ବାପଘର ଯାଏ, page text lines 60–62.

entries.english_summary: A carefree heart finds a cheerful song on the way to a familiar home.
entries.narrative_credit: Translation and interpretation by Project Odisha, informed by the wording witnesses below.

entries.title: Like grandfather, like grandson
entries.odia:
ଅଜା ଜାଣି ନାତି
ମାଛ ଜାଣି କାତି।
entries.literal_meaning: As the grandfather, so the grandson; as the fish, so its scales.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଜାଙ୍କ ସହ ନାତିର ମେଳକୁ ମାଛ ଓ ତାହାର କାତିର ମେଳ ସହ ତୁଳନା କରାଯାଇଛି। ଏଠାରେ ପରିବାରର ଜଣକ ଭିତରେ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କ ଲକ୍ଷଣ ଦେଖାଯିବାର କଥା ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The parallel pairs suggest a likeness: the grandson takes after his grandfather, just as the scales belong to the kind of fish that bears them. This is an editorial reading of the comparison. The lines name no particular good or bad trait.
entries.usage_example: A grandson tells a story with the same gestures and mischievous smile as his grandfather. Someone watching might recall these lines. This example is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: ଅଜା denotes the maternal grandfather, and ନାତି a grandson. The family comparison is paired with the visible covering of a fish: କାତି is read here as scales. The image suggests resemblance without establishing that character is fixed by ancestry.

witnesses.locator: Opening list, two lines beginning ଅଜା ଜାଣି ନାତି; inspected page lines 64–66.
witnesses.note: Matches uploaded PDF page 1, sixth saying. Uploaded image supplies the display reading. The website follows the same surrounding order; independence is not established.

entries.english_summary: A grandson’s resemblance to his grandfather is pictured through a fish and its scales.
entries.narrative_credit: Translation and interpretation by Project Odisha, informed by the wording witness below.

entries.title: Wedding plans with no money
entries.odia:
ଅଣ୍ଟାରେ ନଥାଇ ଧନ
ପୁଅ ବାହା କରି ମନ।
entries.literal_meaning: No money tucked at the waist, yet the mind is set on getting the son married.
entries.meaning_odia: ହାତରେ ସମ୍ବଳ ନଥାଇ ବଡ଼ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚର ଯୋଜନା କରିବାର ଅସଙ୍ଗତିକୁ ଏଠାରେ ପୁଅର ବାହାଘର ଇଚ୍ଛା ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ି ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The wish to arrange the son’s wedding runs ahead of the money available. This edition reads the contrast as a reminder to match a plan with the means to carry it out. The saying supplies the pointed wedding image; this practical interpretation is editorial.
entries.usage_example: Someone begins planning a large celebration before working out how to pay for it. These lines could be recalled while discussing a realistic budget. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: The money is pictured at the waist, making available funds tangible. A son’s wedding supplies the example of an undertaking that needs resources. The wording specifies no particular ceremony, sum or marriage payment.

witnesses.locator: Saying at inspected page text lines 79–81 and repeated at line 100; both public occurrences have ପୁଅଁ.
witnesses.note: Uploaded PDF page 1, eighth saying, supplies readable ପୁଅ and the two-line arrangement. Its first word contains an empty-box glyph, so only that damaged word is supplied from public ଅଣ୍ଟାରେ. The public witness spells ପୁଅଁ in both occurrences; the display retains uploaded ପୁଅ. This is an explicit composite reading, not an exact transcription of the complete public text or a recovery of the missing uploaded glyph. Shared textual lineage is possible.

entries.english_summary: The wish for a wedding runs ahead of the means to arrange it.

entries.title: Care without spending
entries.odia:
ଅଣ୍ଟାରୁ ପଇସା ସାରିବି ନାଇଁ
ପୁଅକୁ ନୁଖୁରା ରଖିବି ନାଇଁ।
entries.literal_meaning: I will not spend the money at my waist; I will not leave my son dry and unoiled.
entries.meaning_odia: ପଇସା ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ କରିବାକୁ ମନ ନାହିଁ, ଅଥଚ ପୁଅର ଯତ୍ନରେ ଅଭାବ ରଖିବାକୁ ବି ମନ ନାହିଁ। ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ବିନା କାମ ସାରିବାର ଏହି ଦୁଇମୁହାଁ ଇଚ୍ଛାକୁ କଥାଟି ଧରିଛି।
entries.explanation: The speaker wants to keep every coin while also seeing the son cared for. The image of leaving him dry and unoiled makes that tension concrete. The inspected Odia Vasa gloss reads the saying as the miser’s conflict between holding on to money and wanting a task accomplished.
entries.usage_example: A person wants a broken household item repaired properly but refuses every necessary expense. Someone could use this saying to point out the conflict. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: ନୁଖୁରା carries the sense of dryness or absence of oiliness. Applied to the son, it is read here as being left unoiled, with care or upkeep as the wider implication. The verse does not specify hair, skin, a particular oil, or a grooming ceremony.

witnesses.locator: Inspected page lines 83–85 and repeated at line 102, beginning ଅଣ୍ଟାରୁ ପଇସା.
witnesses.note: Supplies complete first word ଅଣ୍ଟାରୁ where upload page 1 has a missing-box glyph. Upload page 2 begins with readable second line. Preserve uploaded ନାଇଁ and two-line form. Shared lineage is possible.

witnesses.locator: Item 30, inspected page text line 56.
witnesses.note: Wording uses ନାହିଁ in both clauses rather than displayed ନାଇଁ. Its parenthetical gloss describes a miser caught between retaining money and accomplishing a desired task. This supports interpretation without proving independent origin.

variants.odia:
ଏଣେ ପୁଅ ମୁଣ୍ଡକୁ ଆଶା
ତେଣେ ତେଲ ଘଡିକି ଆଶା।
variants.locator: Hello Odia line184; uploaded compilation page5.
variants.note: Related alternate expression selected editorially for the same son-care versus resource-retention image. Upload has ଘଡିକି; public witness has ଘଡ଼ିକି. No established textual descent. Literal reading: On this side, concern for the son’s head; on that side, concern for the oil pot. ଅର୍ଥ: ପୁଅର ମୁଣ୍ଡରେ ତେଲ ଲାଗୁ ବୋଲି ଇଚ୍ଛା, ଆଉ ତେଲ ଘଡିରୁ ତେଲ ନସରୁ ବୋଲି ବି ଇଚ୍ଛା। ଯତ୍ନ ଓ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ବଞ୍ଚାଇବାର ଏହି ଦୁଇ ଟାଣ ଏକାଠି ହୋଇଛି। Explanation: The same person values care for the son and preserving the oil supply. Oiling the head uses up oil: the two attachments pull in opposite directions. This is an editorial reading of the paired concrete objects, not an independently located gloss of this exact form. Locator: Hello Odia line184; uploaded compilation page5.

entries.english_summary: Wanting the care provided while refusing the expense it takes.

entries.title: When familiarity wears away respect
entries.odia: ଅତି ପରିଚୟେ ଗୌରବ ନଷ୍ଟ।
entries.literal_meaning: Too much familiarity destroys respect.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅତି ପରିଚୟରେ ଲୋକେ ପରସ୍ପରକୁ ହେୟ ମନେ କରିବା ବା ଯଥୋଚିତ ସମ୍ମାନ ଦେବା ଭୁଲିଯିବାର ଆଶଙ୍କା ରହେ—କଥାଟି ସେହି ବିଷୟରେ ସତର୍କ କରେ।
entries.explanation: Knowing someone very well can turn into taking that person for granted. The saying warns about the point where ease becomes disregard. The inspected Odia Vasa gloss likewise connects excessive familiarity with loss of respect.
entries.usage_example: Friends begin interrupting and dismissing one another because they assume no courtesy is needed between them. One might recall this saying to ask for more consideration. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: The compact line makes its warning through the contrast between ପରିଚୟ, familiarity, and ଗୌରବ, dignity or regard. This edition reads it as a reminder to preserve respect within closeness; no particular social rank or household practice is specified.

witnesses.locator: Inspected list lines 89 and 106, beginning ଅତି ପରିଚୟେ.
witnesses.note: Matches the words visible in uploaded PDF page 2. Upload supplies display spelling and punctuation. Shared textual lineage remains possible.

witnesses.locator: Numbered item 36, inspected page line 67.
witnesses.note: Attests the same wording and a short gloss relating excessive closeness to diminished respect. Does not establish earliest origin.

entries.english_summary: Closeness can erode respect when people begin taking one another for granted.

entries.title: A spouse’s teasing complaint
entries.odia:
ଅତି ସୁନ୍ଦରୀ ଲୋ ଚହଟ ଗୋରୀ
ଆଗେ ତୋତେ ହେଲି ବିଭା
ଏବେ ଯହୁଁ ଧନ ବୟସ ସରିଲା
ଦାଣ୍ଡେ ବସାଉଛୁ ସଭା।
entries.literal_meaning: O very beautiful, radiantly fair woman, I married you in earlier days. Now, dear, when youth has passed, you hold gatherings out in the street.
entries.meaning_odia: ପତ୍ନୀର ପୂର୍ବ ରୂପକୁ ମନେ ପକାଇ ସ୍ୱାମୀ ଏବେ ସେ ଦାଣ୍ଡରେ ସଭା ବସାଉଥିବା ନେଇ ଆକ୍ଷେପ କରୁଛି। ଏହାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ସେହି କଥକର ଦାମ୍ପତ୍ୟ ଥଟ୍ଟା ବା ଅଭିଯୋଗ ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: A spouse recalls marrying the woman he describes as beautiful and fair, then complains that she now gathers people in the street. The change from praise to reproach gives the verse its teasing edge. This is an editorial reading of the speaker’s complaint; the lines do not tell us what those gatherings discuss.
entries.usage_example: In discussing a fictional couple’s dialogue, these lines could illustrate how an affectionate address can carry a complaint about changes over time. This is a newly composed reading example, not a documented customary use.
entries.cultural_context: The speaker links his wife’s appearance and age with his judgment of her public sociability. The complexion praise and gendered reproach belong to that source voice. They are not this edition’s standards for women’s worth or conduct. ଧନ is read as an address meaning dear; the verse itself supplies no punctuation to resolve that reading independently.

witnesses.locator: Inspected page lines 95 and 112, four-line saying beginning ଅତି ସୁନ୍ଦରୀ.
witnesses.note: Public text has ଚହଟି, while uploaded PDF page 2 has ଚହଟ. Display preserves uploaded reading and its four lines. Other wording corresponds; shared textual lineage is possible, not independent historical verification.

entries.odia_summary: ପୂର୍ବର ରୂପପ୍ରଶଂସାରୁ ଏବେର ଦାଣ୍ଡସଭାକୁ ନେଇ ଦାମ୍ପତ୍ୟ ଆକ୍ଷେପ।
entries.english_summary: Remembered praise turns into a spouse’s complaint about changed habits.
entries.narrative_credit: Translation and interpretation by Project Odisha, informed by the wording witness below.

entries.title: Hardship tests conduct
entries.odia: ଅଭାବରୁ ସ୍ୱଭାବ ନଷ୍ଟ।
entries.literal_meaning: Want ruins one’s disposition.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭାବର ଚାପରେ ମଣିଷର ସ୍ୱଭାବ ବା ଆଚରଣ ବିଗିଡ଼ିପାରେ ବୋଲି କଥାଟି କହେ। ଏହାକୁ ଏଠାରେ କଷ୍ଟର ପ୍ରଭାବ ନେଇ ଏକ ସତର୍କବାଣୀ ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି, ଗରିବ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଚରିତ୍ର ବିଷୟରେ ସାଧାରଣ ରାୟ ଭାବେ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The saying makes a stark link between deprivation and damaged conduct. This edition reads it as a warning that sustained hardship can strain patience and judgment. That interpretation concerns the pressure of circumstances; the proverb is not evidence that people with little money have worse character.
entries.usage_example: In a story, someone who is usually patient begins speaking harshly under mounting shortages and worry. A reader might recall this saying when discussing that change. This is a newly composed illustration.
entries.cultural_context: The sound echo between ଅଭାବ, want or lack, and ସ୍ୱଭାବ, disposition or habitual nature, gives the short line its force. Its categorical wording is preserved as the saying’s claim, while the commentary distinguishes that claim from a universal judgment about poverty.

witnesses.locator: Inspected public page line 122, ଅଭାବରୁ ସ୍ବଭାବ ନଷ୍ଟ.

This is an orthographic transcription difference, not a different proverb. Shared source lineage is possible.

entries.odia_summary: ଅଭାବର ଚାପ ଆଚରଣକୁ ପ୍ରଭାବିତ କରିପାରେ ବୋଲି କଥାଟିର ସତର୍କବାଣୀ।
entries.english_summary: The proverb warns of the strain that deprivation can place on conduct.

entries.title: Enjoy what you have earned
entries.odia: ଅରଜି ଥିଲେ ଗରଜି ଖା।
entries.literal_meaning: If you have earned it, eat boldly.
entries.meaning_odia: ନିଜେ ଅର୍ଜନ କରିଥିଲେ ତାହାକୁ ସଂକୋଚ ନକରି ଭୋଗ କରିବାର ସାହସ ଥାଏ—କଥାଟିକୁ ଏଠାରେ ନିଜ ରୋଜଗାରରୁ ଆସୁଥିବା ଆତ୍ମବିଶ୍ୱାସ ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: Earning comes first; confident enjoyment follows. ଗରଜି brings the force of a roar into the invitation to eat, giving it a bold, assertive tone. This edition reads it as confidence in enjoying one’s own earnings, rather than a literal instruction to make noise at a meal.
entries.usage_example: After being paid for work, someone hesitates to buy a modest treat. A friend might recall this saying to encourage them to enjoy what they have earned. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: ଅରଜି and ଗରଜି make a close sound pair, linking earning with assertiveness. Eating gives the general idea of enjoying resources a concrete image. The line does not specify a profession, income level or particular meal.

entries.title: One earns, eighty eat
entries.odia:
ଅରଜେ ଜଣେ ଖାଆନ୍ତି ପଣେ
ତା’ ଘରଟି ଡୁବଇ ଦିନେ।
entries.literal_meaning: One person earns and eighty eat; that household will sink one day.
entries.meaning_odia: ଜଣକର ରୋଜଗାର ଉପରେ ଅତ୍ୟଧିକ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚର ଭାର ପଡ଼ିଲେ ଘରର ଆର୍ଥିକ ଅବସ୍ଥା ଭାଙ୍ଗିପଡ଼ିପାରେ। ଜଣେ ଓ ପଣେର ତୁଳନାରେ ସେହି ଅସମତୁଳନକୁ ବଡ଼ କରି ଦେଖାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The verse sets one earner against eighty eaters, then pictures the household sinking under the imbalance. This edition reads the large number as an emphatic contrast between income and the demands placed on it. The warning concerns an unsustainable burden, not a rule that every household member must earn money.
entries.usage_example: A household keeps increasing its spending while relying on one unchanged income. During a budget discussion, someone might recall this saying to show why the arrangement cannot continue. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: ପଣ is a counting unit of eighty; here ପଣେ contrasts with ଜଣେ, one person. The sound pairing reinforces the numerical mismatch. The sinking house is a figurative image of ruin, not a literal flood prediction or an exact household-size threshold.

entries.title: Will bamboo ever smell of sandalwood?
entries.odia:
ଆଉ କି ସେଦିନ ଆସିବ
ବାଉଁସ ଗଛରେ ମଳୟ ଲାଗିଲେ
ଚନ୍ଦନ ପରାଏ ବାସିବ।
entries.literal_meaning: Will that day ever come, when the Malaya breeze touches the bamboo and it smells like sandalwood?
entries.meaning_odia: ମଳୟ ପବନ ଲାଗିଲେ ବାଉଁଶ ଚନ୍ଦନ ପରି ବାସିବ କି—ଏହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ବାହାରର ପ୍ରଭାବରୁ ଅସାଧାରଣ ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତନ ଆସିବାର ଆଶାକୁ ନେଇ ସନ୍ଦେହ ପ୍ରକାଶ ପାଇଛି ବୋଲି ଏଠାରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The imagined breeze promises a fragrance that belongs to sandalwood, while the plant remains bamboo. This edition reads the opening question as doubt that a hoped-for change will arrive merely through a favourable influence. The verse leaves the question hanging; it does not supply a named person or event.
entries.usage_example: Someone expects a new setting alone to transform a habit they have made no effort to change. A reader might recall this question about bamboo and sandalwood. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: ମଳୟ is read as the Malaya or southern spring breeze. Here breeze and sandalwood fragrance form a poetic image of influence and transformation. The verse is not presented as a botanical claim that wind changes one plant into another, or as proof that people cannot change.

entries.title: When the teeth are gone
entries.odia:
ଆଖୁ, କାକୁଡ଼ି, ନଡ଼ିଆ , ମକା
ଦାନ୍ତ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ତଳକୁ ପକା।
entries.literal_meaning: Sugarcane, cucumber, coconut, maize—when your teeth fall out, put them down.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦାନ୍ତ ନଥିଲେ ଆଗରୁ ଚୋବାଇ ଖାଉଥିବା ଜିନିଷକୁ ଛାଡ଼ିବାକୁ ପଡ଼େ—ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟ ବଦଳିଲେ ଅଭ୍ୟାସ ବଦଳାଇବାର କଥାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The four foods lead into a blunt instruction: once the teeth are gone, put the food down. This edition reads the scene as a reminder that changed abilities can require changed habits. The warning stays concrete, with the mouth’s ability to chew setting the limit.
entries.usage_example: In a story about growing older, a character recalls these lines while admitting that an old habit has become difficult. This is a newly composed reading example, not recorded traditional usage.
entries.cultural_context: The rhyme of ମକା and ପକା links the food list to its closing instruction. The verse does not discuss how foods are prepared or adapted. It is recorded here as a proverbial image of changed capacity, not dietary or dental advice.

entries.title: Affection that lasts only in your presence
entries.odia:
ଆଗରେ ଥିଲେ ମୋର ମୋର
ପିଠି କଲେ କିଏ କା’ହାର ?
entries.literal_meaning: While you are in front of them, it is “mine, mine”; turn your back, and who belongs to whom?
entries.meaning_odia: ସାମ୍ନାରେ ଥିଲେ ଆପଣାର ବୋଲି ଦାବି କରିବା, କିନ୍ତୁ ଦୂରେଇଗଲେ ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଭୁଲିଯିବା—ଏହି ଅସ୍ଥାୟୀ ଆପଣାପଣକୁ କଥାଟି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ।
entries.explanation: The repeated “mine” sounds warmly possessive while the person is present. Turning away is followed by a question that makes the relationship disappear. This edition reads the contrast as a criticism of affection that is displayed face to face but does not endure in someone’s absence.
entries.usage_example: Someone is warmly claimed as a close friend during visits, but receives no acknowledgment or concern after leaving. These lines could describe that contrast. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: The verse uses physical orientation—being in front of someone and turning one’s back—to mark presence and absence. Its final question challenges the earlier claim of closeness. It does not identify a particular kinship, event or reason for the change.

entries.title: Praising one’s own cooking
entries.odia:
ଆପେ ରାନ୍ଧି ଆପେ ଖାଏ
ସୁଆଦ ସୁଆଦ ବୋଲୁଥାଏ ।
entries.literal_meaning: They cook it themselves, eat it themselves, and keep saying, “Tasty, tasty.”
entries.meaning_odia: ନିଜେ ତିଆରି କରିଥିବା ଜିନିଷକୁ ନିଜେ ବାରମ୍ବାର ପ୍ରଶଂସା କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର। ଏହାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ନିଜ କାମର ନିଜେ ପ୍ରଶଂସକ ହେବା ଉପରେ ଥଟ୍ଟା ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: Cook, eater and enthusiastic reviewer are all the same person. The repeated praise makes the scene comic. This edition reads it as a teasing picture of self-praise, where the maker supplies the applause as well as the work.
entries.usage_example: Someone presents their own design and repeatedly announces how excellent it is before anyone else responds. A listener might recall this cooking scene. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: The repeated ଆପେ stresses doing both parts oneself; repeated ସୁଆଦ supplies the approving refrain. Enjoying one’s own food is the literal scene, while self-congratulation is the editorial figurative reading. No particular dish or cooking tradition is specified.

entries.title: A tearful request for new bangles
entries.odia:
ଆମ୍ବ ଗଛର ଶିଅ
ବୁଢା ଆଗେ ବୁଢୀ ସକେଇ କାନ୍ଦେ
ଖଡୁ ବଦଳେଇ ଦିଅ।
entries.literal_meaning: The root of a mango tree; an old woman sobs before an old man: “Change my bangles for me.”
entries.meaning_odia: ବୁଢ଼ା ଆଗରେ ବୁଢ଼ୀ ସକେଇ କାନ୍ଦି ଖଡ଼ୁ ବଦଳାଇ ଦେବାକୁ କହୁଛି। ବୟସ ବଢ଼ିଲେ ବି ଅଳଙ୍କାର ବଦଳାଇବାର ଇଚ୍ଛା ରହିବାକୁ ନେଇ ଏକ ଥଟ୍ଟାର ଦୃଶ୍ୟ ଭାବେ ଏହାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The main scene is a tearful request to exchange bangles. Calling both figures old brings age into the joke, while the request shows the woman’s continuing interest in an ornament. This is an editorial reading of the scene, not a judgment that such a wish is improper in later life.
entries.usage_example: When discussing a comic verse about an older character asking for a new ornament, a reader might compare this scene and its exaggerated pleading. This is a newly composed reading example.
entries.cultural_context: ଶିଅ is read as root, and ଖଡୁ as a bangle or bracelet. The mango-root opening rhymes with the closing ଦିଅ; no further symbolic connection is established here. The text does not specify the bangles’ material, a marriage rite, or why they need changing.

entries.title: Trust answered with deception
entries.odia:
ଆଶା କରିଥିଲି ତୋତେ
କାଉକୁ ଯେମନ୍ତ କୋଇଲି ଭଣ୍ଡାଏ
ସେହିପରି କର ମୋତେ।
entries.literal_meaning: I had placed my hopes in you. As the koel deceives the crow, so you treat me.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯାହା ଉପରେ ଆଶା ରଖାଯାଇଥିଲା, ସେହି ଲୋକ ଭଣ୍ଡାଉଛି ବୋଲି କଥକର ଅଭିଯୋଗ। କାଉକୁ କୋଇଲି ଭଣ୍ଡାଇବାର ତୁଳନାରେ ସେ ନିଜ ହତାଶା ପ୍ରକାଶ କରୁଛି।
entries.explanation: The first line declares trust; the next two answer it with an accusation of deception. The speaker casts themself as the crow and the trusted person as the koel. This edition reads the verse as a complaint that reliance on someone has been repaid with trickery.
entries.usage_example: A person relies on a promised favour and later discovers that the promise was only a way to mislead them. These lines could voice their disappointment. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: The comparison gives the crow the speaker’s place and the koel the trusted person’s place. Its force comes from being deceived by someone on whom the speaker had relied.

entries.title: Water finds the low bank
entries.odia:
ଉଣା ହିଡ ଯେଉଁଠି
ପାଣି ଗଡ଼େ ସେଇଠି।
entries.literal_meaning: Where the embankment is low, that is where the water flows.
entries.meaning_odia: ହିଡ଼ର ନିମ୍ନ ଅଂଶ ଦେଇ ପାଣି ବାହାରିଯାଏ। ସେହି ଚିତ୍ରରୁ ଦୁର୍ବଳ ଜାଗାରେ ଚାପ ପଡ଼ିବା ବା ସେହି ବାଟେ କ୍ଷତି ଘଟିବାର କଥାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: An embankment may hold water along most of its length, but a lower section gives the water a way through. This edition reads the image as a reminder that pressure finds a weak point. A small vulnerable part can determine what happens to the whole arrangement.
entries.usage_example: A group prepares carefully for an event but leaves one essential task without an owner. When that gap disrupts the work, someone might recall the water finding a low bank. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: ହିଡ is the raised earthen boundary or bank that holds back water. The verse focuses on a difference in height: the lower part becomes the outlet. Pairing ଯେଉଁଠି with ସେଇଠି makes the connection between vulnerable place and flowing water immediate.

entries.title: An elephant on credit
entries.odia:
ଉଧାର ମିଳିଲେ କିଣନ୍ତି ହାତୀ
ଶୁଝିଲେ ଶୁଝିବ ପୁଅର ନାତି।
entries.literal_meaning: When credit is available, they buy an elephant; if it is repaid, the son’s grandson will repay it.
entries.meaning_odia: ଉଧାର ମିଳୁଛି ବୋଲି ବଡ଼ କିଣାକିଣି କରିବା, ଆଉ ଶୁଝିବାର ଭାରକୁ ଦୂର ଭବିଷ୍ୟତର ବଂଶଧରଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଛାଡ଼ିଦେବା—ଏହି ବେପରୁଆ ମନୋଭାବକୁ କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରେ।
entries.explanation: An elephant makes the purchase extravagantly large; the son’s grandson pushes repayment far into the future. Together they expose the borrower’s indifference to the burden created by easy credit. This edition reads the verse as a satire on enjoying a purchase now while leaving its cost to others later.
entries.usage_example: Someone proposes an extravagant purchase on borrowed money and dismisses repayment as a problem for future family members. Another person might recall the elephant in this saying. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: The image joins scale and distance: a large animal bought immediately, followed by a descendant several generations away who is expected to pay. The conditional ଶୁଝିଲେ adds to the careless tone—repayment itself sounds uncertain.

variants.odia:
ବାପ ଖାଇଛନ୍ତି ତାଳ
ପୁଅଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ତା କାଳ।
variants.locator: Page31, second item beginning ବାପ ଖାଇଛନ୍ତି ତାଳ.
variants.note: Related-family wording grouped editorially with POD-DHAGA-376: consumption by a parent is paired with consequences for descendants. No textual descent asserted. Literal reading: Father has eaten palmyra fruit; for the sons, that is doom. Odia meaning: ତାଳ ଖାଇଛନ୍ତି ବାପ, କିନ୍ତୁ ତାହା ପୁଅଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ କାଳ ହୋଇଛି—ଏହା ପଙ୍କ୍ତିର ବିପରୀତ ଚିତ୍ର। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ, ଜଣଙ୍କ କାମର କୁପରିଣାମ ପର ପିଢ଼ିକୁ ଭୋଗିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବାର କଥା ଏଠାରେ ଆସେ। ତାଳ ଖାଇବାରୁ କାହିଁକି ଏପରି ହେଲା, ପଙ୍କ୍ତି ତାହା କହୁନାହିଁ। Interpretive reading: The person who eats and the people who face doom are different generations. Read editorially, the couplet pictures consequences passing from a parent’s action to the children. Its compressed contrast leaves the connection unexplained; it does not establish that the sons share responsibility for the father’s action. Uploaded page31 inspected17November2026; exact wording retained. The fruit-to-doom connection is unexplained; no debt or intentional evasion inferred. entries.title: Watering above, cutting the roots below
entries.odia:
ଉପରେ ଉପରେ ପାଣି ଛିଞ୍ଚୁଚି
ଭିତରେ ଭିତରେ ଶିଅ କାଟୁଛି।
entries.literal_meaning: On the surface, they sprinkle water; underneath, they cut the roots.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାହାରେ ଉପକାର କରୁଥିବା ପରି ଦେଖାଇ ଗୋପନରେ କ୍ଷତି କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର। ପାଣି ଛିଞ୍ଚିବାର ଯତ୍ନ ଓ ଶିଅ କାଟିବାର ଧ୍ୱଂସ ଏକାସାଙ୍ଗେ ରହିଛି।
entries.explanation: Watering suggests care, but cutting the roots destroys what that care appears to support. The paired actions make the deception visible: a helpful performance conceals damage to the foundation. This edition reads the verse as a warning about outward assistance joined to hidden sabotage.
entries.usage_example: Someone publicly supports a colleague’s work while secretly removing the resources needed to complete it. Another colleague might recall this image. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: The repeated ଉପରେ ଉପରେ and ଭିତରେ ଭିତରେ divide the scene into what is seen and what is concealed. ଶିଅ means root: the damage occurs at the part that sustains the plant, beneath the visible act of watering.

entries.title: Such a helpful friend
entries.odia:
ଉପକାରିଆ ବନ୍ଧୁ
ଆମ୍ବ ଆଣି ନାହିଁ, ଶିମ୍ବ ଆଣିନାହିଁ
ଆଣିଚି କଷା କେନ୍ଦୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: A helpful friend: they brought no mangoes, brought no beans; they brought astringent kendu fruit.
entries.meaning_odia: ବନ୍ଧୁକୁ ଉପକାରିଆ ବୋଲି କୁହାଯାଇଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ସେ ଆମ୍ବ ବା ଶିମ୍ବ ବଦଳରେ କଷା କେନ୍ଦୁ ଆଣିଛି। ଆଶା ମୁତାବକ ଉପକାର ନମିଳିବାରୁ ପ୍ରଶଂସାଟି ଏଠାରେ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ ହୋଇଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The opening calls the friend helpful, then the gift undercuts the praise. Mangoes and beans are named as the things not brought; the final line leaves the speaker with astringent kendu instead. This edition reads the mismatch as irony about a favour that disappoints its recipient.
entries.usage_example: A friend offers to bring something useful for a shared meal, but arrives with something the group cannot use as hoped. Someone might recall these lines with a teasing “such a helpful friend.” This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: The three foods give the complaint a concrete shape. କଷା specifies the astringent, mouth-puckering taste of the offered fruit, sharpening the contrast with the opening praise. The humour lies in the disappointed speaker’s evaluation of this gift.

entries.title: All that fuss for this?
entries.odia:
ଏଇ କଥାକୁ ,
ନାଆ ପେଲିଦେଲି କଲିକତାକୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: For this matter, I pushed the boat off to Calcutta.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏତିକି କଥା ପାଇଁ ଏତେ ଆୟୋଜନ ବା ଚିନ୍ତା କାହିଁକି—ଏହି ଥଟ୍ଟାର ସ୍ୱରରେ କଥାଟିକୁ ଏଠାରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଛୋଟ କଥା ସହ କଲିକତାକୁ ନାଆ ପଠାଇବାର ବଡ଼ ଚିତ୍ର ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: A small-sounding “this matter” is met with the grand gesture of sending a boat to Calcutta. This edition reads the mismatch as a playful response to needless fuss: was such a large undertaking really needed for that?
entries.usage_example: Someone gives a long, anxious account of a problem that turns out to have a simple solution. A friend might respond with this rhyme before explaining the fix. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: The destination କଲିକତା gives the imagined journey a concrete endpoint. The repeated କୁ ending in କଥାକୁ and କଲିକତାକୁ turns the response into a quick rhyme, with the boat journey supplying the comic exaggeration.

entries.title: Look for corroboration
entries.odia:
ଏକା ଆଖି ଆଖି ନୁହଁ
ଏକା ସାକ୍ଷୀ ସାକ୍ଷୀ ନୁହଁ।
entries.literal_meaning: A single eye is no eye; a single witness is no witness.
entries.meaning_odia: ଜଣକର କଥା ଶୁଣି ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ନେବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଅନ୍ୟ ସମର୍ଥନ ବା ପ୍ରମାଣ ଖୋଜିବାର ସତର୍କତା ଭାବେ କଥାଟିକୁ ଏଠାରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଆଖି ଓ ସାକ୍ଷୀର ତୁଳନାଟି ଏହି ପ୍ରବଚନର ଜୋରଦାର କଥନ।
entries.explanation: The two lines repeat the same pattern: one alone is declared insufficient. This edition reads the witness comparison as a call to seek corroboration before settling a disputed account. Its emphatic wording belongs to the proverb; it is neither a rule of law nor a factual assessment of people who see with one eye.
entries.usage_example: Two friends hear one account of a disagreement and decide to ask what else happened before taking sides. One might recall this saying as a reminder to check the account. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: ଏକା begins each line, and the repeated noun is followed by ନୁହଁ, creating a parallel denial. The verse moves from an image of seeing to the act of bearing witness, making corroboration its central concern in this reading.

entries.title: Two contrary claims from one mouth
entries.odia: ଏକାତୁଣ୍ଡରେ ଉଆ ଉଷୁନା।
entries.literal_meaning: Raw rice and parboiled rice in the same mouth.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏକେ ଲୋକ ଥରେ ଗୋଟିଏ କଥା କହି ପରେ ତାହାର ବିପରୀତ କଥା କହିବା। ଏକା ତୁଣ୍ଡରୁ ଉଆ ଓ ଉଷୁନା ଦୁଇପ୍ରକାର କଥା ବାହାରିବାର ତୁଳନାରେ ଏହି ଅସଙ୍ଗତି ଧରାପଡ଼ିଛି।
entries.explanation: The same mouth offers two contrasting descriptions, “raw” and “parboiled.” The inspected Odia Vasa gloss applies the saying to someone who gives one opinion and later its opposite. The rice contrast makes that inconsistency compact and memorable.
entries.usage_example: Someone first insists that a plan is workable, then denies ever considering it workable. A listener might use this saying to point out the contradiction. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: ଉଆ is read as ଅରୁଆ, rice not parboiled, in contrast with ଉଷୁନା, parboiled rice. ତୁଣ୍ଡ makes the mouth the common source of both descriptions. The familiar distinction between rice preparations becomes an image for incompatible statements.

entries.title: One person who outweighs many
entries.odia: ଏକା ମାଧିଆ ବାଇଶି ପଳ।
entries.literal_meaning: Madhia alone is twenty-two palas in weight.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅର୍ଥ, ବିଦ୍ୟା ବା ବୁଦ୍ଧିରେ ଜଣେ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ଅନେକଙ୍କୁ ଟପିଯିବାର କଥା। ଏକା ମାଧିଆର ବାଇଶି ପଳ ଓଜନ ଚିତ୍ରରେ ସେହି ଅଧିକ ପ୍ରଭାବ ବା ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟ ପ୍ରକାଶ ପାଏ।
entries.explanation: A single figure carries unusually great weight in the comparison. The inspected Odia Vasa gloss applies the line to someone who surpasses many others in wealth, learning or intelligence. The weight is therefore read as an image of exceptional capacity or influence.
entries.usage_example: One experienced member solves a problem that has held up a whole group. Someone might use this saying to acknowledge that person’s exceptional contribution. This illustration is newly composed.
entries.cultural_context: The contrast between ଏକା, alone, and ବାଇଶି, twenty-two, gives the line its force. ପଳ is a traditional weight unit; the verse turns weight into a measure of a person’s standing. ମାଧିଆ is retained as Madhia, the figure named in the saying.
