entries.title: Even a straw recovered is something
entries.odia: ଘର ପୋଡିରୁ କୁଟାଖିଏ ପାଇଲେ ସହି।
entries.literal_meaning: Even a piece of straw obtained from a house fire is worth accepting.
entries.meaning_odia: ସବୁକିଛି ନଷ୍ଟ ହେବା ବେଳେ କୁଟାଖିଏ ପରି ଅତି ସାମାନ୍ୟ ଜିନିଷ ମିଳିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହା ଗ୍ରହଣଯୋଗ୍ୟ। ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଅନୁସାରେ ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ହାନି ଅପେକ୍ଷା ଅଳ୍ପ କିଛି ଫେରିପାଇବା ଶ୍ରେୟସ୍କର।
entries.explanation: A straw is small beside the loss of a house, yet it is still something recovered. The inspected gloss makes the comparison explicit: when everything is being lost, even a small recovery is preferable. The saying gives a modest remnant value without pretending it replaces what has gone.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Most of a damaged collection cannot be restored, but a few readable pages survive. Someone quotes the saying to express why preserving those remnants still matters.
entries.cultural_context: The verse contrasts the scale of a whole house with କୁଟାଖିଏ, a single small piece of straw. ସହି accepts that tiny remainder. The image shifts attention from the inadequacy of what survives to the difference between a little and nothing.

entries.title: Digging a well while the house burns
entries.odia: ଘର ପୋଡି ବେଳେ କୂଅ ଖୋଳା।
entries.literal_meaning: Digging a well when the house is burning.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘର ପୋଡ଼ିବା ବେଳେ ନିଆଁ ଲିଭାଇବାକୁ ପାଣି ଦରକାର, ଅଥଚ ସେତେବେଳେ କୂଅ ଖୋଳା ଆରମ୍ଭ ହେଉଛି। ଦରକାର ପଡ଼ିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ କରିବାକୁ ଥିବା ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତିକୁ ସଙ୍କଟ ଆସିବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ପକାଇରଖିବା ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଉପହାସର ବିଷୟ।
entries.explanation: The emergency needs water now, but the work of making a water source is only beginning. Read editorially, the saying mocks preparation delayed until the crisis it should have anticipated. The inspected public gloss calls the situation laughable.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: An event is about to begin when the organisers discover that they have never arranged the essential equipment. As they start searching for it, someone compares their timing to digging a well while the house burns.
entries.cultural_context: The house fire and the unfinished well compress two different timescales into one scene: an urgent need and work that must precede it. The humour lies in treating the moment of need as the moment to begin preparing.

entries.title: Satisfaction gives way to alarm
entries.odia:
ଘର ବର ଦେଖି ପେଟ ପୂରୁଚି
ସଉତୁଣୀ ଦେଖି ହଂସା ଉଡୁଚି।
entries.literal_meaning: Seeing the house and bridegroom, my belly fills; seeing the co-wife, my spirit flies away.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘର ଓ ବରକୁ ଦେଖି ସନ୍ତୋଷ ହେଉଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ସଉତୁଣୀକୁ ଦେଖି ଭୟ ଲାଗୁଛି। ଏଠାରେ ଆନନ୍ଦ ଦେଉଥିବା ଦିଗ ସହିତ ଚିନ୍ତା ଜନ୍ମାଉଥିବା ଅନ୍ୟ ଦିଗଟି ମଧ୍ୟ ରହିଛି। ଏହା କଥକଙ୍କ ମିଶ୍ର ଅନୁଭବର ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠ।
entries.explanation: The first sight brings satisfaction; the second unsettles it. Read editorially, the couplet captures an attractive situation whose troubling side prevents uncomplicated happiness. The fear belongs to the speaker in this domestic image.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A new opportunity offers welcome comforts, but one condition makes the person considering it deeply uneasy. A reader uses the couplet to describe that mixture of attraction and apprehension.
entries.cultural_context: The paired bodily expressions carry the contrast: a full belly suggests contentment, while a spirit taking flight expresses alarm. ସଉତୁଣୀ names a woman sharing the same husband. Her appearance changes the speaker’s response within this verse.

entries.title: No lemon or salt at home, but show outside
entries.odia:
ଘରେ ନଥାଇ ଲେମ୍ବୁ ଲୁଣ
ବାହାରେ ଦେଖ ଚାତର ପଣ।
entries.literal_meaning: No lemon or salt at home—look at the show outside.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘରେ ଲେମ୍ବୁ ଲୁଣ ପରି ସାମାନ୍ୟ ଜିନିଷ ନାହିଁ, ଅଥଚ ବାହାରେ ବଡ଼ ଆଡ଼ମ୍ବର। ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଅନୁସାରେ କଥାଟି ବୃଥା ବାହ୍ୟ ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନକୁ ଉପହାସ କରେ। ଘରର ବାସ୍ତବ ଅବସ୍ଥା ଓ ବାହାରେ ଦେଖାଯାଉଥିବା ଠାଣିର ଫରକ ଏହାର ମୂଳ କଥା।
entries.explanation: The household lacks even the small provisions named in the first line, while its public face puts on a show. The inspected gloss identifies empty outward ostentation. The target is the mismatch between provision and display, rather than a person’s lack of resources.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A club spends its effort on a grand public display while leaving the basic supplies for its work unprovided. A member uses the saying to question those priorities.
entries.cultural_context: ଘରେ and ବାହାରେ set private provision against public appearance. Lemon and salt supply a concrete, modest measure of what is missing; ଚାତର ପଣ names the display that makes the contrast conspicuous.

entries.title: A palm-leaf screen and a key at the waist
entries.odia: ଘରେ ବରଡା ତାଟି ଅଣ୍ଟାରେ ଚାବିକାଠି।
entries.literal_meaning: A palm-leaf screen at home, a key at the waist.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘରେ ବରଡାର ତାଟି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଅଣ୍ଟାରେ ଚାବିକାଠି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ସାମାନ୍ୟ ଘରର ଚିତ୍ର ସହ ଚାବି ଧରିବାର ଠାଣିକୁ ମିଳାଇ ବାସ୍ତବ ଅବସ୍ଥାଠାରୁ ବଡ଼ ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନକୁ ଟାହି କରାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The verse sets the simple leaf screen against a key carried at the waist. Read editorially, the key becomes a conspicuous sign of having things to secure, while the screen exposes the modest setting. The joke concerns the discrepancy between the display and the circumstances.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A small informal club adopts elaborate signs of office before attending to its basic needs. A reader invokes the saying to question the display. This is an editorial analogy, not a collected use.
entries.cultural_context: The two objects do the work: the frond screen belongs to the dwelling, while the key is carried on the person. Their juxtaposition makes the key stand out as a symbol of possession and control in this editorial reading.

entries.title: The wound goes, the mark remains
entries.odia:
ଘା ଯାଏ, ଦାଗ ଥାଏ
ଲୋକ ଯାଏ, କଥା ଥାଏ।
entries.literal_meaning: The wound goes, the scar remains; people go, words remain.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘା ଭଲ ହୋଇଗଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହାର ଦାଗ ରହେ। ସେହିପରି ଲୋକ ଚାଲିଗଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ କଥା ରହିଯାଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଏହା ମଣିଷର ଉପସ୍ଥିତି ଶେଷ ହେଲା ପରେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାଙ୍କ କଥା ବା ତାଙ୍କୁ ନେଇ କଥା ମନରେ ଓ ଆଲୋଚନାରେ ରହିବାର ଚିତ୍ର।
entries.explanation: Each line separates something passing from something that lasts. A scar remains after a wound has gone; words or talk remain after a person has left. The editorial reading extends the bodily image to the persistence of speech and remembrance.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Long after a visitor leaves, the people who met them keep returning to a memorable remark. Someone recalls the second line to describe how the conversation has outlasted the visit.
entries.cultural_context: The repeated ଯାଏ and ଥାଏ give the couplet its parallel structure: departure set against persistence. ଦାଗ makes the first remainder visible; କଥା gives the second a life in memory and conversation.

entries.title: A dream kept within
entries.odia:
ଘୁଙ୍ଗା ଯାହା ସପନ ଦେଖେ
ମନ କଥା ମନରେ ରଖେ।
entries.literal_meaning: Whatever a person unable to speak dreams, they keep the thoughts within their mind.
entries.meaning_odia: କଥା କହିପାରୁନଥିବା ଜଣେ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ସପନରେ ଯାହା ଦେଖନ୍ତି, ତାହା ମନରେ ରଖନ୍ତି—ଏହା ପଦ୍ୟର ଚିତ୍ର। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ମନରେ ଥିବା ଅନୁଭବ କଥାରେ ପ୍ରକାଶ ନହୋଇ ନିଜ ଭିତରେ ରହିଯିବା ଏହାର ଭାବ।
entries.explanation: The dream is experienced inwardly and remains unspoken in the scene the proverb presents. Our editorial reading focuses on that gap between having an experience and putting it into words. The image gives form to a thought or feeling that stays with its bearer.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A vivid experience matters deeply to someone, but they find no words for it in conversation. A reader recalls the couplet as an image of what remains unspoken.
entries.cultural_context: ସପନ supplies an inward event that others cannot directly see. The repeated ମନ holds the second line inside that same private space. The verse’s use of ଘୁଙ୍ଗା belongs to its figurative scene; the commentary concerns unspoken experience.

entries.title: The golden cage and the remembered hollow
entries.odia:
ଘୁଷୁରି କି କାହିଁ ପାଚିଲା କଦଳୀ
ଅନ୍ଧହାତେ ରତ୍ନ ମୁଦି
ପେଚା ଚଢ଼େଇ କି ସୁବର୍ଣ୍ଣ ପଞ୍ଜୁରି
କୋରଡ ସୁମରି କାନ୍ଦି।
entries.literal_meaning: Why a ripe banana for a pig? A jewel-set ring in a blind person’s hand; a golden cage for an owl—it cries, remembering its tree hollow.
entries.meaning_odia: ପାଚିଲା କଦଳୀ, ରତ୍ନ ମୁଦି ଓ ସୁବର୍ଣ୍ଣ ପଞ୍ଜୁରିକୁ ବକ୍ତା ଏପରି ଉପହାର ଭାବେ ରଖିଛନ୍ତି ଯାହାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଗ୍ରହୀତାଙ୍କ ପାଖରେ ମେଳ ଖାଉନାହିଁ। ଶେଷରେ ପେଚା କୋରଡକୁ ମନେପକାଇ କାନ୍ଦୁଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଦାମୀ ଜିନିଷ ଦେଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଆଦର ବା ସନ୍ତୋଷ ନମିଳିବା ଏହାର ଭାବ। ଅନ୍ଧ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ ଉପମାଟି ବକ୍ତାଙ୍କ ପକ୍ଷପାତପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଚିତ୍ର, ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The speaker links three offerings presented as valuable but misplaced: ripe fruit, a jewelled ring and a golden cage. The last image develops the contrast by giving the owl something it still longs for, its tree hollow. Read editorially, outward value does not guarantee appreciation or contentment. The comparison involving blindness expresses the source’s prejudice, not a limit on what blind people can value.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone receives an expensive replacement for a familiar object but still misses the old one. A reader recalls the golden-cage image to describe why price alone has not brought satisfaction.
entries.cultural_context: The verse moves from food to ornament to shelter. Only the final image gives an explicit response: the owl cries while remembering its hollow. That ending supplies a concrete contrast between what the giver prizes and what the recipient misses.

entries.title: A nature said to last a lifetime
entries.odia:
ଘୁଷୁରି ପ୍ରକୃତି ପଙ୍କେ ଲୋଟେ
ମଣିଷ ପ୍ରକୃତି ମଲେ ତୁଟେ।
entries.literal_meaning: A pig’s nature is to wallow in mud; a person’s nature ends only at death.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘୁଷୁରିର ପଙ୍କରେ ଲୋଟିବା ସହ ମଣିଷର ପ୍ରକୃତିକୁ ମିଳାଇ ବକ୍ତା କହୁଛନ୍ତି ଯେ ତାହା ମୃତ୍ୟୁବେଳେ ହିଁ ତୁଟେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ବାରମ୍ବାର ଫେରିଆସୁଥିବା ଅଭ୍ୟାସ ବା ସ୍ୱଭାବ ପ୍ରତି ଏହା ଏକ କଠୋର ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ; ମଣିଷର ବଦଳିବାର କ୍ଷମତା ବିଷୟରେ ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The first line supplies a repeated behaviour; the second turns persistence into an absolute claim lasting until death. Read editorially, the saying expresses frustration or certainty about an entrenched disposition. Its force comes from that exaggeration, rather than establishing that a person cannot change.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A colleague returns to the same habit after repeatedly promising to alter it. Someone quotes the saying in frustration at the recurrence. This illustrates the speaker’s judgment, not a settled prediction about the colleague.
entries.cultural_context: ପ୍ରକୃତି links the animal and human lines, while ଲୋଟେ and ତୁଟେ bind them in rhyme. Mud gives the first line a visible action; death gives the second its emphatic endpoint.

entries.title: Six for the horse, nine for its feed
entries.odia: ଘୋଡା ଛ’ଟଙ୍କାକୁ ଦାନା ନ’ଟଙ୍କା।
entries.literal_meaning: The horse costs six rupees; its feed costs nine.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘୋଡ଼ାର ଦାମ ଛଅ ଟଙ୍କା, କିନ୍ତୁ ତାହାର ଦାନା ପାଇଁ ନଅ ଟଙ୍କା ଲାଗୁଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, କିଣିବା ଦାମଠାରୁ ରଖିବା ଓ ଚଳାଇବା ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ବଡ଼ ହୋଇଯିବାର ଚିତ୍ର। କମ୍ ଦାମରେ ମିଳିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ଭାରି ପଡ଼ିପାରେ।
entries.explanation: Nine exceeds six: the expense attached to keeping the horse is larger than its purchase price. The editorial reading draws attention to the costs that follow an acquisition. A low initial price need not make something inexpensive to maintain.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A second-hand printer costs little, but replacement ink soon costs more than the machine. Its owner recalls the horse and feed comparison.
entries.cultural_context: The proverb puts the animal and its food into the same monetary scale. The small, easily compared numbers make the imbalance immediately visible. It leaves the feeding period unspecified.

entries.title: Loose wheel, loose axle
entries.odia:
ଚକ ଢିଲାକୁ ଅଖ ଢିଲା
ଯାଉ ଯାଉ ଗାଡି ଯୁଆଡେ ଗଲା।
entries.literal_meaning: The wheel is loose and the axle loose; as it goes along, the cart goes whichever way.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚକ ଓ ଅଖ ଦୁହେଁ ଢିଲା ଥିବାରୁ ଗାଡ଼ିର ଗତି ଠିକ୍ ରହୁନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ପରସ୍ପର ସହ ଜଡ଼ିତ କାମର ଏକାଧିକ ଅଂଶରେ ଶୈଥିଲ୍ୟ ରହିଲେ ସମଗ୍ର କାମ ଅନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରିତ ହୋଇଯିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା।
entries.explanation: The trouble is shared by two connected parts: neither wheel nor axle is firm. The cart’s direction then becomes uncertain. Read editorially, the image describes what happens when laxness is present in more than one part of a shared undertaking and nobody supplies the needed steadiness.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: One team leaves the instructions vague, while another carries them out without checking. As the work drifts from its purpose, a colleague recalls the loose wheel and axle.
entries.cultural_context: The verse moves from the wheel and axle to the whole cart. That change of scale gives the image its force: weaknesses in connected parts affect the direction of the undertaking as a whole.

entries.title: The farmer who sustains many lives
entries.odia: ଚଷା, ଲକ୍ଷେ ଜୀବ ପୋଷା।
entries.literal_meaning: The cultivator sustains a hundred thousand lives.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚଷା ନିଜ ପାଇଁ ମାତ୍ର ନୁହେଁ, ଅନେକ ଜୀବଙ୍କ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ପାଇଁ ଚାଷ କରନ୍ତି—ଏହା କଥାଟିର ପ୍ରଶଂସାମୂଳକ ଭାବ। ଲକ୍ଷେ କହି ତାଙ୍କ ଶ୍ରମର ବ୍ୟାପକ ଉପକାରକୁ ବଡ଼ କରି ଦେଖାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The saying honours the cultivator by linking one occupation to the nourishment of many lives. Its large number gives the praise breadth. Read editorially, the line makes the shared benefit of agricultural labour visible beyond the farmer’s own household.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: At a community meal, a speaker thanks those who grew the food and quotes the saying to recognise how their labour supports others.
entries.cultural_context: ଚଷା and ପୋଷା make a compact rhyme that joins an occupation to its nourishing role. ଜୀବ gives that role a wide reach, while ଲକ୍ଷେ magnifies the number of lives sustained.

witnesses.locator: Page17, third complete saying, single line ଚଷା, ଲକ୍ଷେ ଜୀବ ପୋଷା.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; wording and comma retained. Literal hundred thousand preserves ଲକ୍ଷେ; commentary reads it as emphatic abundance, not a measured count.

entries.title: A question about rice, an answer about meals
entries.odia:
ଚାଉଳ ସେରକ କେତେ
ନା’ ମୁଁ ମଠରେ ଖାଏ।
entries.literal_meaning: “How much is a ser of rice?” “I eat at the monastery.”
entries.meaning_odia: ଚାଉଳ ସେରକର ଦାମ ପଚାରିଲେ ଉତ୍ତର ଆସୁଛି—ମୁଁ ମଠରେ ଖାଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ପଚରାଯାଇଥିବା କଥାର ଉତ୍ତର ନଦେଇ ନିଜର ଅଲଗା ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥାର କଥା କହିବାର ଅମେଳ ଏଠାରେ ଧରାପଡ଼ିଛି।
entries.explanation: The question asks for a price; the reply supplies a place of eating. That mismatch makes the exchange comic. Read editorially, it can describe someone who answers from their own arrangements while leaving the practical question unanswered.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Asked how much a commute costs, someone replies that they work from home. A listener recalls this exchange because the reply describes a personal arrangement without supplying the requested fare.
entries.cultural_context: ସେରକ places the question in the language of measuring rice. ମଠରେ shifts the reply away from the market to a place where the speaker eats. The change of subject, rather than a specified monastic custom, carries the joke.

witnesses.locator: Page17, sixth complete saying, two lines beginning ଚାଉଳ ସେରକ କେତେ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; wording and line break retained. English renders the implied question and reply as dialogue. Explanation editorial; no monastic meal custom inferred.

entries.title: Three sharing the rice, and another to bring home
entries.odia:
ଚାଉଳ ସେରକୁ ତିନି ପରାଣୀ
ଆହୁରି ଯାଉଚି ବୋହୁକୁ ଆଣି।
entries.literal_meaning: Three people for a ser of rice, and still going to bring home a daughter-in-law.
entries.meaning_odia: ସେରେ ଚାଉଳ ପାଇଁ ଆଗରୁ ତିନି ପରାଣୀ ଅଛନ୍ତି, ତଥାପି ବୋହୁ ଆଣିବାକୁ ଯାଉଛନ୍ତି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଉପଲବ୍ଧ ସମ୍ବଳରେ ଆଉ ଜଣଙ୍କ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ନେବାର ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ଅଛି କି ନାହିଁ, ସେହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠୁଛି।
entries.explanation: The verse first counts the people sharing a given amount of rice, then adds the prospect of another household member. Read editorially, it questions taking on an added responsibility without considering the means to support it. The concern is provision and planning, not the worth of the person arriving.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A small group already stretches its shared supplies but invites another participant without arranging more. A reader recalls the saying’s contrast between present provision and a new commitment.
entries.cultural_context: The count of three gives the first line a concrete scale. Bringing a daughter-in-law home supplies the next change in that count. The verse leaves the identities of the three and the period covered by the rice unstated.

entries.title: The son follows the household’s role
entries.odia:
ଚାଟ ଘର ପୁଅ ଚାଟ
ଭାଟ ଘର ପୁଅ ଭାଟ।
entries.literal_meaning: The son of a learner’s household is a learner; the son of a bard’s household is a bard.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚାଟ ଘରର ପୁଅ ଚାଟ, ଭାଟ ଘରର ପୁଅ ଭାଟ—କଥାଟି ପରିବାରର ପରିଚୟକୁ ପରପିଢ଼ିରେ ଦେଖୁଛି। ଏଠାରେ ଚାଟର ଶବ୍ଦାର୍ଥ ବିଦ୍ୟାର୍ଥୀ, ଭାଟର ଅର୍ଥ ପ୍ରଶସ୍ତି ଗାୟକ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଏହା ପରିବାରର ଶିକ୍ଷା ବା କାମକୁ ପିଲାଙ୍କ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ିବାର ଧାରଣା; ଜନ୍ମ ମାତ୍ରରୁ ପ୍ରତିଭା ନିର୍ଦ୍ଧାରିତ ହୁଏ ବୋଲି ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: Each line repeats the household’s role in its son. The formula expresses an expectation of continuity between generations. The inspected modern article quotes it while questioning the use of lineage to claim superior ability or inherit positions; that context shows why the expectation deserves scrutiny.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: People assume that a child will follow the family’s occupation before asking about the child’s interests. A reader quotes the saying to identify that expectation and then questions it.
entries.cultural_context: The parallel ଘର ପୁଅ construction carries family identity from one generation to the next. ଚାଟ refers to a learner, while ଭାଟ names a bard. The rhyme makes the repeated social pattern memorable.

witnesses.locator: Page17, ninth complete saying, printed opening ବାଟ ଘର ପୁଅ ଚାଟ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026. Original first line is ବାଟ ଘର ପୁଅ ଚାଟ. Display repairs only opening ବାଟ to ଚାଟ using the separately cited public counterpart; uploaded ପୁଅ in both lines and line break retained.

variants.odia:
ନାଗର ପୁଅ ନାଗ
ବାଘର ପୁଅ ବାଘ।
variants.locator: Uploaded compilation page27, fourth item beginning ନାଗର ପୁଅ.
variants.note: Animal-image variant grouped editorially with the learner-and-bard household formula. Literal: A cobra’s son is a cobra; a tiger’s son is a tiger. ଅର୍ଥ: ନାଗର ପୁଅ ନାଗ, ବାଘର ପୁଅ ବାଘ—ଦୁଇ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ପୂର୍ବ ପିଢ଼ିର ପରିଚୟ ପର ପିଢ଼ିରେ ପୁଣି ଦେଖାଯାଉଛି। ଚାଟ ଘର ପୁଅ ଚାଟ, ଭାଟ ଘର ପୁଅ ଭାଟ ରୂପଟି ପରି ଏହା ପିଢ଼ିରୁ ପିଢ଼ିକୁ ସାଦୃଶ୍ୟର ଆଶା ପ୍ରକାଶ କରେ। ମଣିଷର ଗୁଣ କିମ୍ବା ଯୋଗ୍ୟତା ବଂଶରୁ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହୁଏ ବୋଲି ଏହାକୁ ପ୍ରମାଣ ଧରାଯାଏନାହିଁ। Explanation: The two lines repeat the parent’s identity in the son, using the same parallel formula as the learner-and-bard household version. We group it editorially as an animal-image variant of that continuity theme. The wording leaves open whether a particular speaker admires or fears the resemblance; it does not establish inherited human character or ability. Source: uploaded compilation page27, inspected17November2026; exact two lines retained without repair. Source quotation excluded from collection CC licensing; upload licence unknown.

entries.title: Licking while cutting the throat
entries.odia:
ଚାଟୁଥା
ପଛରୁ ଗଳାକୁ କାଟୁଥା।
entries.literal_meaning: Keep licking; from behind, keep cutting the throat.
entries.meaning_odia: ଶବ୍ଦାର୍ଥରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ପଟେ ଚାଟିବା, ଅନ୍ୟ ପଟେ ପଛରୁ ଗଳା କାଟିବା। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଚାଟିବା ଏଠାରେ ତୋଷାମଦର ଚିତ୍ର; ତାହା ସହ ଗୁପ୍ତରେ କ୍ଷତି କରିବାର ବିରୋଧ ରହିଛି। ମିଠା ବ୍ୟବହାର ଦେଖାଇ ବିଶ୍ୱାସଘାତ କରୁଥିବା ଆଚରଣକୁ କଥାଟି ବିଦ୍ରୂପ କରୁଛି।
entries.explanation: The first line offers the image of licking; the next reveals a throat being cut from behind. Read figuratively, the contrast exposes fawning behaviour that conceals betrayal. The repeated imperative sounds like a bitter accusation: the apparent friendliness and the hidden harm belong to the same conduct.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone repeatedly praises a colleague while secretly undermining that colleague’s work. On discovering the contradiction, a friend quotes this couplet.
entries.cultural_context: The rhyme ଚାଟୁଥା / କାଟୁଥା brings two sharply opposed actions close together in sound. The phrase ପଛରୁ gives the second action its concealed, treacherous character.

entries.title: Across the roofs, unnoticed
entries.odia:
ଚାଳେ ଚାଳେ ଗଲା ଚାଳୁଆ ମୁଷା
କେହି ନଜାଣିଲେ ସାଇ ପଡିଶା।
entries.literal_meaning: The roof-dwelling rat went from roof to roof; none of the neighbours knew.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚାଳରେ ରହୁଥିବା ମୂଷା ଚାଳେ ଚାଳେ ଚାଲିଗଲା, ଅଥଚ ସାଇପଡ଼ିଶା କେହି ଜାଣିଲେ ନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ପାଖରେ ଲୋକ ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ସେମାନଙ୍କ ଅଜାଣତରେ କୌଣସି କାମ ହୋଇଯିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା।
entries.explanation: The rat passes along the roofs while the neighbours remain unaware. Read editorially, the couplet describes something accomplished quietly, beyond the notice of people close by. The second line makes the lack of witnesses the point of the scene.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A small arrangement is completed quietly before anyone nearby hears about it. When it finally becomes known, someone recalls the rat that crossed the roofs unnoticed.
entries.cultural_context: The repetition ଚାଳେ ଚାଳେ carries the movement across roofs, and ଚାଳୁଆ identifies the rat with that setting. The second line shifts attention from the moving animal to the neighbours who know nothing of its passage.

witnesses.locator: Page18, first complete couplet, beginning ଚାଳେ ଚାଳେ.

entries.title: Cultivation and a home
entries.odia: ଚାଷ ନାହିଁ ଯା’ର ବାସ ନାହିଁ ତା’ର।
entries.literal_meaning: Whoever has no cultivation has no home.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯାହାର ଚାଷ ନାହିଁ, ତାହାର ବାସ ନାହିଁ—କଥାଟି ଚାଷ ଓ ଘର କରି ରହିବାକୁ ଏକାଠି ବାନ୍ଧୁଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଚାଷରୁ ମିଳୁଥିବା ଜୀବିକାକୁ ଘରସଂସାରର ଆଧାର ବୋଲି ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଦିଆଯାଇଛି। ଏହି କଠୋର ଉକ୍ତି ଚାଷ ନ କରୁଥିବା ସମସ୍ତ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ବାସ୍ତବ ସ୍ଥିତିର ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The rhyme links cultivation with having a home. Read editorially, it stresses the work that sustains a household, using farming as that work. Its absolute formulation belongs to the saying’s agricultural outlook; it does not establish that people in other occupations lack homes.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A household discussing its neglected fields quotes the saying to stress how closely its own home depends on the farming that supports it.
entries.cultural_context: ଚାଷ and ବାସ form a compact rhyme, while ଯା’ର and ତା’ର tie the two clauses to the same person. The structure turns an economic dependence into a memorable categorical statement.

witnesses.locator: Page18, single-line saying beginning ଚାଷ ନାହିଁ, immediately after the roof-rat couplet.

entries.title: Worry eats away
entries.odia:
ଚିନ୍ତା ଖାଏ ଗଣ୍ଡି
ଲୁଣ ଖାଏ ହାଣ୍ଡି।
entries.literal_meaning: Worry eats the body; salt eats the pot.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚିନ୍ତା ଦେହକୁ ଖାଏ, ଲୁଣ ହାଣ୍ଡିକୁ ଖାଏ—ଦୁଇ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ଏକେ କ୍ରିୟାର ତୁଳନା ରହିଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଲଗାତାର ଚିନ୍ତାରେ ମଣିଷ ଭିତରୁ କ୍ଷୟ ହେଉଥିବା ପରି ଅନୁଭବ କରିବାକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ଧରିଛି। ଏହା ଚିନ୍ତାର ଭାରକୁ ବୁଝାଉଥିବା ରୂପକ।
entries.explanation: The same verb, eats, gives worry and salt a consuming force: one acts on the body, the other on the pot. Read editorially, the comparison conveys the feeling of being worn down by persistent worry. Its strength lies in making an inward burden visible through a familiar household object.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After days of turning the same unresolved matter over in their mind, someone quotes the couplet to describe how worn down they feel.
entries.cultural_context: ଗଣ୍ଡି and ହାଣ୍ଡି rhyme, while ଖାଏ repeats in the same position in both lines. That parallel gives the body and the pot matching places in the comparison.

entries.title: An identity already known
entries.odia: ଚିହ୍ନା ବ୍ରାହ୍ମଣର କି ପଇତା ଲୋଡା?
entries.literal_meaning: Does a known Brahmin need a sacred thread?
entries.meaning_odia: ଯେଉଁ ବ୍ରାହ୍ମଣଙ୍କ ପରିଚୟ ଆଗରୁ ଜଣା, ତାଙ୍କୁ ଚିହ୍ନିବା ପାଇଁ ପଇତାର ଚିହ୍ନ କାହିଁକି ଦରକାର—ଏହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କଥାଟିର ଆଧାର। ପରିଚୟ ଆଗରୁ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ଥିଲେ ତାହାର ଅତିରିକ୍ତ ବାହ୍ୟ ପ୍ରମାଣକୁ ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ବୋଲି କହିବା ଏହାର ଭାବ। ପରିଚୟ ଓ ବିଶ୍ୱସନୀୟତା କିନ୍ତୁ ଏକ କଥା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The question treats the thread as an identifying sign and asks what it adds when the person is already known. It can dismiss a redundant introduction or outward proof of an established identity. The inspected modern essay also challenges the further assumption that familiar people must be trustworthy.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A long-standing member is introduced at length to a group that already knows them. Someone quotes the question to tease the unnecessary introduction.
entries.cultural_context: The sacred thread supplies the social marker in the image; familiarity supplies recognition without that marker. The comparison uses a caste-associated sign, but it makes no sound basis for ranking people’s worth.

entries.title: Let anger die down within
entries.odia:
ଚୂନ ରାଗ ପାନେ ମରୁ
ମନ ରାଗ ମନେ ମରୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: Let lime’s sharpness die in the betel; let the mind’s anger die in the mind.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏହି ପାଠରେ ଚୂନର ରାଗ ଅର୍ଥ କଡ଼ାପଣ, ମନର ରାଗ ଅର୍ଥ କ୍ରୋଧ। ଚୂନର କଡ଼ାପଣ ପାନରେ ମରୁ, ମନର କ୍ରୋଧ ମନରେ ଶାନ୍ତ ହେଉ—ଏହି ତୁଳନା ରହିଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ରାଗକୁ ବାହାରେ ଝାଡ଼ିବା ବଦଳରେ ଶାନ୍ତ ହେବାକୁ ଦେବାର କଥା ଏହା। ମୂଳ ଛାପାର ଦୁଇଟି ରଗକୁ ଏଠାରେ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ଅନୁମାନରେ ରାଗ କରାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The proposed reading turns on two senses of ରାଗ: sharpness in lime and anger in the mind. Each is asked to die away within its own setting. Our editorial reading hears a wish for anger to subside before it is directed outward. Both occurrences of ରାଗ are explicitly conjectural repairs of the upload’s ରଗ.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Before sending an angry reply, someone pauses and recalls the couplet as a wish for the anger to settle first.
entries.cultural_context: The parallel ପାନେ / ମନେ and repeated ମରୁ link the material image to an inner feeling. Lime and betel supply the first setting; the mind supplies the second.

witnesses.locator: Page18, couplet beginning ଚୂନ ରଗ ପାନେ ମରୁ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026. Other words and two-line layout retained.

entries.title: Who can wake the already awake?
entries.odia:
ଚେଇଁ ଶୋଇବ ଯିଏ
ତାକୁ ଉଠାଇବ କିଏ?
entries.literal_meaning: Who will wake someone who sleeps while awake?
entries.meaning_odia: ଚେଇଁ ଥାଇ ଶୋଇବା ଅର୍ଥ ଏଠାରେ ଶୋଇବାର ଛଳନା। ଯିଏ ଜାଣିଶୁଣି ନଜାଣିବା ପରି ରହେ, ତାକୁ କେବଳ ବୁଝାଇଦେଲେ କିପରି ସଚେତନ କରାଯିବ—କଥାଟି ସେହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରୁଛି। ଅଜ୍ଞତା ଓ ସ୍ୱୀକାର କରିବାକୁ ଅନିଚ୍ଛା ମଧ୍ୟରେ ତଫାତ ଏହାର କେନ୍ଦ୍ର।
entries.explanation: Someone genuinely asleep can be awakened; someone only pretending to sleep already has the awareness that waking would supply. The inspected public use makes the pretence explicit. Our reading applies the paradox to deliberate refusal to acknowledge what one already knows.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A participant has understood the agreed plan but repeatedly acts as though it was never explained. A colleague quotes the couplet to distinguish unwillingness from misunderstanding.
entries.cultural_context: The opening puts waking and sleeping together in a deliberate contradiction. The answering question shifts attention from the person pretending to the frustrated effort of anyone trying to rouse them.

entries.title: Brazen words after wrongdoing
entries.odia: ଚୋରଙ୍କର ଭାରି ମୁହଁ ଟାଣ।
entries.literal_meaning: Thieves have very tough mouths.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏଠାରେ ମୁହଁ ଟାଣର ଅର୍ଥ ହେଲା କଟୁ ବା ଅନୁଚିତ କଥା କହିବାରେ ସଂକୋଚ ନଥିବା। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଭୁଲ କରି ମଧ୍ୟ ଲଜ୍ଜା ନକରି ଉଦ୍ଧତ କଥା କହିବାକୁ ଉକ୍ତିଟି ଭର୍ତ୍ସନା କରୁଛି। କେବଳ କାହାର କଥା କହିବା ଢଙ୍ଗ ଦେଖି ସେ ଚୋର ବୋଲି ପ୍ରମାଣ ହୁଏ ନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The tough mouth is an idiom for unrestrained, impudent speech. Our reading hears a rebuke aimed at someone who responds brazenly despite wrongdoing. The force comes from the mismatch between what calls for accountability and the speaker’s unapologetic manner.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone admits taking another person’s belongings without permission, then answers the complaint with insults. A bystander quotes the saying about that brazen response.
entries.cultural_context: The mouth stands for speech, and its hardness gives the speech a resistant, unyielding quality. ଭାରି intensifies the accusation in a compact conversational sentence.

entries.title: Wisdom after the thief escapes
entries.odia: ଚୋର ପଳାଇବା ପରେ ବୁଦ୍ଧି ବାହାରେ।
entries.literal_meaning: Sense emerges after the thief has fled.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚୋର ପଳାଇଯିବା ପରେ କ’ଣ କରିବାର ଥିଲା ସେ ବୁଦ୍ଧି ଆସୁଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଠିକ୍ ସମୟରେ ଦରକାର ଥିବା ବୁଝାମଣା ଘଟଣା ସରିବା ପରେ ଆସିବାକୁ କଥାଟି ବିଦ୍ରୂପ କରୁଛି। ଏହାର ଜୋର ବୁଦ୍ଧିର ଅଭାବ ଅପେକ୍ଷା ବୁଦ୍ଧି ଆସିବାର ବିଳମ୍ବ ଉପରେ।
entries.explanation: The thief has already escaped when the useful thought finally arrives. Read editorially, the line mocks hindsight that appears too late to change that moment. It can be rueful or teasing: the answer seems clear only once the opportunity to act has passed.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After an avoidable mix-up is over, everyone suddenly explains the simple check that would have caught it beforehand. Someone compares their late insight to sense arriving after the thief has fled.
entries.cultural_context: The word ପରେ fixes the order: escape first, understanding afterward. That compact reversal of useful timing carries the saying’s sting.

entries.title: A thief with a soldier’s bearing
entries.odia: ଚୋର ହୋଇ ପୁଣି ପାଇକ ପଣ।
entries.literal_meaning: A thief, yet putting on a soldier’s bearing.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚୋର ହୋଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ପାଇକ ପରି ପଣ ଦେଖାଇବା—ଦୁଇଟି ବିପରୀତ ପରିଚୟକୁ କଥାଟି ଏକାଠି ରଖିଛି। ପାଇକର ଶବ୍ଦାର୍ଥ ପଦାତିକ ସୈନ୍ୟ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ନିଜେ ଭୁଲ କରି ମଧ୍ୟ ଦମ୍ଭ ବା ବାହାଦୁରି ଦେଖାଇବାର ଆଚରଣ ଏଠାରେ ଉପହାସର ବିଷୟ।
entries.explanation: The opening names wrongdoing; the ending adds a soldierly pose. Read editorially, the line mocks someone who answers their own misconduct with swagger. Its tension lies in the gap between the conduct and the bearing the person puts on.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After admitting that they took something without permission, someone boasts of being too formidable to challenge. A listener quotes the line about a thief displaying soldierly bearing.
entries.cultural_context: ପାଇକ supplies the soldier image, and ପଣ turns it into a quality or bearing. ପୁଣି sharpens the surprise that this display accompanies the identity given at the start.

entries.title: Telling the thief and the constable
entries.odia:
ଚୋରକୁ କହୁଚି ଚୋରି କର
ସିପାହିକୁ କହୁଚି ଜଗିଥା।
entries.literal_meaning: Telling the thief, “Steal”; telling the constable, “Keep watch.”
entries.meaning_odia: ଏକ ପଟେ ଚୋରକୁ ଚୋରି କରିବାକୁ କହୁଛି, ଅନ୍ୟ ପଟେ ସିପାହିକୁ ଜଗିବାକୁ କହୁଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଦୁଇ ବିପରୀତ ପକ୍ଷକୁ ବିପରୀତ ପରାମର୍ଶ ଦେଇ ଦୁଇପଟିଆ ଭୂମିକା ନେବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ମୂଳ ଛାପାର କାରକୁ ଏଠାରେ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ଅନୁମାନରେ କର କରାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The same unnamed person encourages the theft and also urges vigilance against it. Our reading sees double-dealing in those incompatible instructions: each side hears support, while the two directions work against one another. The displayed command କର is an explicit editorial repair of printed କାର.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone privately encourages a person to break an agreed rule, then tells the organiser to enforce that very rule. A witness compares the conflicting advice to instructing both thief and constable.
entries.cultural_context: The repeated କହୁଚି keeps the act of advising constant while the recipients and commands change. The thief and the watching constable make the contradiction concrete.

entries.title: Each mind on its own concern
entries.odia:
ଚୋର ମନ ଗଣ୍ଠିରେ
ବାବାଜି ମନ କଣ୍ଠିରେ
ବେପାରୀ ମନ ପାଣ୍ଠିରେ।
entries.literal_meaning: The thief’s mind is on the tied bundle; the ascetic’s mind on his neck beads; the trader’s mind on funds.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚୋରର ମନ ଗଣ୍ଠି ବା ବନ୍ଧା ପୁଟୁଳିରେ, ବାବାଜିଙ୍କ ମନ କଣ୍ଠିମାଳାରେ, ବେପାରୀର ମନ ପାଣ୍ଠିରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଯାହା ସହ ଯାହାର ଆଗ୍ରହ ବା କାମ ଜଡ଼ିତ, ତାହା ଆଡ଼କୁ ତାଙ୍କ ମନ ଯାଉଥିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ତିନି ପ୍ରକାର ଧ୍ୟାନକୁ ତିନିଟି ବସ୍ତୁରେ ଧରାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: Each line gives a person a different object of attention. The tied bundle, devotional beads and funds make those preoccupations tangible. Read editorially, the verse notices how interests and roles shape what occupies the mind; it does not make the three pursuits morally equivalent.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: At the same gathering, one person notices the arrangements, another the accounts and another the music. Someone recalls the verse to comment on their different concerns.
entries.cultural_context: ଗଣ୍ଠି, କଣ୍ଠି and ପାଣ୍ଠି are close in sound but name different objects. Repeating ମନ in each line holds the pattern steady while the focus changes.

entries.title: One sin and a thousand
entries.odia:
ଚୋରି କଲା ଲୋକର ଏକ ପାପ
ଚୋରି ଗଲା ଲୋକର ସହସ୍ର ପାପ।
entries.literal_meaning: The person who stole has one sin; the person who was robbed has a thousand sins.
entries.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଥମ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ଚୋରି କରିଥିବା ଲୋକର ଏକ ପାପ, ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟରେ ଯାହାର ଚୋରି ଯାଇଛି ତାହାର ସହସ୍ର ପାପ କୁହାଯାଇଛି। ଏହି ଓଲଟା ହିସାବର କାରଣ ମୂଳ ପାଠ କହୁନାହିଁ। ଗୋଟିଏ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପଢ଼ା ହେଲା—ଚୋରି ପରେ ଅନେକଙ୍କୁ ବିନା ପ୍ରମାଣରେ ସନ୍ଦେହ କରିବାରୁ ଆଉ ଅନ୍ୟାୟ ବଢ଼ିପାରେ। ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ପାରମ୍ପରିକ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ନୁହେଁ; ଚୋରିର ଶିକାର ହେବା ନିଜେ ଦୋଷ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The numbers create a disturbing reversal: the person who suffers the theft is assigned a much larger burden than the thief. The verse leaves the reason unstated. One possible editorial reading is a warning about multiplying groundless suspicions after a loss; that explanation remains unverified. Being robbed does not itself make someone blameworthy.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example for this possible reading: After a theft, rumours begin naming many people without evidence. A reader discusses the couplet as a warning about those accusations, while questioning its harsh wording toward the person who suffered the loss.
entries.cultural_context: The near-matching କଲା and ଗଲା switch the perspective from the person who acts to the person who loses. ଏକ and ସହସ୍ର then enlarge the reversal through a stark numerical contrast.

witnesses.locator: Page19, two lines beginning ଚୋରି କଲା ଲୋକର, immediately following the three-role preoccupation verse.

entries.title: Plenty of dumplings, an untouched mouth
entries.odia:
ଛ’ ଅଡା ଚାଉଳ ଗଇଁଠା
ପାଟି ହୋଇ ନାହିଁ ଅଇଁଠା।
entries.literal_meaning: Dumplings from six ada measures of rice; the mouth has not even been soiled by eating.
entries.meaning_odia: ଛଅ ଅଡା ଚାଉଳର ଗଇଁଠା, ଅଥଚ ପାଟି ଅଇଁଠା ହୋଇନାହିଁ—ଦୁଇ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ଏହି ଅସଙ୍ଗତି ରହିଛି। ଅଡା ଏକ ଶସ୍ୟମାପ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଏତେ ଖାଦ୍ୟକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ କିଛି ଖାଇବାରେ ଗଣନା ନକରିବାର ଢଙ୍ଗକୁ କଥାଟି ଥଟ୍ଟା କରିପାରେ। କିଏ କେତେ ଖାଇଲା, ପାଠ ତାହା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କହୁନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: A measured quantity of rice dumplings stands beside a mouth said to be untouched by eating. One editorial reading hears a teasing refusal to count plenty as even a taste. The verse leaves the eating itself unstated, so the contrast can be appreciated without inventing a meal or judging anyone’s actual hunger.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example for this reading: Someone receives a substantial share of something and dismisses it as practically nothing. A listener recalls the dumplings that supposedly have not even touched the mouth.
entries.cultural_context: ଗଇଁଠା and ଅଇଁଠା rhyme, connecting the food with the mouth’s claimed condition. The measure in the first line gives weight to what the second line appears to dismiss.

witnesses.locator: Page19, couplet beginning ଛ’ ଅଡା ଚାଉଳ ଗଇଁଠା.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; wording and two-line layout retained. ଅଡା rendered as ada grain measure without conversion. First line has no explicit eating verb; expanded interpretation is editorial.

entries.title: Guile in trade, a bank for water
entries.odia: ଛନ୍ଦେ ବଣିଜ ବନ୍ଧେ ପାଣି।
entries.literal_meaning: Trade by guile; water by an embankment.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏଠାରେ ଛନ୍ଦର ଅଭିଧାନଗତ ଛଳ ବା କପଟ ଅର୍ଥକୁ ନେଇ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ବନ୍ଧ ଯେପରି ପାଣିକୁ ଧରିରଖେ, ଛଳ ସେପରି ବଣିଜକୁ ଧରିରଖେ—ଏହା ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା। କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟବସାୟ ବିଷୟରେ ଏକ ସନ୍ଦେହପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଧାରଣା ରଖୁଛି; ସବୁ ବ୍ୟବସାୟୀ କପଟୀ ବୋଲି ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The line pairs the means of holding water with what it presents as a means of sustaining trade. Taking ଛନ୍ଦ in its attested sense of guile gives the comparison a cynical edge: commerce is pictured as depending on manipulation. That contextual reading is editorial; the brief source supplies no separate gloss.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A seller’s presentation is found to hide important defects. A listener quotes the saying critically about that deal, without treating it as a rule about every business.
entries.cultural_context: ଛନ୍ଦେ and ବନ୍ଧେ rhyme and occupy matching positions. The familiar embankment image gives a concrete shape to the more abstract claim about commercial dealings.

witnesses.locator: Page19, single line beginning ଛନ୍ଦେ ବଣିଜ.

entries.title: Shade that travels with you
entries.odia:
ଛାଇତ ତ ଛାଇ, ଛତାର ଛାଇ
ଗଛ ଛାଇ କି ସଙ୍ଗତେ ଯାଇ?
entries.literal_meaning: Shade indeed, shade—the umbrella’s shade. Does a tree’s shade go along with you?
entries.meaning_odia: ଛତାର ଛାଇ ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ଯାଇପାରେ, ଗଛର ଛାଇ କି ସେପରି ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ଯିବ—କଥାଟି ଏହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରୁଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଏକ ଜାଗାରେ ମିଳୁଥିବା ସୁବିଧା ଓ ଚାଲିବା ବେଳେ ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ନେଇହେଉଥିବା ସୁବିଧାର ତଫାତ ଏଠାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟ। କେବଳ ଛାଇ ଥିଲେ ନୁହେଁ, ଯେଉଁଠି ଦରକାର ସେଠି ତାହା ମିଳିବାର କଥା।
entries.explanation: Both the umbrella and the tree offer shade, but the question asks which can accompany someone who moves. Our editorial reading values help that remains available where it is needed. The contrast is about portability and circumstance, not a claim that stationary shelter has no worth.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone can use an essential reference only in one office but needs it while travelling. A colleague compares a copy they can carry with the umbrella’s shade that goes along with them.
entries.cultural_context: The first line repeats ଛାଇ, making the shared benefit clear. The second introduces ସଙ୍ଗତେ ଯାଇ—going along—and makes that the deciding difference.

entries.title: Mushrooms when the rain comes
entries.odia:
ଛି ଲୋ ଛତୁ,
ମେଘ ବରଷିଲେ କେତେ ତୁ ଫୁଟୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: Tut, mushroom! How you sprout when the clouds rain!
entries.meaning_odia: ଛତୁକୁ ଉପହାସ କରି କୁହାଯାଉଛି—ମେଘ ବରଷିଲେ ତୁ କେତେ ଫୁଟୁ! ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଅନୁକୂଳ ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ମିଳିବାମାତ୍ରେ କାହାର ଅତି ଉତ୍ସାହ ବା ବଢ଼ିଚଢ଼ି ଆଚରଣକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଥଟ୍ଟା କରିହୁଏ। ଛି ଶବ୍ଦଟି ଏହାକୁ ପ୍ରଶଂସା ଅପେକ୍ଷା ତାଚ୍ଛଲ୍ୟର ସ୍ୱର ଦିଏ।
entries.explanation: The speaker addresses a mushroom as though it could hear a rebuke. Rain arrives, and its sprouting becomes something to mock. Our editorial reading is a taunt at exuberance encouraged by favourable circumstances. The inspected dictionary counterpart supports the reproachful tone, while using a different final verb.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After receiving a little encouragement, someone suddenly dominates every discussion. A friend jokingly compares that burst of activity to the mushroom that sprouts when rain arrives.
entries.cultural_context: The rhyme pairs ଛତୁ with ଫୁଟୁ, turning the mushroom’s appearance after rain into a sharp direct address. The opening ଛି sets the speaker’s dismissive tone before the image unfolds.

entries.title: The sulking cat returns
entries.odia:
ଛି ଲୋ ବିଲେଇ କାହିଁକି ରୁଷୁ
ସେଇ ଭାଡ଼ି ତଲେ ପୁଣି ପଶୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: Tut, cat, why do you sulk? You go beneath that same raised storage platform again.
entries.meaning_odia: ବିଲେଇକୁ ପଚରାଯାଉଛି—ସେହି ଭାଡ଼ି ତଳେ ପୁଣି ପଶୁଛୁ ଯଦି, ରୁଷୁଛୁ କାହିଁକି? ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଅଭିମାନ ଦେଖାଇଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ପୁଣି ପୂର୍ବ ଜାଗା ବା ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଫେରିଆସିବାର ଅମେଳକୁ ଏହା ଚିଡ଼ାଉଛି। ଫେରିଆସିବାର କାରଣ କଥାଟି କହୁନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The rebuke puts two actions side by side: taking offence and entering the same place again. Read editorially, it teases a sulk that does not become a lasting break. The speaker treats the return as undercutting the display of displeasure, although the verse leaves the reason for returning unstated.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After a small quarrel, a friend announces that they will stop attending the group’s games, then returns the next evening. Another friend teasingly recalls the cat going under the same platform again.
entries.cultural_context: The raised platform gives the cat a familiar place to enter. The paired verbs ରୁଷୁ and ପଶୁ make the joke audible: taking offence in one line, going back in the next.

entries.title: Small snake, strong venom
entries.odia: ଛୋଟ ସାପର ବିଷ ଟାଣ।
entries.literal_meaning: A small snake’s venom is strong.
entries.meaning_odia: ଢଗଟି ଛୋଟ ସାପ ସହିତ ଟାଣ ବିଷର ଚିତ୍ର ଯୋଡ଼ୁଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଆକାର ଛୋଟ ବୋଲି କାହାର କିମ୍ବା କୌଣସି ଜିନିଷର କ୍ଷତି କରିବାର ଶକ୍ତିକୁ ତୁଚ୍ଛ ଭାବିବା ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ। ଏହା ଢଗର ରୂପକ; ସାପର ଆକାର ଓ ବିଷ ବିଷୟରେ ଜୀବବିଜ୍ଞାନର ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The line puts small size beside strong venom. Our editorial reading is a warning against dismissing a threat because it looks small. The venom claim belongs to the proverb’s imagery; it is not a biological rule about snakes.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A team dismisses a tiny error in a calculation, but it changes every total that follows. A colleague recalls the small snake and its strong venom to challenge that dismissal.
entries.cultural_context: The force comes from the contrast between ଛୋଟ and ଟାଣ: small in visible size, strong in effect. The short sentence leaves the listener to carry that contrast into another situation.

entries.title: An honouring name and a proud response
entries.odia:
ଛୋଟୀ କି ଶ୍ରୀବନ୍ତୀ କହିଲେ
ଗୋଡକୁ ବୁଲାଇ ପକାଏ।
entries.literal_meaning: Call a woman who limps “Sribanti”—an honoured lady—and she swings her leg around.
entries.meaning_odia: ଛୋଟୀକୁ ଶ୍ରୀବନ୍ତୀ କହିବାମାତ୍ରେ ସେ ଗୋଡ଼ ବୁଲାଇ ପକାଉଛି—ଏହା ଢଗର ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗଚିତ୍ର। ମିଳୁଥିବା ସାର୍ବଜନୀନ ପାଠର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ସମ୍ମାନ ପାଇ ଗର୍ବରେ ପୂରିଉଠିବାକୁ ଏହାର ଅର୍ଥ କହେ। ଏଠାରେ ସମ୍ମାନସୂଚକ କଥା ଶୁଣି ଆତ୍ମଗର୍ବ ବଢ଼ିବାର ଭାବକୁ ବୁଝାଯାଉଛି; ଚାଲିବାରେ ଅସୁବିଧା ଥିବାକୁ ଅଯୋଗ୍ୟତା ଭାବେ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରାଯାଉନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: An honouring address is followed by a conspicuous movement of the leg. The inspected public counterpart glosses the scene as pride produced by honour the speaker considers misplaced. The useful distinction is between receiving respectful words and becoming self-important; the source’s disability-based caricature is not a judgment about disabled people’s worth.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A beginner receives an extravagant introduction at a meeting and immediately starts ordering experienced colleagues about. The comparison concerns the inflated response to praise, without applying the source’s bodily insult to the person.
entries.cultural_context: The public counterpart calls the woman ଗୋଦରୀ, while the upload uses ଛୋଟୀ. Both construct their ridicule through a woman’s leg. The change in disability term is recorded openly; the shared sequence is an honouring address followed by a gesture the source treats as pride.

witnesses.locator: Page20, second item beginning ଛୋଟୀ କି.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected 17 November 2026. Exact spelling and spacing retained, including separate କି and ଗୋଡକୁ.

entries.title: Honour held above life
entries.odia:
ଜାନ୍ ଯାଉ, ମହତ ଥାଉ
ମହତ ଗଲେ ନମିଳେ ଆଉ।
entries.literal_meaning: Let life go; let honour remain. Once honour is gone, it cannot be regained.
entries.meaning_odia: ଜୀବନ ଯାଉ ପଛେ ମହତ ରହୁ, କାରଣ ମହତ ଥରେ ଗଲେ ଆଉ ମିଳେନାହିଁ—ଢଗଟି ଏତେ ଦୃଢ଼ ଭାବରେ ସମ୍ମାନର ମୂଲ୍ୟ କହୁଛି। ନିଜ ଆଚରଣରେ ସତ୍ୟନିଷ୍ଠା ଓ ଭଲ ନାଁ ରଖିବାର ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଏଥିରୁ ବୁଝିହୁଏ। ଜୀବନକୁ ବିପଦରେ ପକାଇବା ଏହି ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାର ପରାମର୍ଶ ନୁହେଁ; ମହତ ଆଉ ଫେରେନାହିଁ କହିବାଟି ଢଗର ଚରମ ଜୋର।
entries.explanation: The speaker gives honour a value greater even than life, then reinforces the claim by calling its loss irreversible. That is the verse’s absolute rhetoric. An editorial application is to protect integrity rather than exchange it for an advantage; preserving the wording does not make harm to oneself or anyone else a duty.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone refuses to falsify a record for a profitable deal, saying that a good name matters more than the immediate gain. The example applies the concern for integrity without the verse’s literal life-or-death stakes.
entries.cultural_context: The first line sets two wishes against each other: ଯାଉ and ଥାଉ, let one go and let the other remain. Repeating ମହତ in the next line makes the claimed permanence of its loss the reason for that stark preference.

witnesses.locator: Page20, fifth item beginning ଜାନ୍ ଯାଉ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact wording and two-line layout retained. Literal preserves honour-over-life rhetoric; editorial explanation does not endorse harm.

entries.title: Polished outside, harmful within
entries.odia:
ଠକଙ୍କ ଗୁରୁ
ଉପର ଚିକ୍କଣ ଭିତର ମାରୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: A master of cheats: smooth on the outside, harmful within.
entries.meaning_odia: ଠକଙ୍କ ଗୁରୁ ବୋଲି ବର୍ଣ୍ଣିତ ଲୋକଟିର ବାହାର ଚିକ୍କଣ, ଭିତର ମାରୁ—ଏହି ବିପରୀତ ଚିତ୍ର ଢଗଟି ଦେଉଛି। ଏଠାରେ ମାରୁକୁ ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗ ଅନୁସାରେ କ୍ଷତିକାରକ ଅର୍ଥରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ମନଭୁଲାଣିଆ ବାହ୍ୟ ରୂପ ପଛରେ କ୍ଷତି କରିବାର ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ ଲୁଚିଥିବା ଆମର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା।
entries.explanation: The opening identifies an accomplished cheat; the next line gives that figure two contrary surfaces, polished outside and harmful within. Our editorial reading is of a reassuring presentation concealing harmful intent. Here ମାରୁ is rendered broadly as harmful from the context, without specifying a violent act.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A seller presents reassuring promises and polished paperwork while knowingly concealing a serious defect. Once the concealment is discovered, someone recalls the master cheat’s smooth exterior.
entries.cultural_context: ଗୁରୁ heightens the accusation by making this person a master among cheats. The short paired words ଉପର and ଭିତର organise the portrait around the difference between what is shown and what is concealed.

witnesses.locator: Page20, penultimate item beginning ଠକଙ୍କ ଗୁରୁ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; wording unchanged. ମାରୁ is translated broadly as harmful in the cheat context; exact dictionary sense was not independently established. Expanded explanation is editorial.

variants.odia:
ବଚନ ମଧୁର ତିଳକ ସରୁ
ଏହାକୁ ଜାଣିବ ଠକଙ୍କ ଗୁରୁ।
variants.locator: Uploaded compilation page30, first item beginning ବଚନ ମଧୁର.
variants.note: Related-family variant grouped editorially with POD-DHAGA-483; textual descent unknown. Literal: Sweet speech, a slender tilak mark: know this one as the master of cheats. ଅର୍ଥ: ମଧୁର କଥା ଓ ସରୁ ତିଳକ ଦେଖି ସେହି ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କୁ ଠକଙ୍କ ଗୁରୁ ଜାଣିବ ବୋଲି ପଙ୍କ୍ତିର ବକ୍ତା କହୁଛନ୍ତି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଆକର୍ଷଣୀୟ ବାହ୍ୟ ରୂପ ଆଡ଼ରେ ଛଳନା ଲୁଚିବାର ସନ୍ଦେହ ଅଛି। ଏହା ଧାର୍ମିକ ଚିହ୍ନ ବା ମଧୁର କଥା କହୁଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଠକ ବୋଲି ଧରିବାର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ। Explanation: This version names two reassuring outward signs, sweet speech and a fine forehead mark, before calling their bearer a master of cheats. We group it editorially with the polished-outside, harmful-inside saying, which shares that concluding identity and the suspicion of deceptive presentation. The source’s sharp judgement is not evidence that polite speakers or people wearing a tilak are dishonest. Source: uploaded compilation page30, inspected17November2026; exact wording retained without repair. Source quotation excluded from collection CC licensing; upload licence unknown.

entries.title: Confidence in divine presence
entries.odia:
ଡର କାହାକୁ ଭୟ କାହାକୁ
ଠାକୁର ଅଛନ୍ତି ଚଉବାହାକୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: Whom should one fear, whom should one dread? The Lord is there on all four sides.
entries.meaning_odia: କାହାକୁ ଡରିବା, କାହାକୁ ଭୟ କରିବା—ଠାକୁର ଚାରିଆଡ଼େ ଅଛନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ବକ୍ତା ସାହସ ପାଉଛନ୍ତି। ଏଠାରେ ଚଉବାହାକୁ ଶବ୍ଦକୁ ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗ ଅନୁସାରେ ଚାରିଆଡ଼େ ଅର୍ଥରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଭଗବାନଙ୍କ ସାନ୍ନିଧ୍ୟରେ ଭରସା ରଖି ମନର ଭୟ କମାଇବାର ଏହା ଭକ୍ତିପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଉକ୍ତି।
entries.explanation: The repeated question answers fear with confidence in the Lord’s presence. We read ଚଉବାହାକୁ contextually as on all four sides; the devotional compound can also evoke the four-armed Lord, so this rendering does not resolve every possible nuance. The couplet voices reassurance rather than establishing that danger cannot occur.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Before beginning a difficult journey, a believer repeats the couplet to steady their mind while making the practical preparations the journey requires.
entries.cultural_context: ଡର and ଭୟ repeat the same concern with increasing emphasis. The second line supplies the believer’s answer: the Lord is present around them. The source leaves the deity unnamed.

witnesses.locator: Page21, opening couplet beginning ଡର କାହାକୁ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact wording retained. ଚଉବାହାକୁ is contextually rendered on all four sides. The spatial rendering is contextual; no named deity inferred.

entries.title: The tall head meets the stick
entries.odia: ଡେଙ୍ଗା ମୁଣ୍ଡରେ ଠେଙ୍ଗା।
entries.literal_meaning: A stick on the tall person’s head.
entries.meaning_odia: ଉଚ୍ଚରେ ଥିବା ମୁଣ୍ଡ ଉପରେ ଠେଙ୍ଗା ପଡ଼ିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ଯିଏ ଆଗରେ ରହେ ବା ନେତୃତ୍ୱ ନିଏ, ତାଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ, ଚାପ ବା ଆପତ୍ତି ମଧ୍ୟ ଆସିପଡ଼େ। ଏଠାରେ ଶରୀରର ଉଚ୍ଚତାକୁ ରୂପକ ଭାବରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଉଛି।
entries.explanation: The head that stands higher is the one pictured receiving the stick. Read editorially, prominence brings exposure: the person who leads may also receive the pressure, complaints or blame. The image describes that burden without making punishment deserved.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After volunteering to coordinate a festival, someone becomes the first person everyone approaches with complaints. A friend recalls the tall head and the stick to describe the burden of taking the lead.
entries.cultural_context: ଡେଙ୍ଗା and ଠେଙ୍ଗା form the compact rhyme. The source gives no explicit verb; the placement of the stick on the head is enough to suggest the blow and its figurative pressure.

witnesses.locator: Page21, second item beginning ଡେଙ୍ଗା ମୁଣ୍ଡରେ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact verbless wording retained. Prominence/leadership explanation is editorial; no physical-height rule asserted.

entries.title: The polished, hollow drum
entries.odia:
ଢାଇଁ ଢାଇଁ ଢାଇଁ ବାଜଇ ଢୋଲ
ବାହାର ଚିକ୍କଣ ଭିତର ପୋଲ।
entries.literal_meaning: Boom, boom, boom sounds the drum: polished outside, hollow within.
entries.meaning_odia: ଢୋଲ ଢାଇଁ ଢାଇଁ ଶବ୍ଦ କରୁଛି; ବାହାରଟି ଚିକ୍କଣ ହେଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଭିତରଟି ଫମ୍ପା। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ବହୁତ ଶବ୍ଦ ଓ ଆକର୍ଷଣୀୟ ବାହ୍ୟ ଦେଖାଣି ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ଭିତରେ ସାରବସ୍ତୁ କମ୍ ଥିବାର ଏହା ଏକ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗଚିତ୍ର। ଢୋଲର ଗଠନକୁ ଏଠାରେ ରୂପକ ଭାବେ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The verse lets the drum make its noise before looking beneath the polished surface. Our editorial reading contrasts an impressive presentation with a lack of substance. Unlike a portrait of concealed malice, the criticism here is emptiness behind the display.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A proposal arrives with elaborate publicity and a glossy presentation, but little evidence or practical detail. A reader compares it to the polished drum that makes a great sound while remaining hollow inside.
entries.cultural_context: Three repetitions of ଢାଇଁ make the opening perform the sound it describes. The rhyme ଢୋଲ/ପୋଲ then turns attention from what is heard to what is inside.

witnesses.locator: Page21, third item beginning ଢାଇଁ ଢାଇଁ ଢାଇଁ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026. Exact words and repetitions retained; only space before final punctuation normalised. Hollow reading of ପୋଲ and expanded display/substance interpretation are documented editorially.

variants.odia: ଫମ୍ପା ମାଠିଆରେ ଶବଦ ବେଶି।
variants.locator: Page29, seventh complete item, ଫମ୍ପା ମାଠିଆରେ ଶବଦ ବେଶି.
variants.note: Related empty-object/noise family grouped editorially with the hollow-drum saying; historical descent is unknown. Literal: There is more sound in an empty earthen pitcher. ଅର୍ଥ: ଫମ୍ପା ମାଠିଆରେ ଶବ୍ଦ ବେଶି ବୋଲି ପଙ୍କ୍ତିଟି କହୁଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଭିତରେ ସାର କମ୍, କଥା ବା ଆଡ଼ମ୍ବର ବେଶି—ଏହି ଅମେଳକୁ ମାଠିଆର ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଧରାଯାଇଛି। କେବଳ କଥାର ପରିମାଣରୁ କାହାର ଜ୍ଞାନ ବିଚାର କରିବାର ନିୟମ ଏହା ନୁହେଁ। Explanation: The pitcher’s emptiness is paired with its greater sound. Applied editorially to speech, the image questions a display that is louder than its substance: much talk may give little understanding or useful content. The point is to examine what the talk contains, rather than be impressed by its volume. Source: uploaded compilation page29, inspected17November2026; exact wording retained without repair. entries.title: Blows for the drum, payment for the drummer
entries.odia: ଢୋଲ ଖାଏ ମାଡ ଢୋଲିଆ ଖାଏ କଉଡି।
entries.literal_meaning: The drum takes the blows; the drummer takes the cowries.
entries.meaning_odia: ମାଡ଼ ଖାଉଛି ଢୋଲ, କିନ୍ତୁ କଉଡ଼ି ପାଉଛି ଢୋଲିଆ। ଏଠାରେ କଉଡ଼ିକୁ ପାରିଶ୍ରମିକ ଅର୍ଥରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, କଷ୍ଟ ବା ଆଘାତ ଜଣଙ୍କ ଭାଗରେ ପଡ଼ୁଥିବାବେଳେ ତାହାର ଲାଭ ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣେ ପାଇବାର ଅମେଳକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ଦେଖାଏ।
entries.explanation: The same verb, ଖାଏ, links two very different receipts: blows for the instrument and cowries for the player. Read editorially, the image separates who bears the impact from who receives the proceeds. Its force lies in that unequal allocation.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A team bears the extra work and public criticism for a project while another person claims all the reward. Someone compares the arrangement to blows for the drum and payment for the drummer.
entries.cultural_context: The near-pair ଢୋଲ and ଢୋଲିଆ makes the two participants sound closely connected, while ମାଡ and କଉଡି sharply separate what each receives. Cowries provide the image of payment; the verse supplies no amount.

entries.title: The wary crow’s long life
entries.odia: ତରକିଲା କୁଆ ଶହେ ବରଷ ଜିଏଁ।
entries.literal_meaning: The wary crow lives a hundred years.
entries.meaning_odia: ତରକିଲା କୁଆ ଶହେ ବରଷ ବଞ୍ଚେ ବୋଲି ଢଗଟି କହୁଛି। ଏଠାରେ ତରକିଲାକୁ ଚମକି ଉଠୁଥିବା ବା ସତର୍କ ରହୁଥିବା ଅର୍ଥରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ବିପଦ ପ୍ରତି ସଜାଗ ରହିବା ନିଜକୁ ରକ୍ଷା କରିବାରେ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରେ। ଶହେ ବରଷ କହିବାଟି ଏହି ଭାବର ଜୋର, କୁଆର ଆୟୁଷର ବୈଜ୍ଞାନିକ ହିସାବ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: Wariness and a remarkably long life are placed together. Our editorial reading values noticing danger and responding to it, rather than dismissing every sign of caution as weakness. The hundred years is the saying’s emphatic promise, not a biological claim about crows.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A colleague pauses to check an unexpected request before acting on it and discovers a mistake. A friend recalls the wary crow to appreciate that caution.
entries.cultural_context: The single sentence gives watchfulness a memorable reward: a whole century of life. The crow is the figure carrying that lesson; the source supplies no particular encounter or origin story.

entries.title: Sweeping someone else’s doorway
entries.odia:
ତା ଦୁଆରେ ଖତ କୁଢ
ସିଏ ପର ଦୁଆର ଓଳଉଚି।
entries.literal_meaning: A heap of manure lies at their own doorway; they are sweeping someone else’s doorway.
entries.meaning_odia: ନିଜ ଦୁଆରେ ଖତର କୁଢ଼ ପଡ଼ିଛି, ଅଥଚ ସିଏ ପର ଦୁଆର ଓଳାଉଛି। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ନିଜ ଆଗରେ ଥିବା ଅବହେଳିତ କାମକୁ ଛାଡ଼ି ଅନ୍ୟର କାମ ସଜାଡ଼ିବାରେ ବ୍ୟସ୍ତ ହେବାର ଏହା ଚିତ୍ର। ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ସୁଧାରିବାକୁ ଯିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ନିଜ ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ଦେଖିବାର ଭାବ ଏଥିରୁ ବୁଝିହୁଏ।
entries.explanation: The two doorways make the contradiction visible: the person leaves a heap at home while putting effort into cleaning elsewhere. Our editorial reading is about neglected priorities, and by extension attending to others’ faults while leaving one’s own affairs unattended.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone repeatedly reorganises a colleague’s documents while leaving their own overdue work untouched. A friend compares that misplaced effort to sweeping another doorway with a heap at one’s own.
entries.cultural_context: The repetition of ଦୁଆର turns one everyday task into a comparison between here and elsewhere. The source specifies the neglected heap but gives no reason why the person has chosen the other doorway.

witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact spelling retained, including କୁଢ and ଓଳଉଚି. Literal reads heap and sweeping contextually; priorities explanation is editorial.

entries.title: Three hosts, an unfed guest
entries.odia: ତିନି ଘର କୁଣିଆ ଓପାସ ରହେ।
entries.literal_meaning: A guest of three households goes unfed.
entries.meaning_odia: ତିନି ଘରର କୁଣିଆ ହୋଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ଖାଇବାକୁ ନପାଇବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ଅନେକଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଭରସା ରହିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ କିଏ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଭାବରେ କାମଟି କରିବ ତାହା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନହେଲେ ଦରକାରୀ କାମ ଅକରା ରହିଯାଇପାରେ। ଜଣେ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଛାଡ଼ିଦେବା ଏହାକୁ ବୁଝାଇବାର ଏକ ଉଦାହରଣ; କାରଣଟି ମୂଳ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: Three households appear to offer more support than one, yet the guest still has no meal. Our editorial reading is that shared responsibility can fail when nobody clearly takes it on. The familiar scenario in which each host assumes another has provided food illustrates the saying; it is not narrated in the source.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Three colleagues each assume someone else has arranged lunch for a visitor. When the visitor is left waiting, one of them recalls the guest of three households.
entries.cultural_context: The contrast is numerical and practical: three households, but no meal. ଓପାସ is read here as remaining unfed, rather than undertaking a religious fast.

entries.title: Three-way care, a jackal’s feast
entries.odia:
ତିନି ଥେଣ୍ଟିଆ କାକୁଡି ଭାଡି
ଶିଆଳ ଖାଏ ମୋଡି ମାଡି।
entries.literal_meaning: A cucumber trellis under three-way care; a jackal eats, twisting and trampling.
entries.meaning_odia: ତିନିଜଣଙ୍କ ଦେଖାଶୁଣାରେ ଥିବା କାକୁଡ଼ି ଭାଡ଼ିକୁ ଶିଆଳ ମୋଡ଼ିମାଡ଼ି ଖାଉଛି—ଏହି ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗରେ ପ୍ରଥମ ଧାଡ଼ିକୁ ଏଭଳି ବୁଝାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ଅନେକଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ଦେଖାଶୁଣା ଠିକ୍ ନହେଲେ ସମ୍ପଦ ନଷ୍ଟ ହୋଇପାରେ।
entries.explanation: The crop is exposed to a jackal despite apparently having three-way care. Read editorially, the contrast concerns responsibility shared without effective protection. The rendering of ଥେଣ୍ଟିଆ is contextual: a related public expression describes three guardians, while this upload retains ଭାଡି, a raised support, rather than the public expression’s word for a garden.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Three teams share responsibility for checking a store, but none makes the inspection. After supplies are spoiled, someone recalls the cucumber trellis and the jackal.
entries.cultural_context: The jackal does more than take a neat share: the repeated actions suggest eating amid twisting and trampling. The image makes neglected protection visible as damage to a crop.

witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026. Missing ଣ୍ଟ cluster restored using the documented underlying PDF character mapping. Exact ଭାଡି retained. Three-way care and cucumber trellis are contextual renderings; the compound’s exact lexical formation remains uncertain. A partial public counterpart uses ବାଡ଼ି, not ଭାଡି.

entries.title: Your appeal, my son-in-law
entries.odia:
ତୁ ଗୁହାରି କରୁଚୁ ଯାହାକୁ
ମୁଁ ଜୁଆଇଁ କରିଚି ତାହାକୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: The person you are appealing to—I have made him my son-in-law.
entries.meaning_odia: ତୁମେ ଯାହାଙ୍କୁ ଗୁହାରି କରୁଛ, ସେ ମୋର ଜୁଆଇଁ—ଏହା କହି ବକ୍ତା ନିଜର ପାରିବାରିକ ସମ୍ପର୍କ ଦେଖାଉଛନ୍ତି। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ଏହା ନିଜ ପ୍ରଭାବର ଦାବି ଏବଂ ଗୁହାରି ଶୁଣୁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ ନିରପେକ୍ଷତାକୁ ନେଇ ସନ୍ଦେହର ଇଙ୍ଗିତ। ଗୁହାରିର ଫଳ କିନ୍ତୁ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The reply turns the other person’s hoped-for recourse into a claim of personal influence: the person hearing the appeal is the speaker’s son-in-law. Read editorially, the boast raises a question about impartiality. The saying supplies the relationship and the challenge, while leaving the outcome of the appeal unstated.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: During a disagreement, one person says they will ask a mutual acquaintance to intervene. The other boasts of a close family tie to that acquaintance, echoing this saying.
entries.cultural_context: The paired words ଯାହାକୁ and ତାହାକୁ point to the same person from two directions: someone receiving a plea and someone connected to the speaker by marriage. That shift supplies the force of the reply.

witnesses.locator: Page22, second item beginning ତୁ ଗୁହାରି.

entries.title: A royal mouth, an unprotected back
entries.odia: ତୁଣ୍ଡ ନରେନ୍ଦ୍ର, ପିଠି ଅରକ୍ଷିତ।
entries.literal_meaning: The mouth is a king; the back is unprotected.
entries.meaning_odia: ତୁଣ୍ଡରେ ରାଜାପରି ଦର୍ପ, କିନ୍ତୁ ପିଠି ଅରକ୍ଷିତ—ଏହି ବିରୋଧକୁ ଆମେ କଥାର ଦମ୍ଭ ଓ ତାହାର ପରିଣାମ ସାମ୍ନା କରିବାର ଅସହାୟତା ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ। ପାଠ-ଟୀକା: ମୂଳରେ ଥିବା ନତେନ୍ଦ୍ରକୁ ଅର୍ଥସଙ୍ଗତି ପାଇଁ ନରେନ୍ଦ୍ର ବୋଲି ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ଅନୁମାନରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି; ଅନ୍ୟ ପାଠରୁ ଏହି ସଂଶୋଧନ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହୋଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The mouth assumes royal authority while the back has no protection. Our editorial reading is that confident or domineering speech can exceed the speaker’s ability to face its consequences. Textual note: the uploaded ନତେନ୍ଦ୍ର is conjecturally read as ନରେନ୍ଦ୍ର, “king”; no second witness has confirmed that correction.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone makes sweeping demands on behalf of a group without checking whether anyone will support them. A colleague recalls the royal mouth and the unprotected back.
entries.cultural_context: Two parts of one body carry opposite conditions: authority at the mouth and vulnerability at the back. The compact contrast gives speech a power that the rest of the speaker may not possess.

witnesses.locator: Page22, third item beginning ତୁଣ୍ଡ.
witnesses.note: Original: ତୁଣ୍ଡ ନତେନ୍ଦ୍ର , ପିଠି ଅରକ୍ଷିତ। Display conjecturally changes ନତେନ୍ଦ୍ର to ନରେନ୍ଦ୍ର (king), a one-letter editorial correction without external confirmation; comma spacing regularised. ନତେନ୍ଦ୍ର→ନରେନ୍ଦ୍ର ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ଅନୁମାନ; ଅନ୍ୟ ପାଠରୁ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହୋଇନାହିଁ।

entries.title: Beyond branches, among leaves
entries.odia:
ତୁ ଗଲେ ଡାଳେ ଡାଳେ
ମୁଁ ଯିବି ପତରେ ପତରେ।
entries.literal_meaning: If you go from branch to branch, I shall go from leaf to leaf.
entries.meaning_odia: ତୁମେ ଡାଳେ ଡାଳେ ଗଲେ ମୁଁ ପତରେ ପତରେ ଯିବି—ଅର୍ଥାତ୍ ତୁମ ଚାଲର ଉତ୍ତରରେ ମୁଁ ଆହୁରି ସୂକ୍ଷ୍ମ ଚାଲ ଖେଳିପାରିବି ବୋଲି ବକ୍ତା ଦାବି କରୁଛନ୍ତି। ଏହା ପରସ୍ପରକୁ ଟପିଯିବାର ଆହ୍ୱାନ; ସଫଳତାର ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା ନୁହେଁ। ପାଠ-ଟୀକା: ମୂଳ ଜିବିକୁ ଯିବା କ୍ରିୟାର ମାନକ ରୂପ ଯିବି କରାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The response promises a more finely placed move for every move the other person makes. Branches give way to leaves: the speaker claims they cannot easily be outwitted. This is a challenge or boast, with no outcome narrated. Textual note: uploaded ଜିବି has been editorially regularised to ଯିବି, “I shall go.”
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: During a friendly strategy game, one player announces a clever plan. The other answers with the branch-and-leaf saying, promising an answer to every move.
entries.cultural_context: The repeated phrases give the two voices matching rhythms, while the shift from branch to leaf makes the reply sound more exact and nimble. No particular tree or literal journey is identified.

witnesses.locator: Page22, fifth item beginning ତୁ ଗଲେ ଡାଳେ ଡାଳେ.
witnesses.note: Original second line: ମୁଁ ଜିବି ପତରେ ପତରେ। Display changes ଜିବି→ଯିବି as an explicit editorial regularisation of the verb “go”; parallel grammar and a public counterpart with ଯିବା support the reading, not the exact replacement form. ମୂଳ ଜିବିକୁ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ଭାବେ ଯିବି କରାଯାଇଛି।

entries.title: Oil is oil, water is water
entries.odia: ତେଲ ତେଲ, ପାଣି ପାଣି।
entries.literal_meaning: Oil, oil; water, water.
entries.meaning_odia: ତେଲ ଓ ପାଣିର ନାମକୁ ଅଲଗା ଅଲଗା ଦୋହରାଯାଇଛି। ଆମର ବ୍ୟାପକ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ଦୁଇଟି ଭିନ୍ନ ଜିନିଷକୁ ଏକ କରି ନଦେଖି ସେମାନଙ୍କ ପାର୍ଥକ୍ୟ ଚିହ୍ନିବାର ଇଙ୍ଗିତ ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି। ମୂଳରେ କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଘଟଣା କିମ୍ବା ପ୍ରୟୋଗ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: Each substance is named twice, with a pause between the two. Our broad editorial reading is that different things keep distinguishable identities and should not simply be treated as the same. This reading draws on the familiar contrast between oil and water; a fixed traditional gloss has not been verified.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A discussion treats two quite different problems as though they were interchangeable. Someone repeats “oil, oil; water, water” to ask that the distinction be kept clear.
entries.cultural_context: The force lies in economy: four nouns, no stated action. Repetition gives the two substances separate verbal places, leaving a listener to supply the situation.

entries.title: Your wealth, another’s importance
entries.odia:
ତୋହରି ଧନ ତୋତେ ଦେଇ
ମଝିରେ ମଧ୍ୟସ୍ଥି ବୋଲାଇ।
entries.literal_meaning: Giving you your own wealth, and getting called the intermediary in between.
entries.meaning_odia: ତୁମରି ଧନ ତୁମକୁ ଦେଇ ଜଣେ ମଝିରେ ମଧ୍ୟସ୍ଥି ବୋଲାଉଛନ୍ତି। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ନିଜର କିଛି ଦେବା ବଦଳରେ ଅନ୍ୟର ସମ୍ପଦ ପହଞ୍ଚାଇ ନିଜ ଭୂମିକାର ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଦେଖାଇବାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ବିଦ୍ରୂପ କରାଯାଇଛି। ଧନର ମାଲିକ ଓ ତାହା ପାଉଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ଏକା ହୋଇଥିବାରୁ ଏହି ବିରୋଧଟି ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ହୁଏ।
entries.explanation: The money already belongs to the person receiving it, yet someone between owner and receipt acquires the title of intermediary. Our editorial reading hears a criticism of making one’s role seem important through someone else’s resources. The verse does not specify a fee, theft or the circumstances of the transfer.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A volunteer passes a club member their own deposited funds, then speaks as though this were a personal favour. Another member recalls the saying about giving someone their own wealth.
entries.cultural_context: ତୋହରି and ତୋତେ connect ownership and receipt to the same person. Against that direct connection, ମଝିରେ and ମଧ୍ୟସ୍ଥି repeatedly place another figure in the middle.

entries.title: The hand with means and without
entries.odia:
ଥିଲା ହାତ ଖଲ ଖଲ
ନଥିଲା ହାତ କଲବଲ
entries.literal_meaning: The hand with means is lively; the hand without is distressed.
entries.meaning_odia: ହାତରେ ସମ୍ବଳ ଥିବା ଓ ନଥିବାର ଦୁଇ ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ତୁଳନା କରାଯାଇଛି ବୋଲି ଆମେ ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ। ଖଲ ଖଲକୁ ଏଠାରେ ବ୍ୟାପକ ଭାବରେ ଚଞ୍ଚଳତା, କଲବଲକୁ କଷ୍ଟ ଭାବେ ବୁଝାଯାଇଛି। ସମ୍ବଳ ଥିଲେ କାମ କରିବାର ସୁବିଧା ଓ ନଥିଲେ ଅସୁବିଧା—ଏହା ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା।
entries.explanation: The two lines give the hand opposite conditions: animated when something is available, distressed when it is not. We read the unstated possession as means or resources, and the contrast as room to act versus the strain of shortage. “Lively” is a broad contextual rendering of ଖଲ ଖଲ; its precise expressive shade has not been independently established.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A small workshop can buy materials readily while funds are available, but struggles to keep working when payments are delayed. Someone recalls the contrast between the hand with means and the hand without.
entries.cultural_context: The near-rhyme ଖଲ ଖଲ / କଲବଲ makes the change in condition audible. The hand provides a concrete place to imagine what one has available and what one can do with it.

entries.title: A tiger’s fare, a snake’s fare
entries.odia:
ଥିଲେ ବାଘର ଆହାର
ନଥିଲେ ସାପର ଆହାର।
entries.literal_meaning: When there is [food], a tiger’s fare; when there is none, a snake’s fare.
entries.meaning_odia: ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଥିବା ଓ ନଥିବାର ଦୁଇ ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ଏହି ତୁଳନାରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ସମଧ୍ୱନିର ଏକ ସମ୍ପର୍କିତ ପାଠରେ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଅଂଶ ପବନ ଆହାର; ଲେଖିକା ତାହାକୁ ଅମଳ ପରର ପ୍ରଚୁର ଖାଇବା ଓ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ଅଭାବ ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗରେ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିଛନ୍ତି। ଏଠାରେ ମୂଳ ସାପର ଆହାର ରଖାଯାଇଛି; ସାପର ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ତାତ୍ପର୍ଯ୍ୟ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହୋଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: We read this as a contrast between plentiful eating and shortage, guided by a related expression in Dr Namita Sarangi’s Samadhwani article on winter and harvest. That version ends with air as food. The upload instead says “a snake’s fare,” which remains unchanged here; its precise figurative force is uncertain. The bracketed food makes the contextual completion visible.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A household uses its food stores freely when they are full and later has very little left. Someone recalls the contrast between fare in plenty and fare in scarcity.
entries.cultural_context: The inspected article uses its tiger-and-air version while discussing food consumed after harvest and a later shortage. That is an attested context for the related saying, not evidence of the uploaded snake image’s origin or an assertion about animal feeding.

witnesses.locator: Page23, sixth item beginning ଥିଲେ ବାଘର ଆହାର.
witnesses.note: Exact uploaded wording and line break retained. Food availability is a contextual reading; the precise nuance of ସାପର ଆହାର remains uncertain.

witnesses.locator: Paragraph discussing Pusha harvest, consumption and saving; line185 in inspected digital text.

entries.title: A thousand merits, but no character
entries.odia:
ଥିଲେ ଥାଉ ପଛେ ଗୁଣ ହଜାର
ଚରିତ୍ର ନଥିଲେ ସବୁ ଅସାର
entries.literal_meaning: Even if there are a thousand merits, without character they are all worthless.
entries.meaning_odia: ହଜାର ଗୁଣ ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ଚରିତ୍ର ନଥିଲେ ସେସବୁ ଅସାର—ଏହା ଏହି ବଚନର ଜୋରଦାର ମତ। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ଦକ୍ଷତା କିମ୍ବା ପ୍ରତିଭାକୁ ପ୍ରଶଂସା କଲାବେଳେ ସତତା ଓ ଆଚରଣକୁ ଅବହେଳା ନକରିବାର ତାଗିଦ ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି। ହଜାର ଓ ସବୁ ଅସାର କଥା ଦୁଇଟି ଏହି ତାଗିଦକୁ ତୀବ୍ର କରୁଛି।
entries.explanation: The saying makes a forceful moral claim: however many merits someone has, character is what gives them value. We read its emphasis as a reminder to consider integrity alongside skill or talent. “A thousand” and “all worthless” belong to the verse’s absolute rhetoric, rather than a measured assessment of a person’s whole worth.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A committee admires someone’s ability but also has to consider evidence of dishonesty. A member recalls this saying to insist that ability alone should not settle the decision.
entries.cultural_context: The contrast sets a large number of merits against one missing quality. The rhyme ହଜାର / ଅସାର turns that moral ranking into a short, memorable judgment.

entries.title: Fate’s rope, the human cow
entries.odia:
ଦଇବ ଦଉଡି ମଣିଷ ଗାଇ
ଯେଣିକି ଟାଣିବ ସେଣିକି ଯାଇ।
entries.literal_meaning: Fate is the rope, a human the cow; wherever it pulls, that way the cow goes.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦଇବକୁ ଦଉଡ଼ି ଓ ମଣିଷକୁ ସେହି ଦଉଡ଼ିରେ ଚାଲୁଥିବା ଗାଈ ସହ ତୁଳନା କରାଯାଇଛି। ଯେଉଁ ଦିଗକୁ ଟାଣ ଆସେ, ସେହି ଦିଗକୁ ଯିବାର ଚିତ୍ରରେ ବଚନଟି ଭାଗ୍ୟର ନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରଣକୁ ଜୋର ଦେଉଛି। ଏହା ବଚନର ଭାଗ୍ୟନିର୍ଭର ଦୃଷ୍ଟି; ମଣିଷର ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ଓ ଚେଷ୍ଟା ସର୍ବଦା ଅର୍ଥହୀନ ବୋଲି ଆମର ଦାବି ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The image gives fate the directing force of a rope and the human the place of the cow being led. It expresses a sense that life is pulled along by powers beyond one’s control. That fatalism belongs to the saying; the entry does not treat it as proof that choices or effort have no effect.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: An unexpected transfer changes someone’s plans for where to live. Describing the feeling of being carried in an unforeseen direction, they recall fate’s rope and the cow.
entries.cultural_context: The paired directions ଯେଣିକି and ସେଣିକି make the movement follow the pull. The concrete tethering image turns an abstract idea of fate into something felt as direction and constraint.

entries.title: A month of promises, still tomorrow
entries.odia:
ଦେବୁ ଦେବୁ ବୋଲି ପୂରିଲା ମାସେ
ଆହୁରି ବୋଲୁଚୁ କାଲିକି ଆ’ସେ।
entries.literal_meaning: A month has passed with you saying you will give; still you say, “Come tomorrow.”
entries.meaning_odia: ଦେବୁ ବୋଲି ବାରମ୍ବାର କହିବାରେ ମାସେ ବିତିଗଲା, ତଥାପି କାଲି ଆସିବାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉଛି। ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ପୂରଣ ନହୋଇ ଦିନ ଗଡ଼ିଚାଲିବା ପ୍ରତି ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରୁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ ଅସନ୍ତୋଷ ଏଥିରେ ପ୍ରକାଶ ପାଉଛି। କଣ ଦେବାକୁ କୁହାଯାଇଥିଲା, ମୂଳ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ତାହା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: Repeated assurances have turned into a month of waiting, yet the answer remains “tomorrow.” The complaint is about a promise continually pushed ahead instead of fulfilled. The verse leaves the promised thing unnamed, so its force can extend beyond any one kind of transaction.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone has repeatedly promised to provide material for a shared project. After weeks of being asked to return the next day, the waiting colleague recalls this saying.
entries.cultural_context: The repeated ଦେବୁ makes the assurance sound habitual. A whole month in the first line is set against one more tomorrow in the second, giving the delay its sharpness.

entries.title: Curd with rice, a flower in the hair
entries.odia:
ଦହି ସୁନ୍ଦର ଚୂଡ଼ାକୁ
ଫୁଲ ସୁନ୍ଦର ଜୁଡ଼ାକୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: Curd suits flattened rice; a flower suits a hair bun.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚୂଡ଼ା ସହ ଦହି ଓ ଜୁଡ଼ାରେ ଫୁଲ—ଦୁଇଟି ମାନିଯାଉଥିବା ଯୋଡ଼ିକୁ ଏଠାରେ ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ଉପଯୁକ୍ତ ସାଥି କିମ୍ବା ଉପାଦାନ ମିଳିଲେ ଜିନିଷର ଆକର୍ଷଣ ବଢ଼େ। ଏଠାରେ ସୁନ୍ଦର କେବଳ ଦେଖିବାର ସୌନ୍ଦର୍ଯ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ, ପରସ୍ପରକୁ ମାନିବାର ଭାବ ମଧ୍ୟ ବହନ କରୁଛି।
entries.explanation: The two lines pair a food with its accompaniment and a hairstyle with an ornament. Our editorial reading is that a well-matched addition brings out the appeal of what it accompanies. The verse’s parallel structure links the pleasure of a fitting food combination with the beauty of a fitting adornment.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: An illustration and a short poem work especially well together. An editor recalls the pairing of curd with flattened rice and a flower with a hair bun.
entries.cultural_context: The rhyme ଚୂଡ଼ାକୁ / ଜୁଡ଼ାକୁ joins eating and adornment in one compact comparison. The verse names the pairings without specifying an occasion or prescribing how either must be prepared.

entries.title: One sickle, many handles
entries.odia: ଦାଆ ଥିଲେ ଅଠର ଗଣ୍ଡା ବେଣ୍ଟ।
entries.literal_meaning: If there is a sickle, there are eighteen ganda of handles.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦାଆ ଥିଲେ ତାହା ପାଇଁ ଅଠର ଗଣ୍ଡା ବେଣ୍ଟ—ଏହି ତୁଳନାରେ ମୂଳ ଉପକରଣ ଓ ତାହାର ଅନେକ ବେଣ୍ଟକୁ ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ମୂଳ ଜିନିଷ ଥିଲେ ତାହାର ଆନୁଷଙ୍ଗିକ ଅଂଶ ପାଇଁ ଅନେକ ବିକଳ୍ପ ମିଳିପାରେ। ଗଣ୍ଡା ଗଣନା ଏକକଟିକୁ ମୂଳ ରୂପରେ ରଖାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The sickle is singular in the condition; handles follow in abundance. Our editorial reading puts the central implement before any particular fitting: when the main thing is available, an accessory may have many alternatives. The source’s eighteen ganda is retained as a counting expression, without converting it into a modern total.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A group has secured its main equipment but worries that one minor fitting must be replaced. Someone recalls the sickle and its many handles to keep the difficulty in proportion.
entries.cultural_context: The verse distinguishes the cutting implement from its handle. Its exaggerated plurality gives the handle a different weight from the thing it serves; it does not describe a particular workshop or farming occasion.

entries.title: A stumble outside, a broken stone at home
entries.odia:
ଦାଣ୍ଡରେ ପଥର ଝୁଣ୍ଟିଚି
ଘରେ ଶିଳ ଭାଙ୍ଗୁଚି।
entries.literal_meaning: Someone has stumbled over a stone in the road; at home, they are breaking the grinding slab.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦାଣ୍ଡରେ ପଥରରେ ଝୁଣ୍ଟିବା ପରେ ଘରର ଶିଳ ଭାଙ୍ଗିବାର ଦୁଇଟି କାମ ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ଗୋଟିଏ ଜାଗାର ବିରକ୍ତି ଆଉ ଗୋଟିଏ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦୋଷ ଜିନିଷ ଉପରେ ସୁଝାଇବାର ଅସଂଗତି ଏଠାରେ ଦିଶୁଛି। ରାଗ କଥାଟି ମୂଳରେ ନାହିଁ; କାମ ଦୁଇଟିର ସମ୍ପର୍କରୁ ଏହି ଅର୍ଥ କରାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The stone that caused the stumble is outside; the stone being broken is a useful household grinding slab. We read the mismatch as displaced anger: frustration with one thing is taken out on another. The verse gives the two actions, while this emotional link is editorial interpretation.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After an irritating delay outside, someone comes home and angrily damages an unrelated object. Another person recalls the road stone and the grinding slab.
entries.cultural_context: Both objects are stone, but they occupy different places and serve different purposes. That superficial resemblance makes the retaliation intelligible as a comic mistake without making it reasonable.

entries.title: A donor with too little cloth
entries.odia: ଦାନୀ, ନା ମୁଣ୍ଡକୁ ନପାଏ କାନି ।
entries.literal_meaning: A generous donor—and the cloth end does not reach the head.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦାନୀ ବୋଲି ପରିଚୟ, ଅଥଚ ମୁଣ୍ଡ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ କାନି ପହଞ୍ଚୁନାହିଁ—ଏହି ଅମେଳକୁ ଆମେ ଏଠାରେ ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ। ନିଜ ସମ୍ବଳର ଅଭାବ ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ଉଦାରତାର ବଡ଼ ପରିଚୟ ରଖିଲେ ଯେଉଁ ବିରୋଧ ଦିଶେ, ତାହା ଏହାର ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ ହୋଇପାରେ। ଦାନ କରି କରି ଅଭାବ ହୋଇଛି ବୋଲି ମୂଳରେ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The label “generous donor” stands beside a cloth end too short to reach the head. Our editorial reading hears irony in a claim of generosity set against inadequate means. The line does not say that anything has actually been donated or that giving caused the shortage. The conversational ନା is rendered broadly through the turn marked by the English dash.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone advertises themselves as a major benefactor while having no supplies available for their own proposed work. A listener recalls the donor whose cloth does not reach the head.
entries.cultural_context: The cloth end makes insufficiency visible in a small physical detail. Its short reach is set against the largeness of the donor label; no particular dress rule or ceremony is specified.

entries.title: After the deity and its seat
entries.odia:
ଦିଅଁଙ୍କୁ ଖାଇ, ଖଟୁଲି ଖାଇ
ଆହୁରି ପଚାରେ ପୂଜାରୀ କାହିଁ।
entries.literal_meaning: Having devoured the deity and the little seat, still asking, “Where is the priest?”
entries.meaning_odia: ଦିଅଁ ଓ ଖଟୁଲି ଖାଇସାରି ମଧ୍ୟ ପୂଜାରୀ କାହିଁ ବୋଲି ପଚାରିବାର ଅତିରଞ୍ଜିତ ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ବହୁତ କିଛି ନେଇସାରି ମଧ୍ୟ ଆହୁରି ଚାହିଁବାର ଅତୃପ୍ତି ଏଥିରେ ଦିଶେ। ଶେଷ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ଆଉ ଏକ ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ ଖୋଜାଯାଉଛି; ପୂଜାରୀଙ୍କୁ ଖାଇଦେଲା ବୋଲି ଧାଡ଼ିଟି କହୁନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The appetite has already passed through the deity and its little seat, yet the question seeks someone else. Our editorial reading is of acquisitiveness that does not stop after consuming what is available. The grotesque escalation gives the saying its force; it is not a report of an actual event.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone takes nearly all the shared supplies and immediately asks what else is available. A colleague recalls the saying’s appetite that still looks for another target.
entries.cultural_context: Deity, seat and priest form a connected sequence. The first two have been consumed in the image; the last remains the object of a question, making the appetite seem unfinished. ଖଟୁଲି is a small cot or seat, read here in the deity’s setting.

witnesses.locator: Page24, seventh item beginning ଦିଅଁଙ୍କୁ ଖାଇ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact wording retained. Small seat is contextual ଖଟୁଲି rendering based on small-cot sense. Exaggerated appetite/greed explanation is editorial, not a claim about a recorded event.
