entries.title: The giver and the long-awaited sweets
entries.odia:
ଦିଆ ପୁରୁଷ
ଯାଚି ଯାଉଥିଲା କଟକ ମିଠେଇ
ପୁଅକୁ ହେଲାଣି ବାର ବରଷ।
entries.literal_meaning: A giving man—he kept offering Cuttack sweets; the son is already twelve years old.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦେବାଲୋକ ବୋଲି ପରିଚୟ, କଟକ ମିଠେଇର ଯାଚନା, ଆଉ ପୁଅକୁ ବାର ବରଷ ହୋଇଗଲାଣି—ଏହି ତିନୋଟି କଥା ପାଖାପାଖି ରହିଛି। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, କଥାରେ ଦେବାକୁ କହି ସମୟ ଗଡ଼ାଇଦେବା ପ୍ରତି ଏହା ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ। ପୁଅର ବୟସ ସମୟ ବିତିବାର ଇଙ୍ଗିତ ଦିଏ; ଜନ୍ମବେଳେ ଯାଚିଥିଲା ବୋଲି ମୂଳରେ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The opening calls someone a giver, but the concrete act remains an offer of sweets, followed by the observation that the son is already twelve. We read the juxtaposition as irony about an offer that has lingered unfulfilled. The child’s age supplies a sense of time passing; it does not establish when the offer began or whose child is meant.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone repeatedly offers to bring a small gift, but familiar occasions pass without it appearing. A friend recalls the giver who kept offering Cuttack sweets.
entries.cultural_context: Cuttack names the sweets offered, while the boy’s age makes time tangible. The verse supplies no festival, birth celebration or particular confection, and none is needed for its contrast between a generous-sounding offer and delay.

witnesses.locator: Page24, ninth item beginning ଦିଆ ପୁରୁଷ.

entries.title: Remembering aunt only at the festival
entries.odia:
ଦିନେ ନାଇଁ କାଳେ ନାଇଁ
ଗହ୍ମା ପୁନିଅଁକୁ ମାଇଁ ମାଇଁ।
entries.literal_meaning: Not on any day, not at any time—but at Gahma full moon, “Aunt, aunt!”
entries.meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟ ସମୟରେ ଖୋଜଖବର ନାହିଁ, ଗହ୍ମା ପୁନିଅଁ ଆସିଲେ ମାଇଁ ମାଇଁ ଡାକ—ଏହି ଅମେଳକୁ ଆମେ ଏଠାରେ ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ। ନିୟମିତ ସମ୍ପର୍କ କିମ୍ବା ଯତ୍ନ ନରଖି କେବଳ ଏକ ଅବସରରେ ଆଗ୍ରହ ଦେଖାଇବାକୁ ଏହା ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରେ। କୌଣସି ଖାଦ୍ୟ କିମ୍ବା ଉପହାର ପାଇଁ ଡାକୁଛି ବୋଲି ମୂଳରେ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: Ordinary absence gives way to repeated affectionate address at a festival. We read this as criticism of attention that appears only for an occasion instead of being sustained. The verse leaves the reason for addressing the aunt unstated.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A group ignores a shared concern throughout the year but makes a great display of it on a special day. Someone recalls the aunt remembered only at Gahma full moon.
entries.cultural_context: Gahma full moon provides a named occasion against the open-ended “not on any day, not at any time.” The repeated ମାଇଁ makes the sudden recognition audible; the verse does not explain any particular festival exchange.

witnesses.locator: Page24, eleventh item beginning ଦିନେ ନାଇଁ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload and comparison inspected17November2026; exact ଗହ୍ମା ପୁନିଅଁକୁ and ନାଇଁ retained. Usual absence versus occasional attention is contextual reading; no gift or ritual obligation inferred.

entries.title: Oily hands from tending the lamp
entries.odia: ଦୀପ ତେଜିଲେ ହାତ ଚିକ୍କଣ।
entries.literal_meaning: When you brighten the lamp, your hand becomes oily.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୀପକୁ ତେଜିବା ବେଳେ ହାତରେ ତେଲ ଲାଗି ଚିକ୍କଣ ହେବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏଠାରେ ଅଛି। ଅନ୍ୟର ଅର୍ଥ ବା ସମ୍ପଦର କାରବାର ସମ୍ଭାଳୁଥିବା ଲୋକ ନିଜେ ମଧ୍ୟ କିଛି ଲାଭ ପାଇବାର ଇଙ୍ଗିତ ଭାବେ ଏହାକୁ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇପାରେ। ଯାଞ୍ଚ କରାଯାଇଥିବା ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟରେ ଏହିପରି ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ଅଛି। ମୂଳ ପିଡିଏଫ୍‌ର ତେଳିଲେ ବଦଳରେ ସେହି ପ୍ରକାଶିତ ପାଠର ତେଜିଲେ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The hand that tends the lamp comes away with some of its oil. The inspected editorial applies this image to personal gain while arranging expenditure. Our broader reading is that handling resources can bring a benefit to the handler; the saying can carry suspicion about that benefit.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A person entrusted with arranging purchases quietly secures an advantage for themselves. An observer recalls the oily hand that has been tending the lamp.
entries.cultural_context: The image makes contact visible: the lamp is brighter, but oil remains on the hand that tended it. That residue becomes an image of benefit retained by someone managing another matter.

witnesses.locator: Page24, twelfth item beginning ଦୀପ.
witnesses.note: Uploaded wording is ଦୀପ ତେଳିଲେ ହାତ ଚିକ୍କଣ। Display changes only ତେଳିଲେ to ତେଜିଲେ using the cited public counterpart; this is an explicit editorial repair, not the uploaded visual reading. ମୂଳର ତେଳିଲେ ବଦଳରେ ପ୍ରକାଶିତ ସମାନ ପାଠର ତେଜିଲେ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରାଯାଇଛି।

entries.title: When the lamp’s oil runs out
entries.odia:
ଦୀପରୁ ମାଲପା ସଇଲା
ପ୍ରଭୁଙ୍କ ଲୀଳା ଶେଷ ହେଲା।
entries.literal_meaning: The oil in the lamp ran out; the Lord’s play came to an end.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୀପରୁ ତେଲ ସରିଯିବା ସହ ପ୍ରଭୁଙ୍କ ଲୀଳା ଶେଷ ହେବାକୁ ଏହି ଦୁଇ ଧାଡ଼ି ଯୋଡ଼ିଛି। ଯେଉଁ ସାଧନ ଉପରେ କୌଣସି କାମ ନିର୍ଭର କରେ, ସେହି ସାଧନ ସରିଲେ କାମ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅଟକିଯାଏ—ଏହା ଆମର ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠ। ମାଲପାର ଅର୍ଥ ତେଲ; ମୂଳ ବନାନ ବଦଳାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The first line names a small material supply; the second announces an ending in the larger language of divine play. Our editorial reading notices dependence: an activity comes to a halt when what sustains it runs out. The verse itself leaves the particular occasion unspecified.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: An ambitious programme stops as soon as its supplies are exhausted. Someone recalls the lamp whose oil ran out and brought the play to an end.
entries.cultural_context: The pairing of lamp oil with the Lord’s play gives the ending its force. A modest material limit stands beside a grand expression of activity, making dependence on support visible.

witnesses.locator: Page25, second item beginning ଦୀପରୁ ମାଲପା.

entries.title: The ones in between drown
entries.odia:
ଦୃଢ଼େ ତରନ୍ତି
ମୂଢେ ତରନ୍ତି
ମଝି ମଝିଆ ବୁଡି ମରନ୍ତି।
entries.literal_meaning: The steadfast cross over; the foolish cross over; those in between drown and die.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୃଢ଼ ଲୋକ ଓ ମୂଢ଼ ଲୋକ—ଦୁହେଁ ତରିଯାଆନ୍ତି, ଅଥଚ ମଝି ଅବସ୍ଥାରେ ଥିବା ଲୋକ ବୁଡ଼ିଯାଆନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ଧାଡ଼ିଗୁଡ଼ିକ କହୁଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ଅଧା ବୁଝାମଣା ଓ ଅନିଶ୍ଚିତ ସ୍ଥିତିକୁ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରେ। ମୂଢ଼ତାରେ ସଫଳତା ମିଳେ ବୋଲି କହିବା ଏହି ଢଗର ବିରୋଧାଭାସ; ଏହା ଅଜ୍ଞତାକୁ ଉପଦେଶ କିମ୍ବା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବାକୁ ବାରଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: Two unlike groups reach the other side, while the people between them drown. Our editorial reading hears a pointed contrast between a settled position and an insecure halfway understanding. The surprising success assigned to the foolish gives the saying its paradox; it need not be taken as advice to remain ignorant.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone adopts half of a method, questions the rest without understanding it, and cannot make it work. An observer recalls the people in between who fail to cross.
entries.cultural_context: The repeated ତରନ୍ତି sets up two safe crossings before the last line overturns that rhythm with drowning. A three-part contrast, rather than a simple praise of wisdom, makes the saying memorable.

witnesses.locator: Page25, fourth item beginning ଦୃଢ଼େ ତରନ୍ତି.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; three-line wording retained, including original nukta differences. Crossing and drowning translated literally; discussion of halfway understanding is editorial. Specific original setting not established.

entries.title: What is given and what is kept
entries.odia:
ଦେଇଚୁ ଯାହା ପରଲୋକକୁ
ଥୋଇଚୁ ଯାହା ପରଲୋକକୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: What you have given is for the next world; what you have kept is for other people. [Editorial wordplay reading of the repeated ପରଲୋକକୁ.]
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୁଇ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ଏକେ ପରଲୋକକୁ ଶବ୍ଦ ଅଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ପ୍ରଥମଟି ପରଲୋକ ବା ଆରପାରି, ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟଟି ପର ଲୋକ ବା ଅନ୍ୟ ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ବୁଝାଏ। ଏହି ଶବ୍ଦଖେଳରେ ଦାନର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଓ ସାଇତି ରଖିଥିବା ଜିନିଷ ଅନ୍ୟଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ରହିଯିବାର ଭାବକୁ ତୁଳନା କରାଯାଇଛି। ଏହା ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା; ମୂଳ ଶବ୍ଦ ବଦଳାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The two endings look identical, but can be heard differently: the next world in one line, other people in the next. Read this way, giving carries value beyond possession, while what is stored remains for someone else. This is our editorial interpretation of the verbal contrast, not a verified traditional gloss.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: In a discussion about keeping every possession rather than helping others, someone quotes these two lines and draws attention to their possible double meaning.
entries.cultural_context: The contrast rests on a change of sense within the same sound, ପରଲୋକ. Giving and keeping introduce two possible destinations without changing the written ending. The next-world reference supplies the saying’s religious horizon in this reading.

witnesses.locator: Page25, fifth item beginning ଦେଇଚୁ ଯାହା.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026. Both printed ପରଲୋକକୁ endings retained; extra interword space normalised only. Translation reads next world versus other people as an explicitly editorial pun. No external full-proverb gloss verified. ଏକେ ଶବ୍ଦର ଦୁଇ ଅର୍ଥ ନେବା ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା; ପାଠର ସଂଶୋଧନ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: The good-looking gourd badi
entries.odia: ଦେଖା ସୁନ୍ଦର କଖାରୁ ବଡି।
entries.literal_meaning: Beautiful to look at—a gourd badi.
entries.meaning_odia: କଖାରୁ ବଡ଼ିର ଦେଖିବା ସୁନ୍ଦର ବୋଲି ଏହି ସଂକ୍ଷିପ୍ତ ପଦ କହୁଛି। ବାହାର ଦେଖାର ପ୍ରଶଂସାକୁ ଧରି ଏହାକୁ ଆମେ ଏଠାରେ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ: ଦେଖିବାକୁ ଭଲ ଲାଗିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅନ୍ୟ ଗୁଣର ବିଚାର ବାକି ରହେ। ଏହି ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ବଡ଼ିର ସ୍ୱାଦ କିମ୍ବା ଖାଦ୍ୟଗୁଣ ସମ୍ପର୍କରେ ରାୟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The phrase offers praise specifically for appearance. Our editorial reading hears a reservation within that limited praise: looking attractive does not settle the question of quality. The food supplies the comparison; the verse does not actually describe its taste.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A proposal arrives in an elegant presentation, but its practical details remain weak. Someone responds with the comparison to a good-looking gourd badi.
entries.cultural_context: Badi names a dried pulse-based food preparation; this one includes gourd. The saying draws its compact image from a recognisable food and places all its expressed praise on how it looks.

entries.english_summary: Attractive appearance alone does not establish quality.

entries.title: A fine-looking cow, not a drop of milk
entries.odia:
ଦେଖା ସୁନ୍ଦର ବଉଳା ଗାଈ
ଦୁହିଁଲା ବେଳକୁ ଟୋପାଏ ନାହିଁ।
entries.literal_meaning: Baula the cow looks beautiful; when milked, not a drop [of milk].
entries.meaning_odia: ବଉଳା ଗାଈ ଦେଖିବାକୁ ସୁନ୍ଦର, କିନ୍ତୁ ଦୁହିଁବା ବେଳେ ଟୋପାଏ କ୍ଷୀର ମଧ୍ୟ ମିଳୁନାହିଁ। ଦେଖାରୁ ହୋଇଥିବା ଭଲ ଧାରଣା ଓ କାମ ବେଳର ଫଳ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଏଠାରେ ଅମେଳ ଅଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ବାହାର ଆକର୍ଷଣ ଦେଖି ଉପଯୋଗିତା ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ କରିବାକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ।
entries.explanation: The first line invites admiration; the second puts that impression to a practical test and finds no milk. Our editorial reading concerns an attractive presentation that fails to deliver the expected result. Unlike an unspecified reservation about appearance, the verse states exactly what is missing.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A beautifully presented tool proves unable to perform its basic task. Someone compares it to the fine-looking cow that yields no milk.
entries.cultural_context: Milking turns visual praise into a concrete test. The tiny measure ଟୋପାଏ, a single drop, makes the absence emphatic. Baula is retained as the cow’s designation without supplying a breed or a story about it.

witnesses.locator: Page25, seventh item beginning ଦେଖା ସୁନ୍ଦର ବଉଳା.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact two-line text retained. Baula is carried into English as a cow designation/name; no breed, colour or story identity inferred. Milk in the literal translation is supplied by the explicit milking context.

entries.title: Giving praised, asking disparaged
entries.odia:
ଦେବା ଠାରୁ ପୁଣ୍ୟ ନାହିଁ
ମାଗିବା ଠାରୁ ହୀନ ନାହିଁ।
entries.literal_meaning: Nothing is more meritorious than giving; nothing is lower than asking.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦେବାକୁ ସବୁଠୁ ପୁଣ୍ୟର କାମ ଓ ମାଗିବାକୁ ସବୁଠୁ ହୀନ କାମ ବୋଲି ଏହି ଢଗ କହେ। ଏହା ଦାନକୁ ପ୍ରଶଂସା କରିବା ସହ ସହାୟତା ମାଗିବାକୁ ଛୋଟ କରୁଥିବା ଏକ ମୂଲ୍ୟବୋଧକୁ ଦେଖାଏ। ଏହି ମୂଲ୍ୟବିଚାର ମୂଳ କଥାର; ସହାୟତା ଦରକାର ହେବାରୁ କାହାର ମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦା କମେ ନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The parallel lines put giving at the top of a moral scale and asking at the bottom. The praise of generosity therefore comes with a harsh judgement of dependence. Read critically, the saying reveals that hierarchy; it does not establish why anyone asks for help or diminish their dignity.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: In a discussion about charity, someone quotes the saying to praise giving. Another participant points out that generosity can be valued without shaming the person who needs it.
entries.cultural_context: The word ପୁଣ୍ୟ gives the first line a moral and religious register, while ହୀନ supplies the opposing judgement in the second. Repeating ଠାରୁ and ନାହିଁ makes both claims absolute.

witnesses.locator: Page25, eighth item beginning ଦେବା ଠାରୁ ପୁଣ୍ୟ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact two-line text retained. Comparative syntax translated as nothing more meritorious/nothing lower. Critical response to the stigma of asking is editorial.

entries.title: Keep saying yes to giving
entries.odia:
ଦେବା ଦେବା କହୁଥିବା
ନାହିଁ ନଦେବା ନକରିବା।
entries.literal_meaning: Keep saying, “We will give, we will give”; do not answer, “No, we will not give.” [Editorial parsing of the compressed second line.]
entries.meaning_odia: ଦେବା ଦେବା ବୋଲି କହୁଥିବା, ନାହିଁ ଦେବୁ ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ଉତ୍ତର ନକରିବା—ଏପରି ଭାବେ ଆମେ ଏଠାରେ ସଂକ୍ଷିପ୍ତ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଧାଡ଼ିକୁ ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ। ଏହି ପାଠରେ କଥାଟି ସିଧାସଳଖ ମନା କରିବା ବଦଳରେ ସକାରାତ୍ମକ ଆଶ୍ୱାସନ ଦେବାକୁ ନେଇ। ପ୍ରକୃତରେ ଦେଲେ କି ନାହିଁ ମୂଳରେ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The repeated positive answer is set against a refusal that should not be spoken. Our editorial parsing reads the line as a formula for keeping the answer agreeable. It could sound reassuring or evasive in different situations; the wording alone does not settle whether the promise is carried out.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: During a discussion of a request, someone recalls this saying about continuing to say yes. Another asks what practical commitment those assurances will mean.
entries.cultural_context: Repetition gives ଦେବା the sound of a ready assurance. The second line packs several negatives together; this translation treats “no, we will not give” as the reply being ruled out, while retaining the source text unchanged.

witnesses.locator: Page25, ninth item beginning ଦେବା ଦେବା.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact two-line wording retained. Quoted-answer boundaries in English are an editorial parsing of the compressed second line, not printed punctuation. Neither fulfilment nor deliberate non-fulfilment is asserted. ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଧାଡ଼ିର ଉତ୍ତର-ରୂପ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ; ମୂଳ ପାଠ ବଦଳାଯାଇନାହିଁ।

entries.title: Whose wealth, whose greed
entries.odia: ଧନ ଯା’ର, ଲୋଭ ତା’ର।
entries.literal_meaning: Whoever owns the wealth owns the greed.
entries.meaning_odia: ଧନ ଯାହାର, ଲୋଭ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହାର ବୋଲି ଏହି ସଂକ୍ଷିପ୍ତ କଥା କହେ। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଧନ ଥିବା ଓ ତାହା ପ୍ରତି ଆସକ୍ତିକୁ ଏହା ଏକାଠି ରଖେ। କାହାର କେତେ ଧନ ବା କେଉଁ ଜିନିଷ ପାଇଁ ଲୋଭ ମୂଳରେ ନାହିଁ; ସବୁ ସମ୍ପତ୍ତିଧାରୀଙ୍କ ଚରିତ୍ର ବିଷୟରେ ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The matching phrases make greed seem another possession belonging to the wealth-holder. Our editorial reading notices the attachment that can accompany having something, rather than assuming that possession ends desire. The saying compresses that observation into a generalisation; it supplies no measure of wealth or particular act of greed.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: The owner of a well-stocked store cannot bear to part with a small surplus. Someone recalls this pairing of possession and greed.
entries.cultural_context: The force lies in the mirrored possessives ଯା’ର and ତା’ର. Wealth is named first, and greed follows as though it belonged in the same account.

witnesses.locator: Page25, tenth item beginning ଧନ ଯା’ର.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact wording and punctuation retained. Attachment reading is editorial; quantity of wealth and object of desire are unspecified.

entries.title: Honesty without an opportunity
entries.odia: ଧନ ନ ପଡିଲେ ଚୋର ବି ସାଧୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: If wealth does not come [within reach], even a thief is honest.
entries.meaning_odia: ଧନ ହାତକୁ ଆସିବାର ସୁଯୋଗ ନଥିଲେ ଚୋର ମଧ୍ୟ ସାଧୁ ପରି ରହେ ବୋଲି ଏହି କଥା କହୁଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ସୁଯୋଗ ନମିଳିବା ଓ ସୁଯୋଗ ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅସାଧୁ କାମ ନକରିବା ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଫରକ ଅଛି। ଏଠାରେ ଧନ ନଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଚୋର କୁହାଯାଉନାହିଁ; ମୂଳର ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଚୋର ବୋଲି ବର୍ଣ୍ଣିତ।
entries.explanation: The condition comes before the praise: nothing tempting has come within reach. Our editorial reading distinguishes conduct that has faced an opportunity from conduct that has never been tested by one. The line’s thief is already identified as such; it is not evidence for accusing an untested person of dishonesty.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone is praised for never misusing funds they have never handled. Another person recalls the saying and asks whether that record actually demonstrates restraint.
entries.cultural_context: ଚୋର and ସାଧୁ create a sharp moral opposition within one short sentence. The missing opportunity, expressed by ଧନ ନ ପଡିଲେ, makes it possible for the same figure to occupy both descriptions.

witnesses.locator: Page25, eleventh and final item beginning ଧନ ନ ପଡିଲେ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact wording retained. Within reach is a marked contextual completion of ପଡିଲେ. Honesty-versus-untested-conduct discussion is editorial; no specific custody or transaction inferred.

entries.title: Tough only before his wife
entries.odia:
ଧାଇଁ ନପାରଇ ପାଇକ ଆଗେ
ଟାଣ କରୁଥାଇ ମାଇପ ଆଗେ।
entries.literal_meaning: He cannot rush forward before a soldier, but keeps acting tough before his wife.
entries.meaning_odia: ପାଇକ ଆଗରେ ଧାଇଁ ପାରୁନଥିବା ଲୋକ ମାଇପ ଆଗରେ ଟାଣ ଦେଖାଉଛି—ଏହି ଦୁଇ ପରିସ୍ଥିତିର ଅମେଳ ଏଠାରେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ବାହାରେ ସାହସ ଦେଖାଇ ନପାରି ଘରେ ପତ୍ନୀଙ୍କ ଆଗରେ କଠୋରତା ଦେଖାଇବାକୁ ଏହା ଉପହାସ କରେ। ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ପତ୍ନୀଙ୍କୁ ଦମନ କରିବାର ଅଧିକାର ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The same person changes his bearing with the person facing him: unable to rush forward before a soldier, forceful before his wife. Our editorial reading targets selective courage and domestic swagger. The contrast makes the show of toughness look less convincing, rather than making it a model of strength.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone avoids standing up to an intimidating outsider, then tries to sound commanding at home. A listener recalls the contrast between the soldier and the wife.
entries.cultural_context: The repeated ଆଗେ places two audiences side by side. The source’s colloquial ମାଇପ supplies the domestic setting; its paired structure directs attention to the man’s change of conduct.

entries.title: The day went in sorting grains
entries.odia:
ଧାନ ଗୋଟି ଗୋଟି
ଖଇ ଗୋଟି ଗୋଟି
ବାଛୁ ବାଛୁ ଦିନ ସରିଲା
ବାପାଙ୍କୁ କହିବ
ହଡା ନ ବିକିବ
ବାବାଜି ହୋଇବା ନୋହିଲା।
entries.literal_meaning: Paddy grain by grain, popped rice piece by piece—the day ended in sorting. Tell father not to sell the old bullock; becoming an ascetic did not work out.
entries.meaning_odia: ଧାନ ଓ ଖଇ ଗୋଟି ଗୋଟି ବାଛିବାରେ ଦିନ ସରିଗଲା। ତା’ପରେ ବାପାଙ୍କୁ ହଡ଼ା ନବିକିବାକୁ କହିବା ଓ ବାବାଜି ହେବା ନହେବାର କଥା ଆସୁଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏକ ବଡ଼ ଇଚ୍ଛା ସହ ଧୈର୍ଯ୍ୟ ଲୋଡ଼ୁଥିବା ଛୋଟ କାମର ମୁହାଁମୁହିଁ ହେବାର ହାସ୍ୟ ଅଛି। ହଡ଼ା ବିକ୍ରିର କଥା କାହିଁକି ଥିଲା ବା କେଉଁଠି ଏ କାମ ହେଉଥିଲା ମୂଳରେ ନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The opening makes the work feel slow: one grain, then another, until the day is gone. The ending abruptly turns to a message home and an aspiration that has not worked out. Our editorial reading hears the comic gap between a large ambition and the patient work encountered along the way, without supplying an untold story about the bullock.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone is attracted to a new vocation but gives up after meeting its repetitive daily tasks. A friend recalls the day spent sorting grains before the announcement that becoming an ascetic did not work out.
entries.cultural_context: The six short lines move from repeated small actions to the practical instruction not to sell an animal. That change of scale gives the ending its comic weight; the named ascetic role provides the aspiration, not a description of a verified monastic routine.

witnesses.locator: Page26, second item beginning ଧାନ ଗୋଟି ଗୋଟି.

entries.title: A blow when someone is bowed down
entries.odia:
ନଇଁ ପଡିଥିବ ଯେତିକି ବେଳେ
ବିଧାଏ ମାରିବ ସେତିକି ବେଳେ।
entries.literal_meaning: Just when someone is bent down, give them a punch.
entries.meaning_odia: କେହି ନଇଁ ପଡ଼ିଥିବା ବେଳକୁ ବିଧାଏ ମାରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏଠାରେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଅନ୍ୟର ଦୁର୍ବଳ ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ସୁଯୋଗ କରି ଆଉ ଆଘାତ ଦେବାକୁ ଏହା ବୁଝାଏ। ଏପରି ବ୍ୟବହାରକୁ ଚିହ୍ନାଇବା ପାଇଁ କଥାଟି ଉଦ୍ଧୃତ ହୋଇପାରେ; ଏହା ଆମ ପକ୍ଷରୁ ଆଘାତ ଦେବାର ପରାମର୍ଶ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The two halves make the timing exact: the blow lands when the other person is already bowed down. Our editorial reading concerns taking advantage of vulnerability to add another injury. The directive shape of the line can expose that conduct when quoted critically.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A person already struggling with a setback faces someone who deliberately chooses that moment to add pressure. An observer recalls the punch timed to a bowed posture.
entries.cultural_context: The repeated time phrases ଯେତିକି ବେଳେ and ସେତିକି ବେଳେ connect weakness and attack tightly. The physical image makes the chosen moment, rather than the size of the blow, central.

entries.title: Beautiful in one’s own eyes
entries.odia:
ନବ ଗୁଞ୍ଜର
ଆପଣା ମନକୁ ଆପେ ସୁନ୍ଦର।
entries.literal_meaning: Navagunjara—to one’s own mind, oneself is beautiful.
entries.meaning_odia: ନବ ଗୁଞ୍ଜର ନାମ ପରେ ନିଜ ମନକୁ ନିଜେ ସୁନ୍ଦର ଲାଗିବାର କଥା ଆସିଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ନିଜ ପ୍ରତି ଥିବା ଅନୁକୂଳ ବିଚାରକୁ ନେଇ ଏକ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ। ଏଥିରୁ ନବଗୁଞ୍ଜରଙ୍କୁ ଅସୁନ୍ଦର କୁହାଯାଇଛି ବୋଲି ଧରାଯାଇନାହିଁ; ମୂଳରେ ସେପରି ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା ନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The judgement of beauty is located inside the person doing the judging. Our editorial reading notices how readily self-regard supplies its own favourable verdict. The opening names Navagunjara, but the line gives no description that would justify declaring the figure ugly.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone admires their own appearance and assumes everyone must agree. A friend gently recalls the saying about being beautiful in one’s own eyes.
entries.cultural_context: The named figure in the short first line is followed by the rhyming ସୁନ୍ଦର. Repeated self-reference in ଆପଣା and ଆପେ makes the second line turn back on its own judge; no surrounding story is supplied.

entries.title: The bee’s unexpected choice
entries.odia:
ନ ରସି ଭ୍ରମର ରସିଲା
ଜାଈ ଯୁଈ ଫୁଲ ପାଣିକି ପକାଇ
ପୋକ ଶୁଙ୍ଗା ମୂଳେ ବସିଲା।
entries.literal_meaning: Not drawn [elsewhere], the bee took a fancy: throwing jai and jui flowers into the water, it settled at the base of pokasunga.
entries.meaning_odia: ଭ୍ରମର ଜାଈ ଯୁଈ ଫୁଲକୁ ପାଣିରେ ପକାଇ ପୋକଶୁଙ୍ଗା ମୂଳରେ ବସିଲା ବୋଲି ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର କହେ। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ତାହାର ପସନ୍ଦକୁ ଦେଖି କଥକଙ୍କ ବିସ୍ମୟ ବା ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ: ଯାହାକୁ କଥକ ଆଦର କରୁଛନ୍ତି, ଭ୍ରମର ତାହା ଛାଡ଼ି ଅନ୍ୟଠାରେ ରସୁଛି। ଏଥିରୁ କୌଣସି ଗଛର ନିକୃଷ୍ଟତା କିମ୍ବା ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ପ୍ରେମକାହାଣୀ ଧରାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The bee’s attraction is shown through a conspicuous rejection: the named flowers go into the water, and it settles at another plant. Our editorial reading hears surprise or mockery at a preference the speaker does not share. The verse leaves the human application open.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone rejects options a friend admires and enthusiastically chooses a different one. The friend recalls the bee’s unexpected preference, revealing their own judgement as well as the choice.
entries.cultural_context: The verse gives the bee deliberate human-like actions, throwing flowers away and choosing where to sit. Jai and jui name the rejected flowers; pokasunga names the chosen plant. The contrasting actions carry the image without requiring a botanical ranking.

witnesses.locator: Page26, final three-line item beginning ନ ରସି ଭ୍ରମର.
witnesses.note: Rendered page inspected17November2026; exact spelling and line layout retained. Elsewhere in brackets is contextual completion of opening negative participle. Plant names retained; no botanical ranking or specific human relationship inferred.

entries.title: Appeal calls for attention
entries.odia:
ନ ଲାଗିଲେ ସବୁବେଳେ
ଘର କି ଶୋଭେ
ନ ମାଠିଲେ ବୟସ ବେଳେ
ମନ କି ଲୋଭେ?
entries.literal_meaning: Without continual effort, does the house look pleasing? Without polishing in one’s prime, is the heart attracted?
entries.meaning_odia: ନିୟମିତ ଲାଗି ନରହିଲେ ଘର ଶୋଭା ପାଏ କି, ବୟସ ବେଳେ ମାଠିବା ନହେଲେ ମନ ଆକର୍ଷିତ ହୁଏ କି—ଦୁଇଟି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଏଠାରେ ଅଛି। ମାଠିବାକୁ ଘଷିମାଜି ପରିଷ୍କାର ବା ପରିମାର୍ଜିତ କରିବାର ବ୍ୟାପକ ଅର୍ଥରେ ରଖାଯାଇଛି; ଠିକ୍ କେଉଁ ଜିନିଷକୁ କିପରି ମାଠିବା କୁହାଯାଇଛି ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଆକର୍ଷଣ ସହ ଯତ୍ନ ଓ ପ୍ରୟାସର ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଏହା ଆଗକୁ ଆଣେ।
entries.explanation: Both questions place work before appeal: sustained attention for the house, polishing or refinement in one’s prime. Our editorial reading connects a pleasing result with effort rather than assuming it arrives by itself. The second question leaves the thing being polished unstated, so this edition keeps that action broad.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone expects a project to remain inviting without regular attention. A colleague recalls the paired questions about effort and appeal.
entries.cultural_context: The house gives the first question a concrete object. The second turns to attraction while leaving its object implicit. Repeating the negative condition and rhetorical question links the two without identifying a particular grooming or social practice.

witnesses.locator: Page27, first four-line item beginning ନ ଲାଗିଲେ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact wording retained. ମାଠିଲେ translated broadly as polishing/refinement with object unspecified; no gender, adornment custom or character-training practice inferred. The interpretation of the parallel is editorial.

entries.title: A healer in name, death in practice
entries.odia:
ନାଆଁକୁ ଧନ୍ୱନ୍ତରୀ
ଚିକିତ୍ସାରେ ଯମ।
entries.literal_meaning: Dhanvantari in name; Yama in treatment.
entries.meaning_odia: ନାଆଁରେ ଧନ୍ୱନ୍ତରୀଙ୍କ ପରି ବଡ଼ ବୈଦ୍ୟ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଚିକିତ୍ସାରେ ଯମଙ୍କ ପରି—ଏହି ବିପରୀତ ଚିତ୍ର କଥକଙ୍କ କଟାକ୍ଷ। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ସୁନାମ କିମ୍ବା ଉପାଧି ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ କାମରେ ଉପକାର ବଦଳରେ କ୍ଷତି କରିବାକୁ କହେ। ମୂଳର ଚିକିସ୍ରାରେ ଶବ୍ଦକୁ ଅର୍ଥ ଓ ବ୍ୟାକରଣ ଆଧାରରେ ଚିକିତ୍ସାରେ ବୋଲି ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ଅନୁମାନରେ ସୁଧାରାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The first name promises healing; the second turns that promise into its opposite. Our editorial reading hears a sharp criticism of someone whose impressive reputation conceals work that causes harm. The contrast is stronger than simple failure to live up to a title.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A celebrated repair expert makes a machine worse while claiming to restore it. A disappointed customer recalls the contrast between a healer’s name and harmful practice.
entries.cultural_context: Dhanvantari supplies the image of healing and Yama the image of death. Placing these names on either side of a single practitioner makes the satire immediate: the advertised role and the actual effect pull in opposite directions.

witnesses.locator: Page27, second item beginning ନାଆଁକୁ ଧନ୍ୱନ୍ତରୀ.

entries.title: One ornament, two turns
entries.odia:
ନାକ ଚଣା ବୋଲି ଖଣ୍ଡେ
ତାକୁ ବୋହୂ ନାଉଥାଏ ଦଣ୍ଡେ
ତାକୁ ଶାଶୁ ନାଉଥାଏ ଦଣ୍ଡେ।
entries.literal_meaning: Just one nose ornament: the daughter-in-law wears it for a while, and the mother-in-law wears it for a while.
entries.meaning_odia: ନାକଚଣା ଖଣ୍ଡିଏ ଅଛି; ତାକୁ ବୋହୂ କିଛି ସମୟ ପିନ୍ଧୁଛନ୍ତି, ପୁଣି ଶାଶୁ କିଛି ସମୟ ପିନ୍ଧୁଛନ୍ତି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ଅଳ୍ପ ସାମଗ୍ରୀକୁ ଏକାଧିକ ଲୋକ ପାଳି କରି ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର। ଦୁହିଁଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଝଗଡ଼ା କିମ୍ବା କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ପ୍ରଥା ଏଥିରେ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The repeated lines pass the same ornament from one wearer to the other. Our editorial reading focuses on limited means: two people’s wishes are accommodated through turns with a single object. The verse leaves their feelings about the arrangement unstated.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Two colleagues have only one piece of equipment between them and arrange alternating turns. Someone recalls the single ornament worn first by one household member and then by the other.
entries.cultural_context: The household relationship gives the repeated action two distinct participants, while ଖଣ୍ଡେ keeps the available ornament singular. Repeating ଦଣ୍ଡେ makes the alternation audible. The scene can be understood without treating it as a documented household practice.

entries.title: Applying a matter in the wrong place
entries.odia:
ନିରିମାଇଲ
କାହିଁ କଥା ନେଇ କାହିଁ ମାଇଲ?
entries.literal_meaning: Nirimaila! Taking a matter from where, where have you applied it?
entries.meaning_odia: କେଉଁଠାର କଥା ନେଇ କେଉଁଠି ଲଗାଇଲ ବୋଲି କଥକ ପଚାରୁଛନ୍ତି। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହି ଢଗଟି ମାରିବାର ପ୍ରୟୋଗ କରିବା ଅର୍ଥରେ ଦିଆଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ଗୋଟିଏ ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗର କଥାକୁ ଅନ୍ୟ ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗରେ ଅସଙ୍ଗତ ଭାବେ ଲଗାଇବା ଉପରେ ଆପତ୍ତି। ଆରମ୍ଭର ନିରିମାଇଲ ସମ୍ବୋଧନଟି ଅବିକଳ ରଖାଯାଇଛି; ତାହାର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ପରିଚୟ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The repeated where questions the leap from a matter’s original setting to its new use. The dictionary quotes the line under applying or using, so the final verb does not describe a blow. Our editorial reading hears a protest against making one context’s words serve an unrelated argument.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A comment about one project’s schedule is offered as evidence about another person’s honesty. Someone objects that the remark has been carried into a context it did not address.
entries.cultural_context: The rhyme between the opening address and the final verb gives the objection a compact, pointed sound. Nirimaila is retained as an unexplained address; the question itself carries the contrast between where a matter came from and where it is being used.

entries.title: The gourd that must be lifted
entries.odia:
ନିଲଜ ଲାଉ
ଟେକି ଟାକି ଦେଲେ ପିଢାକୁ ଯାଉ।
entries.literal_meaning: Shameless gourd! When lifted up, you go onto the pidha.
entries.meaning_odia: ଲାଉକୁ ନିଲଜ ବୋଲି ସମ୍ବୋଧନ କରି କଥକ କହୁଛନ୍ତି, ଟେକି ଦେଲେ ସେ ପିଢ଼ାକୁ ଯାଏ। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ଅନ୍ୟର ସାହାଯ୍ୟରେ ଉପରକୁ ଉଠିବା ଉପରେ ଏକ କଟାକ୍ଷ। ଏଠାରେ ପିଢ଼ାକୁ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଲାଉ ମାଡ଼ିବାର ଚାଳ ବା ଆଧାର ଭାବେ ବୁଝାଯାଇଛି; ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଗଠନ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନୁହେଁ। ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ଦରକାର ହେବାକୁ ନିଜେ ଲଜ୍ଜାର ବିଷୟ ବୋଲି ଧରାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The gourd is addressed like a person and mocked for reaching its support through someone else’s lifting. Our editorial reading focuses on dependence on that help. The force of the taunt belongs to the speaker; the image alone does not make assistance a moral failing.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A teammate waits for others to initiate every step before joining in. An impatient colleague recalls the gourd that moves upward when lifted, making their frustration audible.
entries.cultural_context: The verse turns an ordinary lifting action into an exchange with a gourd. Pidha is retained in translation and read here as a roof or growing support; its precise structure remains uncertain.

entries.title: One’s observance in another’s house
entries.odia: ପର ଘରେ ପଶି ମଙ୍ଗଳବାର ଓଷା।
entries.literal_meaning: Entering someone else’s house and observing the Tuesday fast.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟର ଘରେ ପଶି ମଙ୍ଗଳବାର ଓଷା କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହି କଥାରେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ନିଜର କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ବା ଆୟୋଜନକୁ ଅନ୍ୟର ଜାଗାରେ ନେଇ ବସାଇବା ଉପରେ ଏହା ଏକ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ। କାହାର ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ହେଲା, ଅନୁମତି ଥିଲା କି ନାହିଁ, କିମ୍ବା କେଉଁ ପୂଜାବିଧି ହେଲା—ମୂଳ କଥା ସେସବୁ କହୁନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The pointed detail is the location: the observance takes place after entering somebody else’s home. Our editorial reading applies that mismatch to carrying one’s own arrangements into another person’s space as though it were one’s own. The line leaves the practical circumstances unstated.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A guest begins reorganising the host’s room for a personal activity without first discussing it. The host recalls the saying about conducting one’s observance in another’s house.
entries.cultural_context: Tuesday names the occasion and osha names a religious observance involving a vow or fast. The proverb’s compact scene depends on the contrast between that personal activity and another person’s household, without detailing the ritual.

entries.title: The mouth’s taste and the belly
entries.odia:
ପାଟି ସୁଆଦ
ପେଟ କି ଜାଣଇ ତହିଁରେ ଭେଦ?
entries.literal_meaning: Taste is for the mouth; does the belly know the difference?
entries.meaning_odia: ସୁଆଦ ପାଟିର କଥା; ପେଟ ସେଥିରେ ଭେଦ ଜାଣେ କି ବୋଲି ଢଗଟି ପଚାରେ। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ସୁଆଦର ପସନ୍ଦ ଓ ଖାଇ ପେଟ ପୂରାଇବାର ଦରକାରକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଦେଖାଏ। ଏହା ଖାଦ୍ୟର ପୋଷକଗୁଣ ବା ଶରୀର ବିଷୟରେ ବୈଜ୍ଞାନିକ ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ। ମୂଳ ଲେଖାରେ ତହିଁରେ ଶବ୍ଦର ଅତିରିକ୍ତ ଇକାର ଚିହ୍ନଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ ଏଠାରେ ସଜାଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
entries.explanation: The mouth values flavour, while the question imagines the belly as unconcerned with that distinction. Our editorial reading separates the pleasure of a particular taste from the simpler need to be fed. It is a rhetorical contrast, not a claim that different foods have identical effects.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: During a journey, someone rejects an adequate simple meal because it is not their favourite flavour. A companion recalls the mouth-and-belly contrast to distinguish preference from the immediate need for food.
entries.cultural_context: Two parts of one body become different voices in the argument: the mouth stands for taste, and the belly for being fed. The short first line names the preference; the question then challenges how far that preference matters.

witnesses.locator: Page28, seventh item beginning ପାଟି ସୁଆଦ.

entries.title: Wrongful gain spent on atonement
entries.odia: ପାପ ଧନ ପ୍ରାୟଶ୍ଚିତ୍ତରେ ଯାଏ।
entries.literal_meaning: Wealth gained through wrongdoing goes on atonement.
entries.meaning_odia: ପାପ ଉପାୟରେ ଆସିଥିବା ଧନ ପ୍ରାୟଶ୍ଚିତ୍ତରେ ଚାଲିଯାଏ ବୋଲି କଥାଟି କହେ। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ଅନ୍ୟାୟ ଲାଭ ପଛରେ ଥିବା ପରିଣାମକୁ ମନେ ପକାଏ: ଯାହା ଅର୍ଜନ କରାଗଲା, ଭୁଲର ପ୍ରତିକାର କରୁ କରୁ ତାହା ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ହୋଇପାରେ। ଏହା ନୈତିକ ଚେତାବନୀ; ଧନ ଦେଲେ ଭୁଲ ମିଟିଯାଏ କିମ୍ବା ସବୁବେଳେ ଏକେ ପରିଣାମ ହୁଏ ବୋଲି ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The gain is answered by the cost of atoning for how it was obtained. Our editorial reading treats this as a warning that an apparent benefit can be consumed in addressing the wrong behind it. The proverb gives no procedure for atonement and does not make money a substitute for responsibility.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone considers an unfair shortcut for extra gain. A colleague invokes the saying to ask whether dealing with the consequences could consume what seemed to be a profit.
entries.cultural_context: The line pairs ପାପ, wrongdoing or sin, with ପ୍ରାୟଶ୍ଚିତ୍ତ, atonement. Wealth links the two: it is gained through the first and spent on the second. That compact moral accounting supplies the force of the warning.

entries.title: Bangles before the son arrives
entries.odia:
ପୁଅ ନାଇଁ, ପୁଅ ପେଟରେ
ପୁଅର ବାପ ଖଡୁ ଗଢଉଚି
ବନମାଳିପୁର ହାଟରେ।
entries.literal_meaning: The son is not here; the son is in the womb. His father is making bangles at Banamalipur market.
entries.meaning_odia: ପୁଅ ଏଯାଏଁ ଜନ୍ମ ହୋଇନାହିଁ, ପେଟରେ ଅଛି; ଅଥଚ ତାହାର ବାପ ବନମାଳିପୁର ହାଟରେ ଖଡ଼ୁ ଗଢ଼ୁଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଆସିବାକୁ ଥିବା ଫଳକୁ ଧରି ଆଗୁଆ ଆୟୋଜନ କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ଗର୍ଭସ୍ଥ ପୁଅ ଓ ହାଟରେ ଚାଲିଥିବା କାମକୁ ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖି କଥକ ସେହି ଆଗ୍ରହକୁ ଦେଖାଉଛନ୍ତି। ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ମାତ୍ରକୁ ଭୁଲ କିମ୍ବା କୌଣସି ପ୍ରଥାର ପ୍ରମାଣ ବୋଲି ଧରାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The son is still in the womb, while his father is already occupied with making bangles at the market. Our editorial reading hears a teasing contrast between an awaited arrival and preparations running ahead of it. The pregnancy is real within the imagined scene; the verse need not condemn every act of preparation before birth.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Before a proposed event is confirmed, an organiser enthusiastically commissions decorative details. A friend recalls the father making bangles while the son is still in the womb.
entries.cultural_context: Banamalipur market supplies a concrete location for the father’s activity, set against the son’s position in the womb. The source names bangles but does not identify their material, intended wearer or a customary occasion for presenting them.

witnesses.locator: Page28, tenth item beginning ପୁଅ ନାଇଁ.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact three-line wording retained without repair. ଖଡୁ translated bangles; making versus commissioning is unresolved. Anticipatory-planning interpretation is editorial; no jewellery custom inferred.

entries.title: The son at court, the father’s bowl
entries.odia:
ପୁଅ ବସିଚି କଚେରୀରେ
ବାପ ଖାଉଚି ପଥୁରିରେ।
entries.literal_meaning: The son is seated at court; the father eats from a stone bowl.
entries.meaning_odia: ପୁଅ କଚେରୀରେ ବସିଛି, ବାପ ପଥୁରି ବା ପଥରର ଛୋଟ ପାତ୍ରରେ ଖାଉଛି—ଏହି ଦୁଇ ଚିତ୍ର ପାଖାପାଖି ରହିଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ପୁଅର ବାହାର ଅବସ୍ଥାନ ଓ ବାପର ଘରୋଇ ଜୀବନ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଅମେଳର ଇଙ୍ଗିତ ଅଛି। ପୁଅ କେଉଁ ପଦରେ ଅଛି ତାହା କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ; ପଥୁରିରେ ଖାଇବା ମାତ୍ରକୁ ଅବହେଳା ବା ଦାରିଦ୍ର୍ୟର ପ୍ରମାଣ ଧରାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The couplet places a public setting beside an intimate household detail. Our editorial reading hears a contrast between the son’s apparent standing and the father’s modest circumstances. It can question whether outward advancement reaches those at home, while leaving the son’s role and the cause of the contrast unstated.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A discussion celebrates someone’s public success but overlooks how an elderly relative is living. Another participant recalls the son at court and the father’s bowl to bring the household circumstances into view.
entries.cultural_context: The rhyme joins କଚେରୀ, a court or administrative office, with ପଥୁରି, a small stone bowl. These concrete places and objects make the comparison; no particular occupation or household custom is needed to translate it.

entries.title: Why save, whichever son he becomes?
entries.odia:
ପୁଅ ଯଦି ଯୋଗ୍ୟ ହୁଏ
ଧନ କାହିଁ ପାଇଁ ସଞ୍ଚୁ।
ପୁଅ ଯଦି ଅଯୋଗ୍ୟ ହୁଏ
ଧନ କାହିଁ ପାଇଁ ସଞ୍ଚୁ?
entries.literal_meaning: If the son is capable, why do you accumulate wealth? If the son is incapable, why do you accumulate wealth?
entries.meaning_odia: ପୁଅ ଯୋଗ୍ୟ ହେଲେ ବି ଧନ କାହିଁକି ସଞ୍ଚୁଛ, ଅଯୋଗ୍ୟ ହେଲେ ବି କାହିଁକି ସଞ୍ଚୁଛ—ଦୁଇ ବିପରୀତ ଅବସ୍ଥାରେ ଏକା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠିଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଯୋଗ୍ୟ ପୁଅ ନିଜେ ଚଳିପାରେ, ଅଯୋଗ୍ୟ ପୁଅ ସଞ୍ଚିତ ଧନ ସମ୍ଭାଳି ନପାରେ—ଏହି ଯୁକ୍ତିରେ କେବଳ ପୁଅ ପାଇଁ ଧନ ଜମା କରିଚାଲିବାକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରାଯାଉଛି। ଏହି କାରଣ ଦୁଇଟି ମୂଳ ପଙ୍କ୍ତିରେ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The same question follows opposite conditions: a capable son and an incapable son. Our editorial reading supplies the implied challenge: one may be able to provide for himself, while the other may fail to preserve what is left to him. The verse thus questions making accumulation for a son an unquestioned purpose; its sharp paradox does not supply a practical rule about how much a family should save.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone says every decision must increase the wealth left to a son. A friend quotes the paired questions to open a conversation about helping him develop capability as well as leaving possessions.
entries.cultural_context: Repetition is the device: only ଯୋଗ୍ୟ changes to ଅଯୋଗ୍ୟ, while the question about wealth returns unchanged. The source names a son; no wider rule about children’s abilities is established by that wording.

witnesses.locator: Page29, first complete four-line item beginning ପୁଅ ଯଦି ଯୋଗ୍ୟ ହୁଏ.

entries.title: Two grandsons, two opposed images
entries.odia:
ପୁଅର ପୁଅ ନାତି
ମାରଇ ଝିଙ୍କର କାତି
ଝିଅର ପୁଅ ନାତି
ସରଗେ ଜାଳଇ ବତୀ।
entries.literal_meaning: The son’s son is a grandson: he strikes with the porcupine’s kati [contextually, a quill]. The daughter’s son is a grandson: he lights a lamp in heaven.
entries.meaning_odia: ପୁଅର ପୁଅ ଓ ଝିଅର ପୁଅ—ଦୁହେଁ ନାତି, ଅଥଚ ପଙ୍କ୍ତିର ବକ୍ତା ପ୍ରଥମକୁ ଝିଙ୍କର କାତି ମାରିବା ସହ, ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟକୁ ସରଗରେ ବତୀ ଜାଳିବା ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ିଛନ୍ତି। ଏଠାରେ କାତିକୁ ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗକ୍ରମେ ଝିଙ୍କକଣ୍ଟା ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି; ଏହି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଶବ୍ଦର ଅର୍ଥ ସ୍ୱତନ୍ତ୍ରଭାବେ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହୋଇନାହିଁ। ଆଘାତ ଓ ଆଲୋକର ଦୁଇ ଚିତ୍ରରେ ବକ୍ତାଙ୍କ ପକ୍ଷପାତ ଫୁଟିଛି; ନାତିମାନଙ୍କ ଗୁଣ ବିଷୟରେ ଏହାକୁ ସତ୍ୟ ନିୟମ ଧରାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: Both children have the same kinship name, yet the speaker gives them opposite images: a hurtful strike and a light in heaven. Read editorially, the verse favours the daughter’s son over the son’s son. That preference belongs to the speaker; the verse does not establish how either kind of grandson actually behaves.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: While discussing old family sayings, a reader quotes this verse to show how the same kinship label can carry sharply unequal expectations, then questions that preference.
entries.cultural_context: The repeated ନାତି makes the contrast especially pointed. The heavenly lamp supplies a favourable image, but the verse does not name a ceremony, recipient or religious obligation. In translation, kati is retained because its precise lexical sense remains uncertain; a porcupine quill is the contextual reading.

entries.title: Food for the belly, blows for the back
entries.odia:
ପେଟକୁ ଦେଇ
ପିଠିକି ମାଇଲେ ସୁହାଉ ଥାଇ।
entries.literal_meaning: Having given to the belly, if one strikes the back, it remains agreeable.
entries.meaning_odia: ପେଟକୁ ଖାଇବା ଦେଇ ପିଠିରେ ମାଡ଼ ମାରିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହା ସୁହାଏ ବୋଲି ପଙ୍କ୍ତିର ବକ୍ତା କହୁଛନ୍ତି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ବା ଜୀବିକା ପାଇଁ ନିର୍ଭରତା ଭିତରେ ଅପମାନ ଓ କଷ୍ଟ ସହିବାର ଇଙ୍ଗିତ ଅଛି। ଖାଇବା ଦେବା ଦ୍ୱାରା କାହାକୁ ମାଡ଼ ମାରିବାର ଅଧିକାର ମିଳେ—ଏପରି ମତକୁ ଏହି ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ସମର୍ଥନ କରୁନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The saying places nourishment and a blow in the same exchange. Its speaker claims that feeding makes even the blow acceptable. Read critically, the image can expose how dependence for sustenance makes harsh treatment something a person endures. That is an editorial interpretation of the contrast, not a justification for the treatment.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: In a discussion of dependence, someone quotes the belly-and-back saying. Another participant points out that providing food cannot excuse humiliating or hurting the person who needs it.
entries.cultural_context: Belly and back give the exchange two bodily locations: the belly receives sustenance, the back receives the blow. The source leaves both people unnamed, allowing the contrast to be discussed without assigning it to a particular household or occupation.

witnesses.locator: Page29, fourth complete item beginning ପେଟକୁ ଦେଇ.
witnesses.note: Rendered wording inspected17November2026; source spelling ସୁହାଉ ଥାଇ retained without repair. Feeding is the contextual sense of giving to the belly. Expanded dependence interpretation editorial; source statement about acceptability attributed to its speaker.

entries.title: Hunger within, shame on the face
entries.odia: ପେଟରେ ଭୋକ, ମୁହଁରେ ଲାଜ।
entries.literal_meaning: Hunger in the belly, shame on the face.
entries.meaning_odia: ପେଟ ଭୋକିଲା, ଅଥଚ ମୁହଁରେ ଲାଜ। ଦରକାର ଥିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହା କହିବାକୁ ବା ମାଗିବାକୁ ସଙ୍କୋଚ ଲାଗିବା—ଏହା ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠ। ଲାଜ କାହିଁକି ଲାଗୁଛି ବା କାହା ପାଖରେ ଲାଗୁଛି, ପଙ୍କ୍ତିରେ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: A bodily need is set beside an emotion that can keep it unspoken. Our editorial reading is of someone who is hungry but too embarrassed to ask. More broadly, the compact contrast can describe a genuine need concealed by shyness, without saying why the person feels that way.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A guest has not eaten but keeps quiet when food is offered. A friend gently recalls the line about hunger in the belly and shame on the face, making room for an honest answer.
entries.cultural_context: The line needs only two locations: the belly holds the need, while the face displays embarrassment. This economy gives the saying its force without naming a household rule or particular occasion.

entries.title: Coarse rice, hand on the moustache
entries.odia:
ବଗଡା ଭାତ
ନିଶରେ ହାତ।
entries.literal_meaning: Coarse cooked rice; a hand on the moustache.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏପଟେ ବଗଡ଼ା ବା ମୋଟା ଚାଉଳର ଭାତ, ସେପଟେ ନିଶରେ ହାତ—ଦୁଇଟି ସଂକ୍ଷିପ୍ତ ଚିତ୍ର ପାଖାପାଖି ରହିଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ସାଧାରଣ ଭୋଜନ ସହ ଗର୍ବିତ ଭଙ୍ଗୀର ମିଳନ ଦେଖାଯାଏ। କହିବାର ସ୍ୱର ଅନୁସାରେ ଏହା ବଡ଼େଇକୁ ଥଟ୍ଟା କରିପାରେ ବା ସାଧାରଣ ଅବସ୍ଥାରେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଆତ୍ମସମ୍ମାନ ରଖିବାକୁ ବୁଝାଇପାରେ; ମୂଳ ପଙ୍କ୍ତି ସେହି ସ୍ୱର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ କରୁନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The two fragments put a plain meal beside a hand resting on a moustache. We read the gesture contextually as a proud pose. The juxtaposition can sound mocking when directed at swagger, or approving when it suggests dignity despite modest circumstances; the bare wording leaves that tone open.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Discussing a character who eats simply but carries himself proudly, readers quote the rice-and-moustache line and debate whether its tone is affectionate or teasing.
entries.cultural_context: The rhyme joins ଭାତ and ହାତ, food and gesture. It does not describe the rice being eaten or the moustache being twirled, so the translation leaves those actions unstated.

entries.title: Your face and mine look beautiful
entries.odia:
ବଗ ମୁହଁ ଚାହିଁ ବଗୁଲୀ ବସେ
ତୋ ମୁହଁ ମୋ ମୁହଁ ସୁନ୍ଦର ଦିଶେ।
entries.literal_meaning: The female egret sits looking at the egret’s face; your face and my face look beautiful.
entries.meaning_odia: ବଗର ମୁହଁକୁ ଚାହିଁ ବଗୁଲୀ ବସିଛି; ପର ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ତୋ ମୁହଁ ଓ ମୋ ମୁହଁ ଦୁହେଁ ସୁନ୍ଦର ଦିଶୁଥିବା କଥା ଅଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ପରସ୍ପର ପ୍ରଶଂସା ସହ ନିଜକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ସେହି ପ୍ରଶଂସାରେ ସାମିଲ କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର। କହିବାର ସ୍ୱର ଅନୁସାରେ ସ୍ନେହ ବା ଥଟ୍ଟା ଥାଇପାରେ; କାହାକୁ ଅସୁନ୍ଦର ବା କପଟୀ ବୋଲି ପଙ୍କ୍ତିଟି କହୁନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The gaze at another face leads to a favourable judgement that includes both “you” and “me.” Our editorial reading is of mutual admiration that also makes room for self-admiration. The scene can be affectionate or teasing; the wording alone does not turn it into an accusation of dishonest praise.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Two friends each admire the other’s portrait and then praise their own. Someone fondly quotes the egret pair and its verdict on “your face and mine.”
entries.cultural_context: The bird pair gives the judgement a small scene rather than an abstract lesson. Repeating ମୁହଁ and moving from ବଗ to ତୋ and ମୋ lets the image pass from birds to a speaking pair without specifying a human relationship.

entries.odia:
ବଡ଼ ବଡ଼ ଗଲେ ଫସର ଫାଟି
ସାନ ବାହାରିଲେ ବେସର ବାଟି।
entries.literal_meaning: The great ones came to nothing; the small ones set out, having ground mustard paste.
entries.meaning_odia: ବଡ଼ ବଡ଼ମାନେ ବିଫଳ ହୋଇଗଲେ, ଅଥଚ ସାନମାନେ ବେସର ବାଟି ବାହାରିଲେ—ଏହି ବିପରୀତ ଚିତ୍ର ପଙ୍କ୍ତିରେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଆଗରୁ ଅଧିକ ସମର୍ଥ ବୋଲି ଧରାଯାଉଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ବିଫଳତା ଦେଖାଇ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ଚେଷ୍ଟାକୁ ସନ୍ଦେହ କରାଯାଉଛି। ବେସର କାହିଁକି ବଟା ହୋଇଛି ତାହା କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ; ସାନ ବୋଲି କେହି ନିଶ୍ଚୟ ବିଫଳ ହେବେ ବୋଲି ମଧ୍ୟ ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The first line announces failure; the second shows others already equipped with a preparation of their own. Our editorial reading hears a sceptical challenge to their confidence: if the supposedly greater people failed, what makes these smaller ones so ready? The question can discourage ambition, but the verse supplies no outcome for the later attempt.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After experienced teams abandon a difficult task, newcomers announce that they are ready. Someone quotes the mustard-paste line sceptically; the newcomers still have to show what their different approach can achieve.
entries.cultural_context: Grinding mustard paste gives readiness a tangible action. The saying leaves its intended use unexplained, so the translation preserves the preparation without supplying a dish, a catch or a missing story.

entries.title: A friend gives strength, a river footing
entries.odia:
ବନ୍ଧୁ ବଳ ଦିଏ
ନଈ ଥଳ ଦିଏ।
entries.literal_meaning: A friend gives strength; a river gives footing.
entries.meaning_odia: ବନ୍ଧୁ ବଳ ଦିଅନ୍ତି, ନଈ ଠିଆ ହେବାକୁ ଥଳ ଦିଏ—ଦୁଇ ପ୍ରକାର ଭରସାକୁ ପଙ୍କ୍ତିଟି ଏକାଠି ରଖିଛି। ପାଣିରେ ପାଦ ରଖିବାର ସ୍ଥାନ ପରି ବନ୍ଧୁଙ୍କ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ମଣିଷକୁ ସ୍ଥିରତା ଓ ସାହସ ଦିଏ ବୋଲି ଆମ ପାଠ। ଏଠାରେ ଥଳର ଅର୍ଥ ପାଣି ଭିତରେ ଠିଆ ହେବାର ସ୍ଥାନ।
entries.explanation: The rhyme brings two kinds of support together. Footing in water gives the body somewhere to stand; a friend’s support gives a person strength. Our editorial reading emphasises the steadiness that help can offer, without specifying whether that help is practical, emotional or material.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A difficult task feels manageable after a friend offers to help. The person receiving that support recalls the friend who gives strength and the river that gives footing.
entries.cultural_context: ବଳ and ଥଳ rhyme, while the repeated ଦିଏ balances the two gifts. The water image makes support tangible: something beneath the feet rather than an abstract assurance.

entries.title: Meeting the smith, remembering the iron
entries.odia:
ବାଟରେ ଦେଖିଲି କମାର
ଲୁହା ପଜାଇଦେ ଆମର।
entries.literal_meaning: I saw a blacksmith on the road: sharpen our iron [implement].
entries.meaning_odia: ବାଟରେ କମାରଙ୍କୁ ଦେଖିବାମାତ୍ରେ ଆମ ଲୁହା ପଜାଇଦିଅ ବୋଲି ଅନୁରୋଧ ଆସୁଛି। ପଜାଇବା ମାନେ ଧାର କରିବା; କେଉଁ ଲୁହା ଉପକରଣ ତାହା କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଅଚାନକ ମିଳିଥିବା ସୁଯୋଗକୁ ନିଜ କାମ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। କାମଟି ହେଲା କି ନାହିଁ, ପଙ୍କ୍ତି ସେ କଥା କହୁନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: An encounter immediately becomes a request for useful work. Our editorial reading notices the quick move from recognising someone’s skill to asking for one’s own task to be done. Depending on the setting, it can sound resourceful or opportunistic; the verse does not say whether the smith accepts.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone meets a friend who repairs bicycles and immediately remembers a wheel needing attention. Another person teases them with the blacksmith-on-the-road saying.
entries.cultural_context: The rhyme links କମାର and ଆମର, the worker encountered and the speaker’s own possession. The change from “I saw” to a direct request compresses the whole encounter into two lines.

entries.title: A father’s backing and a son’s intelligence
entries.odia:
ବାପ ଥିଲା ପୁଅ ସଭାରେ ଜିଣେ
ବୁଦ୍ଧିଥିଲା ପୁଅ ପୋଷଇ ପଣେ।
entries.literal_meaning: A son who has a father prevails in the assembly; a son who has intelligence supports eighty.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାପ ଥିବା ପୁଅ ସଭାରେ ଜିଣେ, ବୁଦ୍ଧି ଥିବା ପୁଅ ପଣେ ବା ଅଶୀ ଜଣଙ୍କୁ ପୋଷେ—ପଙ୍କ୍ତିଟି ଦୁଇ ପ୍ରକାର ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟକୁ ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖିଛି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ପ୍ରଥମଟି ବାପଙ୍କ ଭରସା ବା ସହାୟତା, ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟଟି ନିଜ ବୁଦ୍ଧିରେ ଅନ୍ୟଙ୍କୁ ଚଳାଇବାର କ୍ଷମତା। ବାପ ନଥିଲେ କେହି ସଫଳ ହୋଇପାରିବେ ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ପଙ୍କ୍ତି କହୁନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The parallel puts support received beside support provided. Our editorial reading hears the father’s presence as backing in public affairs, while the son’s own intelligence enables him to sustain many others. The large number gives the second claim emphasis; neither line is a guarantee of success or a rule about who can succeed.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A discussion distinguishes the help someone receives from family from the ability they develop to help others. A participant recalls the assembly and the eighty people supported in this couplet.
entries.cultural_context: The repeated ଥିଲା ପୁଅ balances having a father with having intelligence. ପଣେ preserves an old counting expression for eighty, giving provision for others a deliberately large scale.

witnesses.locator: Page30, final item beginning ବାପ ଥିଲା ପୁଅ.
witnesses.note: Rendered page inspected17November2026; exact wording including joined ବୁଦ୍ଧିଥିଲା retained. ପଣେ rendered eighty. Father’s backing and received/provided support comparison editorial.

entries.title: The nest sways in the wind
entries.odia:
ବାୟାର କି ଯାଏ,
ବାଆ କଲେ ବସା ଦୋହଲୁଥାଏ।
entries.literal_meaning: What does it matter to the baya bird? When the wind blows, its nest keeps swaying.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାଆ କଲେ ବସା ଦୋହଲୁଛି, ତଥାପି ବାୟାର କି ଯାଏ—ପଙ୍କ୍ତିର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଏକ ନିଶ୍ଚିନ୍ତ ଭାବ ଆଣୁଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ, ଚାରିପାଖର ହଲଚଲକୁ ବଡ଼ କ୍ଷତି ବୋଲି ନଧରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ଅନୁସାରେ ଏହା ଆଶ୍ୱାସନ ବା କାହାର ନିର୍ବିକାର ଭାବ ପ୍ରତି ଥଟ୍ଟା ହୋଇପାରେ।
entries.explanation: The nest moves, but the opening question asks what difference that makes to its occupant. Read editorially, the couplet treats surrounding disturbance with unconcern. It may reassure someone or tease a person who remains untroubled; the wording alone does not settle that tone.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Amid a bustle of complaints, one person remains relaxed. A friend recalls the baya bird whose nest sways in the wind, leaving it open whether the remark admires or teases that calm.
entries.cultural_context: The repeated ବ sounds connect bird, wind and nest. The movement belongs to the nest; the question places the bird at a distance from the surrounding fuss. This is a rhetorical image, not a guarantee that nests withstand every wind.

witnesses.locator: Page31, fourth item beginning ବାୟାର କି ଯାଏ.

entries.title: Sinking down and down
entries.odia: ବୁଡିଗଲା ଗୋଡ ତଳକୁ ତଳକୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: The sunken foot goes down and down.
entries.meaning_odia: ବୁଡ଼ିଯାଇଥିବା ଗୋଡ଼ ଆହୁରି ତଳକୁ ଯାଉଛି—ଏହା ପଙ୍କ୍ତିର ଚିତ୍ର। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ, ଅବସ୍ଥା ଖରାପ ହେବା ପରେ ଆହୁରି ଖରାପ ହୋଇଚାଲିବାକୁ ଏହା ବୁଝାଇପାରେ। କାହିଁକି ଏପରି ହେଉଛି ବା ଏଥିରୁ ଉଠିବା ଅସମ୍ଭବ କି ନୁହେଁ, ପଙ୍କ୍ତି କହୁନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: Repeating the downward direction makes the sinking feel unfinished. Read editorially, the line describes a situation that keeps deteriorating after it has already gone wrong. It names the movement, without assigning blame or declaring that recovery is impossible.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A neglected project develops one difficulty after another. Someone describes its worsening condition with the image of a foot sinking down and down.
entries.cultural_context: ତଳକୁ ତଳକୁ carries the whole motion of the short line. The foot supplies a bodily image for a decline that has begun and continues; the source supplies no particular water, mud or other setting.

entries.title: A straw for someone drowning
entries.odia: ବୁଡିଗଲା ଲୋକର କୁଟାଖିଅକୁ ଆଶ୍ରା।
entries.literal_meaning: A drowning person relies on a strand of straw.
entries.meaning_odia: ବୁଡ଼ିଯାଉଥିବା ଲୋକ କୁଟାଖିଅକୁ ବି ଆଶ୍ରା କରୁଛି—ଏହା ପଙ୍କ୍ତିର ଚିତ୍ର। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ, ଘୋର ବିପଦରେ ମଣିଷ ସାମାନ୍ୟ ସାହାଯ୍ୟର ସମ୍ଭାବନାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଭରସା କରିବାର କଥା ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି। କୁଟା ତାକୁ ନିଶ୍ଚୟ ଉଦ୍ଧାର କରିବ ବୋଲି ପଙ୍କ୍ତି କହୁନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: The danger is immense and the thing relied on is tiny. Read editorially, the contrast shows how desperation can make even a slight possibility of help feel worth holding onto. The line describes reliance without promising that the support will be enough.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After several attempts to solve an urgent problem fail, someone puts their remaining hope in a small lead. A friend recalls the drowning person’s reliance on a straw.
entries.cultural_context: ଆଶ୍ରା names support or reliance. The smallness of କୁଟାଖିଅ intensifies the person’s need; the image concerns a hoped-for way through danger rather than something already recovered afterward.

entries.title: A greeting for the wife’s sake
entries.odia: ଭାରିଜା ଲାଗି ସାନ ଶଳାକୁ ନମସ୍କାର।
entries.literal_meaning: For the wife’s sake, a respectful salutation to the younger brother-in-law.
entries.meaning_odia: ଭାରିଜାଙ୍କ ଲାଗି ତାଙ୍କ ସାନ ଭାଇକୁ ନମସ୍କାର କରାଯାଉଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ, ଜଣଙ୍କ ସହ ସମ୍ପର୍କ ରଖିବାକୁ ତାଙ୍କ ନିକଟଜନଙ୍କ ପ୍ରତି ମଧ୍ୟ ଆଦର ଦେଖାଇବାର କଥା ଏଥିରେ ଆସେ। ଏହା ଥଟ୍ଟାର ସ୍ୱରରେ କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ, କିନ୍ତୁ ସାନ ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ସମ୍ମାନ ଦେବା ଅନୁଚିତ ବୋଲି ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The wife is the reason named for the salutation, while her younger brother receives it. Our editorial reading notices how regard for one person can extend to someone connected with them. The line can tease that indirect motive without establishing fear, compulsion or an improper act.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone makes a special effort to greet a partner’s relative warmly. A friend recalls this line with a teasing smile about courtesy extended through another relationship.
entries.cultural_context: The saying separates the person for whose sake respect is shown from the person who receives it. ସାନ gives the recipient a younger or junior position, but the line supplies no detailed greeting ritual or rule about who may deserve respect.

witnesses.locator: Page31, final item beginning ଭାରିଜା ଲାଗି.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact ଭାରିଜା and ଶଳା preserved. Brother-in-law means wife’s brother here. Interpretation of courtesy through a relationship editorial; no specific gesture or mandatory custom inferred.

entries.title: Garb brings alms
entries.odia: ଭେକ ଥିଲେ ଭିକ ମିଳେ।
entries.literal_meaning: With the garb, one receives alms.
entries.meaning_odia: ଭେକ ବା ବେଶ ଥିଲେ ଭିକ ମିଳେ ବୋଲି ପଙ୍କ୍ତି କହୁଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ, ବାହ୍ୟ ପରିଚ୍ଛଦ ଦେଖି ଲୋକେ ଜଣଙ୍କ ଭୂମିକା ଚିହ୍ନନ୍ତି ଓ ସେହି ଅନୁସାରେ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ବା ସମ୍ମାନ ଦେଇପାରନ୍ତି। ସେହି ବେଶ ମିଛ ବା ଭିକ ମାଗୁଥିବା ଲୋକ ଠକ ବୋଲି ପଙ୍କ୍ତିରୁ ଧରାଯାଉନାହିଁ।
entries.explanation: A visible sign of a role is linked to the response it brings. Read editorially, the rhyme notices how appearance can influence recognition and material help. It leaves open whether the garb is sincere or assumed, and does not make alms a guaranteed reward for dressing a certain way.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A group notices that people respond more readily when a visitor’s role is clear from their dress. Someone recalls this saying about garb and alms.
entries.cultural_context: ଭେକ and ଭିକ differ by a vowel, turning dress and alms into a compact pair. The saying focuses on what presentation elicits from others, rather than describing a particular garment or proving the wearer’s character.

witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact wording retained. ଭେକ rendered garb, without assuming disguise or deception. Wider recognition/response reading editorial.

entries.title: A sour mango tastes good to hunger
entries.odia: ଭୋକିଲା ପାଟିକି ଆମ୍ବିଳା ଆମ୍ବ ସୁଆଦ।
entries.literal_meaning: To a hungry mouth, a sour mango is tasty.
entries.meaning_odia: ଭୋକିଲା ପାଟିକୁ ଆମ୍ବିଳା ଆମ୍ବ ବି ସୁଆଦ ଲାଗେ—ପଙ୍କ୍ତି ଭୋକ ଓ ଖାଦ୍ୟର ରୁଚିକୁ ଯୋଡ଼ିଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ, ଦରକାର ତୀବ୍ର ହେଲେ ସାଧାରଣତଃ କମ୍ ପସନ୍ଦ ହୋଇପାରୁଥିବା ଜିନିଷ ମଧ୍ୟ ଆଦର ପାଇପାରେ। ଏଠାରେ ଆମ୍ବିଳାର ଅର୍ଥ ପଚା ନୁହେଁ, ସୁଆଦର ଅର୍ଥ ମିଠା ହୋଇଯିବା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.explanation: The mango remains sour, but the hungry mouth finds it pleasant. Read editorially, the saying shows how need can change appreciation. It describes a shift in the eater’s response, rather than a change in the fruit itself.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After a long morning without a meal, someone enjoys a simple snack they would usually pass over. A companion recalls the sour mango that tastes good to a hungry mouth.
entries.cultural_context: The contrast is between ଆମ୍ବିଳା, sour, and ସୁଆଦ, pleasing to taste. They need not be opposites: the hungry mouth connects them. The wording gives no recipe, ripeness test or claim about food safety.

witnesses.locator: Page32, fifth and final item beginning ଭୋକିଲା ପାଟିକି.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact wording retained. ଆମ୍ବିଳା rendered sour and ସୁଆଦ tasty, not rotten or sweet. Wider need/appreciation reading editorial.

entries.title: I will not stay and endure it
entries.odia:
କହିବେ ନାଇଁ
କହିଲେ ଏ ଘରେ ରହିବି ନାଇଁ
ତାଟି କିଳା ମାଡ଼ ସହିବି ନାଇଁ
ଖଣ୍ଡିଆ ପଥୁରି ଧୋଇବି ନାଇଁ।
entries.literal_meaning: Do not say [it]. If [it is] said, I will not stay in this house. I will not endure blows with the door fastened. I will not wash a chipped stone bowl.
entries.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଥମ ପଙ୍କ୍ତିର କହିବେ ନାଇଁକୁ ଏଠାରେ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କୁ କହିବାକୁ ମନା କରିବା ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି; କହିବି କରି ବଦଳାଯାଇନାହିଁ। କହିଲେ କିଏ କହିବେ, ତାହା ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ନୁହେଁ। ପରେ ଘରେ ନରହିବା, ତାଟି କିଳା ଅବସ୍ଥାରେ ମାଡ଼ ନସହିବା ଓ ଖଣ୍ଡିଆ ପଥୁରି ବା ପଥରର ଛୋଟ ପାତ୍ର ନଧୋଇବାର ମନା ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ନିଜେ କଣ ସହିବେ ବା କରିବେ ନାହିଁ, ତାହା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କରୁଥିବା ଏକ ସ୍ୱର; ବକ୍ତାଙ୍କ ଘରୋଇ ପରିଚୟ ଅଜଣା।
entries.explanation: The repeated refusal moves from speech and staying in the house to enduring blows and washing a damaged bowl. Our editorial reading hears a voice setting limits on what it will accept or do. The changes in person are preserved: the first line is read as an address, while who speaks in the following condition remains unspecified. The source gives no household role or reason for the conflict.
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: In discussing a passage about a difficult household, a reader notices how each repeated refusal adds another limit, rather than assuming the speaker must be a particular family member.
entries.cultural_context: The repeated ନାଇଁ holds the four lines together. Door fastening, blows and a chipped stone bowl are concrete details, but they do not identify a wife, servant, employer or abuser. The bowl’s newly verified meaning makes the last refusal translatable without constructing such a story.

witnesses.locator: Page9, third item beginning କହିବେ ନାଇଁ, all four lines.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload re-inspected17November2026; original କହିବେ retained. Opening translated as respectful prohibition; conditional subject unspecified. ତାଟି କିଳା ମାଡ଼ contextually rendered blows with door fastened; ପଥୁରି small stone bowl. These readings do not assign household identities. Public shorter first-person version is not substituted.
